edge-22.title: Edge 22
edge-22.prompt: Edge 22” is a fast, strategic card game inspired by Blackjack but built with completely new rules, special cards, and a fresh scoring system. The goal is to reach as close to 22 as possible without going over. Players compete against an AI dealer, so the game is always playable even when no other players are online. The deck includes traditional cards plus a few unique cards like Boost, Swap, Reverse, and Shield, which create exciting strategy moments and give players more control than classic Blackjack. The dealer follows fixed logic while the player can choose to Hit, Stand, or use special cards, making every round fun, quick, and skill-based. “Edge 22” is designed for casual gamers who enjoy card games but want something new, simple, and highly replayable.

fouter.title: Fouter
fouter.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page. Interface should be dark mode.

pong.title: Pong
pong.prompt:
APP NAME: PONG

DESCRIPTION: Classic Ping Pong game. 

GAME LAYOUT

Create a single-screen game.

Game board: square shaped.

Background color:  green.

Ball: small white square.

Player paddle: color dark purple, big wide rectangle on the left side of game board.

Computer paddle: color dark purple, big wide rectangle on the right side of game board. 

Everything sized proportionally so it fits on screen.

Start Screen: Centered yellow rectangle button labeled “Start Game”.

Only show this button before play begins.

PLAYER PADDLE CONTROLS:

Place these below the game board.

One Up Arrow button.

One Down Arrow button.

Button are rectangle shaped.
When pressed, they should immediately move the player paddle  up or down very extremely fast.

Computer paddle behavior:
Paddle movement extremely fast.
Always have the computer paddle return ball back to player.

BALL PHYSICS

Ball rules:

Starts centered

Moves diagonally

On paddle collision return ball horizontally and diagonally to the other direction.

Ball Speed:  extremely slow
Keep the movement smooth. 

Do NOT end game on paddle collision. 
Game ends only when:
The ball goes fully past a paddle.

When this happens:

Stop the ball movement.

Show a “Try Again” button below the board.

Score = number of paddle hits during the round.

After game ends, display score.

RESET BEHAVIOR.

When Try Again is pressed:

Reset ball to center.

Reset score to 0.

Show “Start Game” button again

Hide “Try Again” button

stonks.title: Mini App Factory App
stonks.prompt:
Role: Act as a Senior Web3 Full-Stack Engineer specializing in Farcaster Mini Apps (Frames v2), Solidity, and Next.js.

Objective: Code a functional Farcaster Mini App that mimics the functionality of the PancakeSwap Lottery. The app consists of a Solidity Smart Contract (deployed on Base) and a Next.js frontend that runs inside the Farcaster client.

Tech Stack:

Smart Contract: Solidity ^0.8.20 (Hardhat environment).

Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), Tailwind CSS, Lucide React.

Web3 Integration: Wagmi v2, Viem, and Tanstack Query.

Farcaster: @farcaster/frame-sdk for identity and context.

Project Requirements:

Part 1: The Smart Contract (Lottery.sol) Create a contract optimized for the Base L2 network.

Variables: ticketPrice (set to 0.001 ETH), lotteryId, players array, history mapping.

Functions:

buyTicket(): Accepts ETH. Rejects if value is incorrect. Adds sender to array.

drawWinner(): (For this MVP, use block.prevrandao or a simplified pseudo-random generator to avoid complex Chainlink setup). Selects a random index from players, transfers 90% of balance to winner, keeps 10% in contract as fee/rollover. Resets the array.

getPotBalance(): Returns current contract balance.

getPlayers(): Returns list of current participants.

Part 2: The Mini App Frontend Create a mobile-first, responsive UI that looks similar to PancakeSwap (playful, rounded, colorful).

File Structure: Please provide the code for:

app/page.tsx (Main UI).

app/providers.tsx (Wagmi + Query Client setup).

app/layout.tsx (Including the Farcaster SDK script).

public/.well-known/farcaster.json (The manifest file).

Key Features:

SDK Initialization: Use sdk.actions.ready() on load.

UI State: Show the current "Pot Size" (read from contract).

Action: A large "Buy Ticket" button.

Feedback: Show a loading spinner during transaction and a "Success" confetti animation when the ticket is bought.

Wallet: Assume the user is using the Farcaster-injected wallet or a standard connector via Wagmi.

Output Instructions:

Provide the full Solidity code for the contract.

Provide the Install Command (npm install ...) for all necessary frontend dependencies.

Provide the Full Code for the Next.js files listed above.

Ensure the code handles the window.ethereum injection correctly for Farcaster mobile users.

wednesday-addams-quiz.prompt:
ROLE & GOAL
You are an expert web app and quiz creator. Build a fast, mobile-friendly personality quiz mini app themed around Wednesday (Netflix) and its upcoming/ongoing Season 2. The quiz should help fans discover:

“Which Wednesday Season 2 character are you?”

The app must be fun, replayable, and easy to share.

CORE CONCEPT

Quiz title: “Which Wednesday Season 2 Character Are You?”

Tone: Spooky, witty, and deadpan with a touch of dark humor, in the spirit of Wednesday Addams.

Characters to sort into (you choose 4–6 core options, for example):

Wednesday

Enid

Xavier

Bianca

Ajax

A “mystery wildcard” result (e.g., “You’re the shadow no one saw coming.”)

IMPORTANT:

Do not reveal or invent major plot spoilers.

Keep references high-level (personality traits, vibes, archetypes), not detailed episode summaries.

QUIZ STRUCTURE

7–10 multiple-choice questions.

2048-app.title: 2048 App
2048-app.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

fx1-digital-hubs.title: Fx1 Digital Hubs
fx1-digital-hubs.prompt:
FX1 Digital Hubs is an onchain creative ecosystem built on the Base blockchain, designed to empower creators, collectors, and digital entrepreneurs through a unified hub of tools: NFT fashion art, smart-contract powered creator assets, onchain identity, and gamified digital experiences.

At its core, FX1 Digital Hubs solves one major problem in Web3:
Most creators don’t have a simple, accessible, and engaging way to build, showcase, monetize, and expand their onchain presence — all from one place.

FX1 Digital Hubs brings everything together in one ecosystem:
	•	Onchain Fashion Art Hub: Create, collect, and showcase NFT fashion pieces and surreal digital wearables on Base.
	•	Smart Contract Hub: Deploy custom creator contracts, dynamic NFTs, and utility-based assets easily.
	•	Digital Wardrobe Mini-App: A gamified experience where users build an onchain identity through fashion, collectibles, and achievements.
	•	Creator Passport: A Zora-powered onchain passport that unlocks access to future quests, drops, and community experiences.
	•	$FDH Ecosystem: A micro-token economy that rewards engagement, creativity, and participation.
	•	Community Space: A home for Web3 creators, designers, writers, and digital builders to collaborate and grow.

Who is it for?
• Web3 creators
• NFT artists
• Digital fashion designers
• Collectors
• Onchain entrepreneurs
• Anyone exploring digital identity onchain

Problems FX1 Digital Hubs Solves:
	•	Fragmented creative tools scattered across multiple platforms
	•	Lack of simple onboarding into NFT creation and digital fashion
	•	No unified space for onchain identity, creator economy, and interactive experiences
	•	Limited visibility for small Web3 builders
	•	No accessible gateway to bring more African creatives onchain

FX1 Digital Hubs is built for the future of digital culture — where art, fashion, identity, and smart contracts connect to create new economic opportunities.

I am actively building this as a one-man founder and young dad, fully committed to Base for almost two years. Right now, I’m seeking an angel investor, partner, or collaborator who sees the vision and wants to help take this project to the moon.

FX1 Digital Hubs is early, raw, and powerful — and with the right backing, it can become the leading onchain creative hub on Base.

x-score.prompt:
Title: Tweet Engagement Analyzer — Minimal

Icon: /mnt/data/a77cf7de-8fea-4d98-91b4-ca28d168bf36.png

Goal:
Simple tool — accept a Twitter/X profile (URL or handle) and show average likes and views per tweet for 7, 30, 90 day windows. Minimal controls, fast feedback, compact results.

Page structure (minimal)

Header (small)

Left: app icon + title Tweet Engagement Analyzer

Right: small text Minimal

Hero / Input (single row)

Text input placeholder: @elonmusk or https://x.com/elonmusk

Primary button: Analyze

Below input (tiny text): Defaults: exclude replies, exclude retweets, max 200 tweets

Loading state

Inline spinner and text Analyzing… replace the button while fetching.

Results (single compact row)

Three small cards side-by-side (responsive stack on mobile):

Card A: 7d — tweets: X • avg likes: Y • avg views: Z / “unavailable”

Card B: 30d — same fields

Card C: 90d — same fields

Each card is one line of text, small font, subtle border. No charts.

Raw data (collapsible)

Hidden by default. Small link: Show tweets used (N) toggles a simple table:

Columns: Date | Likes | Views | Tweet ID

Table is plain and horizontally scrollable.

Errors & edge copy

Invalid handle → inline red text: Please enter a valid Twitter/X profile.

Protected account → Profile is private — cannot analyze.

No tweets in window → show Not enough data inside the relevant card.

Data & API binding (exact)

When user clicks Analyze, the front-end should POST JSON to /api/analyze:

Request body:

{
  "handle": "elonmusk",          // string (backend should accept handle or full URL)
  "includeReplies": false,
  "includeRetweets": false,
  "maxTweets": 200
}


Expect response JSON exactly like:

{
  "profile": { "username":"elonmusk", "profile_url":"https://x.com/elonmusk" },
  "timeframes": {
    "7":  { "tweet_count": 5, "avg_likes": 120, "avg_views": 4000, "engagement_rate": 0.03 },
    "30": { "tweet_count": 20, "avg_likes": 90,  "avg_views": null,   "engagement_rate": null },
    "90": { "tweet_count": 50, "avg_likes": 75,  "avg_views": 1500,  "engagement_rate": 0.05 }
  },
  "raw_sample": [ {"tweet_id":"1","created_at":"2025-11-22T12:00:00Z","likes":10,"views":200} ]
}


Note: If avg_views is null, show unavailable on the card.

Behaviour details (one-line rules)

Parse handle from input stripping https:// and @ automatically on submit.

Disable Analyze while request in-flight.

Show inline error messages (no modal).

Cache last successful result in UI until a new search.

Collapsible raw table must show tweet count N in toggle label.

Styling guidance (minimal)

Neutral background, white cards, small rounded corners.

Compact typography (small labels, medium numbers).

Keep vertical spacing tight — single-column hero + results row.

No charts, no animations (keep it fast and minimal).

In the swirling ether of blockchain stars, the Crypto Alchemy & Chaos App manifests wealth and risk as living entities. Users summon coins, whisper to wallets, and navigate the cryptic tides of market chaos. Profit, loss, and paranoia dance together in a mystical symphony.

Purpose: Transform mundane portfolio management into an arcane ritual of numbers, charts, and random chaos.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Summoning the Coins

Add coins via ritualistic gestures (manual entry) or invoke through exchange API keys (Binance, Kraken, Coinbase).

Track quantity, mystical purchase price, astral date.

Observe invisible threads of correlation linking your coins to market destinies.

2.2 Chaos & Risk Oracles

Portfolio volatility shown as fluctuating flame graphs.

Sharpe ratio appears as an aura; max drawdown as storm clouds.

Simulate apocalyptic scenarios: sudden 50% dips, meteoric rises.

Alerts whisper warnings when overexposed to a single currency’s dark magic.

2.3 Automated Rituals (Trading Bots)

Bot familiars obey commands: Buy, Sell, or Hover in shadow.

Strategies: “Moonlight Entry”, “Shadow Exit”, “The Panic Dance”.

Test in phantom realm (paper trading) before risking corporeal coins.

2.4 Portals & Visualization

Dashboard portal: shows portfolio essence, bot familiars, risk aura.

Candlestick crystals with mystical overlays (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands).

Pie charts of allocation appear as spinning talismans.

Push notifications as whispers of fate: “BTC trembles!”, “ETH ascends!”

Vibrations mimic heartbeat of crypto cosmos.

API keys and wallet secrets sealed in encryption runes.

Multi-factor authentication: finger, face, or secret chant.

Optional “Cold Vault” integration for items too precious for mortal eyes.

AI Oracle predicts market prophecies.

Social Coven: share spells (strategies) with other summoners.

DeFi portals and staking circles.

NFT familiars appearing in your portfolio aura.

2048.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

2d-to-3d-printer.title: 2D To 3D Printer
2d-to-3d-printer.prompt:
App Prompt
App Name:
2D to 3D PRINTER
Tagline:
Transform 2D pictures into 3D printer-ready files.
App Description
Create a beautiful, AI-powered mobile application that converts 2D images into realistic, high-fidelity 3D models. The app should combine cutting-edge AI technology with a vibrant, modern, and intuitive user experience.
Use AI-based depth estimation and photogrammetry to reconstruct real-world depth, lighting, and texture — delivering models that look lifelike, not artificial or blocky. Users can upload photos, capture them directly via their camera, or optionally use LiDAR-enabled devices for enhanced depth accuracy. Needs to be Android and ISO compatible.
Core Features
1. Image Preparation & Smart Cropping
• Once a picture is uploaded or captured, allow users to optionally draw around the desired object or subject in the photo.
• Use AI-powered auto-cropping to intelligently detect and isolate the selected area.
• The crop should be adjustable, allowing users to fine-tune the selection before proceeding.
• This ensures that only the intended image portion is used in the 2D-to-3D conversion process, improving accuracy and reducing noise. 
2. The 2D-to-3D Conversion
• Implement AI vision models (MiDaS, DPT, or Gaussian Splatting) to estimate depth and surface geometry.
• Generate true-to-life 3D models with accurate lighting, proportion, and material reflection.
• Ensure smooth rendering transitions during model creation (animated “depth reveal” effect).
• Optional LiDAR Support: Users with LiDAR-enabled devices can capture point cloud data to improve depth precision and generate highly accurate 3D models. LiDAR can be combined with 2D images to enhance surface detail, scaling, and real-world accuracy.
3. Scaling & Measurement Tools
• Allow users to scale models using metric units (mm, cm, m).
• Provide an interactive 3D viewport with smooth pinch-to-zoom, rotate, and pan gestures.
• Include gridlines or AR-guided scale overlays for precision. Allow users to edit and adjust the model if needed.
4. File Export Options
• Export in multiple 3D printing-ready formats (.STL, .OBJ, .3MF, .G-CODE, .AMF).
• Allow compression or high-detail export modes.
• Preview export size and complexity before downloading.
5. Performance & AI Processing
• Support on-device AI for fast local tasks and cloud rendering for advanced models.
• Display an elegant progress bar with a glowing or wave animation during processing.
• Combine LiDAR point clouds with AI depth estimation for devices with LiDAR, producing the most precise 3D reconstructions.
User Interface (UI/UX Design)
Design a colorful yet minimal interface with vibrant gradients, futuristic neon look, and smooth animations. The look should feel professional, futuristic, and intuitive — similar to Apple’s Vision Pro or Adobe Firefly aesthetic.
Visual Style & Feel:
• Color Palette: Deep purples, electric blues, and subtle neon accents.
• Typography: Clean sans-serif (e.g., Inter, Poppins, or SF Pro).
• Icons: Rounded, glowing icons for key actions (e.g., “Upload Photo,” “Generate 3D Model”).
• Motion Design: Use micro-interactions (hover glow, tap ripple, animated transitions between 2D → 3D).
UI Layout:
• Futuristic neon UI for the 2D-to-3D app, glowing gradients in deep purple and electric blue, luminous rounded icons, smooth animated transitions, holographic depth indicators, reflective surfaces, subtle neon accents, intuitive and minimal layout, cyberpunk sci-fi aesthetic with cinematic lighting and immersive glow.
• Home Screen: Two large buttons — “Take Photo” and “Upload Photo.”
• After Upload: Launch the smart cropping interface with draw-to-select and AI auto-crop adjustment.
• Bottom Navigation Bar: Home, My Projects, Generate, Settings.
• 3D Preview Screen: Gradient background, easy gesture control, fullscreen toggle.
Allow users to edit and make adjustments to model if needed before and after 2D to 3D conversion.
Storage & Sharing
• Allow users to save projects locally or sync with cloud storage.
• Enable direct sharing via email, AirDrop, or QR link.
• Include project gallery thumbnails with a 3D hover effect.
Technical Requirements
• Platform: Mobile (Android & iOS)
• Frontend: Flutter or React Native
• Backend: Python (FastAPI) or Node.js (Express)
• AI Models: MiDaS / DPT / Gaussian Splatting for depth + texture estimation
• Libraries: Three.js / MeshLab for 3D rendering and exporting
Optional Add-ons
• Compare Mode: Toggle between 2D and 3D versions.
• Basic Editor: Tools for texture smoothing, brightness, and color tuning.
• Cloud Credit System: For complex rendering workloads.
• AR Preview Mode: View generated 3D models in real-world space.
• LiDAR-Enhanced Capture: Optional mode for LiDAR-enabled devices to scan scenes and improve 3D model accuracy and scale precision.
Overall Experience
The app should feel dynamic, colorful, and immersive, yet remain simple enough for beginners. Every screen transition should feel fluid — giving users the sense that they’re stepping from photography into another dimension. LiDAR data should integrate seamlessly when available, enhancing realism without altering the core 2D-to-3D experience.

The interface should feel dynamic and cheerful, with smooth animations, uplifting visuals, and easy sharing options so users can save or send their motivational messages. Optional features include voice narration of the AI-generated speech, themed visual overlays like sparkles or glowing effects, daily inspiration notifications, and the ability to track favorite messages. The unique appeal of the app is transforming ordinary objects and moments into sources of creativity, positivity, and personal encouragement through AI-powered storytelling.

abeddehmet.title: Abeddehmet
abeddehmet.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

agro-ins.prompt:
**Technical Specification (TS)

Construction Assistant Application “BuildPro”**

1. Project Overview

BuildPro is a mobile and desktop application designed for construction workers, site managers, and independent contractors.
The app helps users calculate materials, manage tasks, track project progress, and generate reports for construction jobs.

2. Objectives

Simplify daily work for builders and foremen.

Provide reliable tools for material calculation and cost estimation.

Improve communication between team members.

Reduce paperwork by digitizing checklists, measurements, and reports.

Increase project efficiency through planning and monitoring features.

3. Core Features
3.1 Material Calculator

Concrete volume calculator (slabs, columns, beams).

Brick and block calculator (walls, openings, mortar).

Rebar calculator (length, weight, layout).

Wood and insulation calculator.

Roofing material calculator.

Automatic unit conversion (metric/imperial).

3.2 Cost Estimation Module

Price database (editable by user).

Automatic calculation of project cost:

Materials

Labor

Machinery

Transport

Export to PDF/Excel.

3.3 Project Management

Task planning (daily / weekly / monthly).

Gantt chart for timelines.

Assign tasks to workers.

Progress tracking with photos and notes.

Notifications and reminders.

3.4 Measurement Tools

Augmented Reality (AR) measurement for distance, height, area.

Digital ruler and level tool.

Laser meter integration (Bluetooth).

3.5 Documentation & Reporting

Daily construction log.

Safety checklist.

Defect reporting (with image attachments).

Automatic report generation (PDF).

Cloud storage for documents.

3.6 Team Communication

Group chats for each project.

File and drawing sharing (DWG, PDF, JPG).

Voice messages.

Push notifications for updates.

3.7 Blueprint Viewer

Support for PDF, DWG, PNG.

Layer toggling for DWG.

Annotation tools: draw, comment, highlight.

3.8 AI Assistant (optional)

Generate material lists from a room/wall photo.

Detect measurement from image.

Suggest optimal materials based on project type.

Auto-fill daily reports.

4. Platform Requirements
4.1 Supported Platforms

Android 9+

iOS 13+

Web version (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

4.2 Recommended Tech Stack

Frontend: Flutter (mobile) + React (web)

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL

Cloud Storage: AWS S3 / Google Cloud

AI Models: Cloud-based API

5. UI/UX Requirements

Simple, durable design suitable for outdoor use.

Large buttons for use with gloves.

Offline mode for remote construction sites.

Dark and high-contrast modes.

Dashboard with quick access to:

Calculator

Projects

Reports

Measurements

6. Performance Requirements

App startup time ≤ 3 seconds.

Material calculation ≤ 200 ms.

Messaging latency < 500 ms.

Offline data sync within 10 seconds after network restoration.

7. Security Requirements

User authentication (email, phone, or company account).

Role-based access control (worker, foreman, manager).

Encrypted data storage and communication (HTTPS, AES-256).

Daily automatic cloud backup.

8. Monetization Model

Free version with basic calculators.

Pro version (subscription):

AI tools

Unlimited reports

Team management

AR measurement

Cloud storage

9. Key Performance Indicators

Monthly active users (MAU).

Calculation tool usage frequency.

Time saved on reporting.

Team collaboration events.

Subscription conversion rate.
+

✅ архітектуру бази даних
✅ user stories для розробників
✅ логіку калькуляторів

ai-powered-habit-tracker.title: Ai Powered Habit Tracker
ai-powered-habit-tracker.prompt:
The AI-Powered Habit Tracker is a smart, personalized self-improvement app designed to help users build consistency, stay motivated, and achieve long-term goals. The app uses artificial intelligence to analyze behavior patterns, recommend improvements, predict habit success, and provide tailored motivation to keep users on track.

This app combines simplicity, gamification, and intelligent insights to create an engaging daily habit-building experience.

🔑 Core Features
1. Habit Creation & Scheduling

Users can:

Add new habits (e.g., “Read 20 mins,” “Drink water,” “Work out”)

Choose frequency (daily, weekly, custom days)

Set reminders at specific times

Attach goals, notes, or motivational quotes

The interface should be clean, intuitive, and allow quick creation of habits.

2. Streak Tracking & Progress Visualization

The app displays:

Daily streaks

Total completions

Progress bars

Monthly habit calendar highlights

Weekly & monthly progress summaries

This helps users stay motivated by visually tracking consistency.

3. AI-Driven Insights

AI analyzes user behavior and provides:

Predictions on whether a habit might be missed soon

Suggested optimal reminder times based on past completion patterns

In-depth habit statistics

Productivity score per habit

Personalized motivation messages when streaks drop or improve

Example insight:

“You usually complete your reading habit in the evening. Want me to adjust reminders to 7 PM?”

4. Personalized Motivation System

AI sends smart motivational notifications:

“You're 2 days away from beating your longest streak!”

“Missed yesterday? No worries, today is a fresh start.”

“You’re most productive on Mondays. Let’s make this week great!”

Motivation adapts to user mood, consistency, and behavior patterns.

5. Daily Check-In & Dashboard

A clean dashboard shows:

Today’s habits

Pending tasks

Streaks and rewards

A quick “Mark as Done” button for each habit

AI suggestions for improving daily routine

6. Gamified Rewards System

The app includes:

XP points for completing habits

Achievements (7-day streak, 30-day streak, etc.)

Level progression

Unlockable badges

Streak protector options

This boosts user engagement and habit adherence.

7. Smart Reminders

AI automatically adjusts reminder frequency and time, based on:

When the user completes habits

Which reminders are ignored

Time of day the user is most active

Example:

“You often finish hydration early in the morning — should I shift reminders earlier?”

8. Habit Categories & Templates

Easy-to-use templates:

Health

Fitness

Productivity

Learning

Finance

Mindfulness

Each template includes AI-suggested frequencies and goals.

9. Optional Social/Community Features

(If your app builder allows it)

Share progress with friends

Compare streaks

Join challenges

Rank on leaderboards

This increases competition and accountability.

10. Cloud Sync & Multi-Device Support

Sync habits and progress securely across devices

Backup automatically

🎨 Design & UI Suggestions

Minimal, modern design

Calm color palette (whitespace, soft gradients)

Circular progress rings

Smooth animations

Easy swipe-to-check habit actions

💡 AI Behavior Summary

AI should:

Analyze daily progress

Detect habit patterns

Predict drop-off points

Adjust reminders

Recommend new habits based on user behavior

Generate motivational text

Provide periodic behavioral reports

ai-story-generator.title: Ai Story Generator
ai-story-generator.prompt:
App Overview

The AI Story Generator is a creative writing companion that allows users to instantly generate stories, plot ideas, character profiles, and full-length narratives using AI. Designed for writers, students, roleplayers, and creative enthusiasts, this app provides endless inspiration and tools to craft unique stories across any genre.

The app focuses on simplicity, creativity, and customization, giving users full control over story elements while using intelligent AI models to create rich, immersive content.

🔑 Core Features
1. AI Story Generator

Users can instantly generate:

Short stories

Full novels

Fairy tales

Horror stories

Romance plots

Sci-fi adventures

Mystery/thriller narratives

Educational stories for kids

Users simply enter:

Genre

Themes

Characters

Writing style

Story length

The AI then produces a complete, coherent story in seconds.

2. Character Builder

A full character creation system:

Name, age, traits

Backstory generator

Personality analysis

AI suggestions for flaws, strengths, and arcs

Portrait generator (if supported by your tool)

AI can generate full character sheets to use across multiple stories.

3. Plot & World Generator

AI creates:

Plot outlines

Chapter-by-chapter plans

Worldbuilding details

Magic systems

Sci-fi technology

Nations, maps, cultures, languages (text-based)

This is perfect for deep storytelling and creative writing.

4. Story Editor & Rewrite Modes

Users can:

Rewrite entire chapters

Expand scenes

Simplify language

Change tone (dark, funny, poetic, etc.)

Fix pacing issues

Continue the story from any paragraph

AI acts as a writing coach and co-author.

5. Creative Modes

Provide different writing modes like:

Story Starter Mode – AI writes opening hooks

Kids Mode – simple, safe, fun stories

Poetry Mode – rhyme-based or free-verse

Fanfiction Mode – user inputs fandom, characters, themes

Roleplay Mode – AI responds in character

These modes help users explore different writing styles.

6. Save, Export & Share

Users can:

Save stories to in-app library

Export as PDF, DOCX, TXT

Share directly via social media

Sync story progress across devices

7. AI Voice Narration (Optional)

If your builder supports audio:

Convert stories to audio

Choose narrator voice styles

Adjust speed & tone

8. Genre Templates

To speed up creation, the app includes templates for:

Fantasy adventure

Sci-fi dystopia

Slice-of-life

Romance drama

Comedy

Horror/thriller

Mythology

Detective/mystery

Children’s bedtime stories

These templates pre-fill story settings and structures.

9. Daily Writing Prompts

AI generates a new prompt every day

Streak system for writing consistency

Option to turn prompts into full stories

10. Smart Suggestions While Writing

AI offers:

Plot twist suggestions

Character dialogue improvements

Scene expansion ideas

Setting enhancements

Tone adjustment tips

Perfect for overcoming writer’s block.

🎨 Design & UI Suggestions

Elegant minimalistic design

Book/library aesthetic

Floating text editor with distraction-free mode

Dark & light mode

Smooth animations for story generation

💡 AI Behavior Summary

AI should:

Understand genres and writing styles

Maintain consistent story tone

Track story continuity (characters, world rules, timelines)

Offer creative ideas without breaking user intent

Provide coherent long-form content

alertwhale.title: Alertwhale
alertwhale.prompt:
Idea: An alert service for large trades (“whale” orders) and abnormal volume.
User goal: Catch moments when big players enter the market.
Core features (MVP):

* Real-time volume monitoring for several pairs.
* Alert rules:

Candle volume > X times the average.
Single order > N $.


* Notification delivery: Telegram bot or email.
* History of recent “whale” events.

Development plan:

1. Connect to the exchange WebSocket API for streaming tickers/candles/trades.
2. Implement a backend service that:

aggregates volumes;
compares them with a moving average;
triggers events.


3. Create a Telegram bot to deliver alerts.
4. Build a minimal web interface for:

setting thresholds,
entering Telegram ID / email.


5. Log events for history and simple charts.

alias.title: Alias
alias.prompt: Create a mobile game inspired by the classic Alias game, but using images instead of words. Players see a random picture and must explain or describe it to their teammates without using certain “forbidden” keywords, while the teammates try to guess the concept as quickly as possible. The app can include multiple categories, difficulty levels, timers, and point systems for correct guesses. Users can upload their own images, share creative or funny interpretations, and unlock achievements for clever explanations. AI can suggest hints, generate bonus challenges, or create themed image packs. The interface should be playful, colorful, and easy to navigate, with smooth animations and sound effects to enhance excitement. The game can be played in real-time multiplayer mode, in teams, or solo with AI teammates. The unique appeal of the app is turning ordinary or quirky images into a fun, fast-paced, and social guessing game that challenges creativity and communication.

api04.title: Api04
api04.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

aplee.title: Aplee
aplee.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Emotional & Psychological State Tracker App
1. Project Overview

The Emotional & Psychological State Tracker app is designed to help users monitor, record, and analyze their emotional and psychological well-being. The app allows users to log moods, track patterns over time, receive insights, and optionally set reminders for self-care or mental health activities.
The goal is to increase self-awareness, identify triggers, and support personal mental health management.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Mood Logging

Users can log their current emotional state multiple times per day.

Each entry may include:

Mood (select from predefined options, e.g., Happy, Sad, Anxious, Calm)

Intensity (e.g., 1–10 scale)

Notes or journal text

Tags (e.g., Work, Family, Exercise, Sleep)

Optional: location or activity context

2.2 Psychological Metrics

Track additional psychological factors:

Stress level

Energy level

Sleep quality

Anxiety or depressive symptoms (self-assessment scales)

Optionally include short questionnaires (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7).

2.3 Visualization & Analytics

Daily, weekly, and monthly summaries of emotional patterns.

Graphs and charts showing mood trends, intensity, and triggers.

Correlations between mood and activities, sleep, or other factors.

Highlight unusual or extreme patterns for self-awareness.

2.4 Reminders & Notifications

Optional notifications to prompt mood logging.

Reminders for mindfulness exercises, meditation, or journaling.

Configurable frequency and time of reminders.

2.5 Journaling & Notes

Users can write daily notes or journal entries.

Optionally link notes to mood entries.

Searchable text for reflection over time.

2.6 Search & Filtering

Search past entries by date, mood, tags, or keywords.

Filter entries by mood category, intensity, or activity context.

2.7 Privacy & Security

Local storage of all entries by default.

Optional cloud sync with encryption (end-to-end) for multi-device access.

Optional passcode, fingerprint, or face authentication for privacy.

2.8 User Interface

Intuitive mood logging screen with simple emoji or slider selection.

Dashboard for quick overview of mood trends.

Calendar view showing entries over time.

Graphical display for trends (line chart, bar chart, pie chart).

Light/Dark mode and customizable themes.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile app (iOS & Android recommended)

Optional web version

3.2 Performance

Logging a mood entry must take <1 second.

Dashboard and charts must load instantly (<0.5 seconds for 1000+ entries).

3.3 Reliability

Local data must persist reliably even if app is closed.

Cloud sync must handle offline entries and conflicts gracefully.

3.4 Usability

Easy-to-use interface suitable for daily interaction.

Minimal taps to log mood (<3 taps).

Accessible design (readable fonts, colorblind-friendly palettes).

4. Technical Stack
Mobile

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local database: SQLite, Realm, or Hive

Notifications: native push / local notifications

Web (Optional)

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

Optional PWA support for offline use

Optional Analytics/AI

Machine learning for mood pattern prediction or trend alerts.

Suggest personalized interventions based on mood patterns.

5. Future Enhancements

Mood sharing with therapist or support group (optional).

Integration with wearable devices (heart rate, sleep tracking).

Guided meditation or mindfulness exercises.

Gamification: streaks for regular logging.

Export mood data for research or personal records (CSV, PDF).

appmame.title: Appmame
appmame.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Crypto Portfolio & Risk Analyzer App
1. Project Overview

The Crypto Portfolio & Risk Analyzer App helps users track their cryptocurrency investments, analyze portfolio performance, assess risks, and make informed decisions. The app provides real-time price tracking, alerts, analytics, and advanced risk metrics.

Goal: Allow users to manage crypto assets effectively, understand risk exposure, and optimize portfolio allocation.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Portfolio Management

Users can add multiple wallets and exchanges.

Add cryptocurrencies with:

Name / Symbol

Quantity

Purchase price / date

Notes (optional)

Manual entry or API integration with major exchanges (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, etc.).

2.2 Real-Time Price Tracking

Track prices of cryptocurrencies in real-time.

Display portfolio value in multiple fiat currencies.

Graphs showing price trends over different timeframes (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 1y).

2.3 Risk Analysis

Calculate portfolio risk metrics:

Volatility

Sharpe ratio

Maximum drawdown

Correlation between assets

Simulate potential losses/gains based on market scenarios.

Highlight overexposure to single assets or high-risk coins.

2.4 Alerts & Notifications

Price alerts for specific coins (threshold up/down).

Portfolio value alerts (daily/weekly).

Risk exposure warnings when thresholds are exceeded.

2.5 Analytics & Reporting

Dashboard showing portfolio allocation, top gainers/losers, and risk metrics.

Pie charts, bar charts, and line graphs for visualization.

Historical performance charts.

Export portfolio report to PDF or CSV.

2.6 Security & Authentication

Optional two-factor authentication (2FA).

Encrypted local storage for sensitive data.

API keys for exchange integration stored securely.

Optional biometric login (fingerprint/face).

2.7 User Interface

Dashboard with portfolio summary, value, and risk score.

Detailed coin page with performance metrics and historical charts.

Portfolio analytics page showing risk and allocation.

Light/Dark mode and customizable themes.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile: iOS & Android

Optional Web Dashboard

3.2 Performance

Real-time price updates (<2 seconds delay).

Smooth navigation between portfolio, analytics, and alerts.

Load portfolio of 100+ assets quickly (<1 second).

3.3 Data Storage

Local database (SQLite, Realm, Hive) for offline data.

Cloud sync optional for multi-device access with encryption.

3.4 Security

End-to-end encryption for API keys and sensitive data.

Optional multi-factor authentication.

3.5 Usability

Intuitive UI for both beginner and advanced crypto users.

Easy portfolio addition/editing and alert setup.

Responsive design for mobile and web.

4. Technical Stack
Mobile

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local DB: SQLite, Realm, or Hive

APIs: CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap, or exchange-specific APIs

Notifications: native push/local

Web (Optional)

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

5. Future Enhancements

AI-powered portfolio optimization (rebalancing suggestions).

Predictive analytics for potential price movements.

Integration with DeFi protocols and staking dashboards.

Social trading features: see top portfolios or strategies (optional).

Advanced charting with interactive indicators (MACD, RSI, Bollinger Bands).

april-time.title: April Time
april-time.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

apsaa.title: Apsaa
apsaa.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Recipe & Meal Planner App
1. Project Overview

The Recipe & Meal Planner app is a tool designed to help users store recipes, plan weekly meals, automatically generate shopping lists, and search for recipes by ingredients or categories.
The application aims to simplify meal planning, reduce food waste, and make grocery shopping more efficient.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Recipe Management

Users can add, edit, and delete recipes.

Each recipe contains:

Title

Ingredients (with quantity and unit)

Steps / Instructions

Preparation and cooking time

Category (e.g., Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Dessert)

Optional image of the dish

Tags (e.g., Vegetarian, Gluten-Free, Quick)

Users can mark recipes as favorites for easy access.

2.2 Weekly Meal Planner

Users can plan meals for each day of the week.

Each meal slot can be assigned a recipe.

Users can copy a week’s plan to another week.

Ability to view planned meals in calendar view or list view.

Notifications/reminders for planned meals (optional).

2.3 Automatic Shopping List

Generate a shopping list based on planned recipes.

Merge duplicate ingredients (e.g., 2x “tomatoes” → 4 tomatoes).

Allow users to:

Check/uncheck items while shopping

Manually add items not in recipes

Export list to text, CSV, or PDF

Optional: categorize shopping list by sections (e.g., Vegetables, Dairy, Meat).

2.4 Recipe Search & Filtering

Search recipes by:

Name or keyword

Ingredient(s)

Category

Tags (e.g., Vegan, Quick)

Search results display recipe title, category, and preparation time.

Filter recipes based on dietary preferences or available ingredients.

2.5 User Interface Requirements

Clean, intuitive UI for easy navigation.

Recipe creation/editing form.

Weekly planner calendar view.

Shopping list view with checkboxes and grouped categories.

Search bar with filters.

Optional: Light/Dark mode, adjustable font size.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile app (iOS & Android recommended)

Optionally web-based version.

3.2 Performance

Loading recipe list and weekly plan must be <0.5s.

Searching recipes should be instantaneous (<1s for 1,000+ recipes).

3.3 Data Storage

Local storage (SQLite / Realm / IndexedDB for web) for offline access.

Optional cloud sync for multi-device use.

3.4 Security

User data stored securely.

Cloud sync (if implemented) should use encryption in transit and at rest.

3.5 Usability

Easy-to-use interface with minimal clicks for adding recipes or planning meals.

Drag-and-drop for arranging meals in the planner (optional).

Undo/redo support for edits.

4. Recommended Technical Stack
Option A – Mobile App

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local database: SQLite or Realm

Notifications: native push/local notifications

Option B – Web App

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

Optional: PWA for offline access

5. Optional Future Enhancements

User accounts & cloud sync across devices

Recipe rating system

AI-powered recipe suggestions based on past meals

Nutritional information calculation

Barcode scanner for ingredients

Export meal plan & shopping list to calendar apps

aptos.title: Aptos
aptos.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

base-snake.title: Base Snake
base-snake.prompt:
Create a mini app called “Base Snake”. It is a fun and modern version of the classic Snake game, themed around the Base network. The player controls a small blue snake that moves around the screen to eat Base logos or blue dots. Each item collected makes the snake longer and increases the score by 1 point. Every 10 points, the snake becomes slightly faster and the player advances to the next level, up to level 10. As the levels increase, the speed rises and small obstacles start to appear on the map, such as blue blocks or walls that the snake must avoid.
Add simple sound effects: a short sound when collecting a dot, and a different sound when the game ends. The snake’s color changes dynamically as the player progresses, starting from light blue and becoming brighter and more electric at higher levels.
Show the current level and score during the game, and display the highest local score on the device so the user can try to beat their own record. Include a global leaderboard where users can submit their nickname and view the top scores from other players. When the game ends, show a short animation or fade-out effect before offering buttons to “Restart” or “Play Again”.
The interface should be minimal, fast, and mobile-friendly, using Base colors (blue and white) with smooth motion. The goal is to make a fun, nostalgic arcade-style game that becomes more challenging and rewarding as the levels increase, while allowing players to compete through a shared leaderboard.

base-survival.title: Base Survival
base-survival.prompt:
You are the OpenxAI Mini App Factory builder.

I want you to build a very simple, self-contained onchain mini-game on Base, that an AI can implement reliably from this prompt in one shot.

0. Game identity

Game name: Lucky Blocks – Guess & Score
Tagline: “Guess the right block, climb the score, store your best on Base.”

This should be:

A tiny, casual game.

Easy to understand in 5 seconds.

With one simple smart contract on Base to store best scores.

AI is used only for text (intro + recap), not for game logic.

1. Core game rules (keep them exactly like this)

Each run (game session) works like this:

A run has exactly 5 rounds.

At the start of a run:

currentRound = 1

score = 0

For each round (1 to 5):

The game picks a hidden random integer secret between 1 and 5 (inclusive).

This randomness can be done off-chain (e.g. Math.random() on the frontend).
It does NOT need to be verified onchain. This is just a fun casual game.

The UI shows the player 5 buttons:

1, 2, 3, 4, 5

The player chooses a number guess between 1 and 5.

The game compares:

If guess == secret: add 10 points to score.

Else: add 0.

Then currentRound += 1.

After round 5, the run ends. The final score is simply the score accumulated:

Min score = 0

Max score = 50

There are no extra mechanics:
no HP, no Risk, no lives, no combo, no multipliers.

Just 5 guesses, +10 points per correct guess.

2. Onchain logic on Base (one simple contract)

Create one smart contract on Base called LuckyBlocksScoreboard.

It must do ONLY this:

Store each player’s best score:

Mapping: mapping(address => uint256) public bestScore;

Function submitScore(uint256 score):

msg.sender is the player.

If score is greater than the current bestScore[msg.sender], update it.

Otherwise, do nothing.

Emit an event, e.g.:

event ScoreSubmitted(address indexed player, uint256 score);

View functions:

function getBestScore(address player) external view returns (uint256);

(This can simply return bestScore[player].)

Optional (only if easy to implement):

Keep an array of the top scores to display a simple leaderboard.

But if this is complex, it is OK to skip a global leaderboard and only show the best score per player.

No other onchain complexity is required.
No tokens, no NFTs, no admin functions are strictly necessary (owner can just be the deployer).

3. AI usage (text only, no logic)

Use the AI only for narrative text and flavor, not for calculating scores or randomness.

Implement 3 AI interactions:

Intro text when a run starts

After the player clicks “Start Game”, ask AI to generate a short intro (1–2 sentences), e.g.:

Example style:
“Welcome to Lucky Blocks on Base. You have 5 guesses to test your luck. Pick the right block, stack points, and lock in your best score onchain.”

Optional short line after each round

After the player guesses, the game already knows if it was correct or not (from local logic).

Ask AI for a very short reaction (one sentence max), e.g.:

If correct: “Nice hit! You guessed the hidden block.”

If wrong: “Unlucky this time, the hidden block slipped away.”

End-of-run recap

When the run ends (after 5 rounds), provide AI with:

total score

number of correct guesses

Ask AI to generate:

A short run title (max 40 characters).

A short recap paragraph (max 200 characters).

Example style:

Title: “Sharpshooter of Base”
Recap: “You nailed 4 out of 5 guesses – serious intuition. Your luck and timing make you a top contender in Lucky Blocks.”

The AI must:

Avoid NSFW or offensive content.

Avoid financial advice or claims.

Use a light, playful, arcade-style tone.

All numeric logic (rounds, score, correctness) must be done in code, not by AI.

4. Frontend / UX (very simple)

Build a single-page UI with 3 main states:

Home / Lobby

Show:

Game name: “Lucky Blocks – Guess & Score”

Short description: “Guess the right block 5 times to build your score. Your best runs live on Base.”

Button:

“Connect Wallet”

Once wallet is connected:

Show the player’s onchain best score (read from LuckyBlocksScoreboard).

Button: “Start Game”.

Game screen (run in progress)

Show:

“Round X of 5”

Current score for this run.

Display the latest AI narrative (intro, then per-round reactions).

Show 5 big buttons labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

When the player clicks one:

The code runs the game logic:

random secret between 1–5

compares

updates score

Shows whether the guess was correct or not.

Requests short AI reaction.

Moves to next round, unless it was round 5.

End-of-run screen

Show:

“Final score: X / 50”

AI-generated title and recap text.

Buttons:

“Submit Score Onchain”

Calls submitScore(score) on LuckyBlocksScoreboard with the final score of this run.

After transaction, update the displayed best score.

“Play Again”

Starts a new run (reset rounds and score to zero).

UI specifics:

Must be mobile-friendly and responsive.

Use a simple, clean layout. No need for complex design systems.

A light “Base / neon” theme is nice but not required for functionality.

5. Technical simplifications (important for reliability)

To keep this easy for an AI to implement in one shot:

Do not implement complex randomness onchain.
Use simple frontend randomness; we accept that players could cheat if they want. It’s just a casual game.

Do not implement complex tokenomics, reward pools, staking, or NFTs.
The only onchain part is the best score per wallet.

Do not build multi-contract architectures.
One contract LuckyBlocksScoreboard is enough.

Everything should be designed for:

Clarity

Few moving parts

High chance of working correctly on first deployment

6. Deliverables

From this prompt, please:

Generate and deploy the LuckyBlocksScoreboard contract on Base.

Build the mini app frontend with:

Wallet connection

5-round guessing game

Score calculation and display

Onchain best-score submission

Implement the AI calls:

Intro text at run start

Optional per-round reaction

End-of-run title + recap

The result should be a fully working, simple mini-game that can be demoed quickly:

Connect wallet → play 5 quick guesses → see score → store best score on Base → play again.

baseweb3bot.title: Baseweb3Bot
baseweb3bot.prompt:
"BaseGuard AI" (Full End-to-End Product Prompt)

Act as a Senior Blockchain Security Architect and Agentic AI Engineer.
Your task is to design a full working product for a Telegram Mini-App called:

🛡️ BaseGuard AI — Smart Contract & Transaction Security Analyzer

Users paste a Base network smart contract address or a transaction hash, and the Agent (powered by OpenxAI Xnodes) fetches, analyzes, and explains what it does in simple English, highlighting risks, backdoors, honeypots, or hidden logic.

The Agent must operate through its own ERC-6551 Token-Bound Account (TBA) to log verified analyses on-chain, proving decentralized trust.

🔥 Your Response MUST Include All Sections Below (Do NOT skip anything):
1. Executive Summary

What BaseGuard AI does.

Why it solves a critical user pain point.

Why decentralized AI via Xnodes is superior to centralized LLM security tools.

2. Full User Story (Step-by-Step Flow)

Describe the entire UX journey:

User opens BaseGuard AI in Telegram.

User pastes a contract address or transaction hash.

Backend fetches on-chain bytecode / ABI / storage / TX data.

OpenxAI Xnode analyzes:

Functions

Hidden permissions

Upgrade patterns

Dangerous opcodes

External call risks

tx.value, attacker vector, etc.

Agent produces plain-English explanation.

If high-risk → show red warning (“⚠️ This contract can drain your wallet”).

If safe → explain what it does (“Standard swap; no malicious opcodes found”).

Agent optionally publishes a signed on-chain report from its TBA wallet.

User can share report link as a verifiable security certificate.

3. Agent Architecture (Detailed)

Breakdown of every component:

A. ERC-721 Agent NFT

Represents the BaseGuard AI agent.

Gives identity to the analyzer.

B. ERC-6551 Token-Bound Account

Wallet owned by the Agent NFT.

Used to sign:

Analysis reports

Risk attestations

Verification proofs

C. Security Pipeline

Bytecode fetch

Static analysis

ABI decomposition

Simulation (eth_call)

Opcode detection (SELFDESTRUCT, DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE)

Permission map

Logical risk scoring

D. OpenxAI Xnode Workflows

Define every step Xnode must perform:

Data ingestion

Decompile bytecode

Pattern matching for known exploits

Generate summary in natural language

Emit structured JSON risk report

Sign output

E. Backend Orchestrator

Fetch on-chain data

Route tasks to Xnode

Validate Xnode signatures

Store reports

Interact with TBA wallet for attestations

4. Security Analysis Engine

Describe the exact logic the AI must perform:

Contract Analysis

Detect upgrade proxy patterns

Identify owner permissions

Analyze function visibility

Identify unrestricted transferFrom

Check if contract can drain tokens

Look for infinite approvals

Check for malicious mint logic

Analyze constructor edge cases

Identify honeypot conditions

Check LP lock status (optional)

Transaction Analysis

Simulate transaction using eth_call

Decode calldata

Identify fund flow

Show what tokens move where

Detect rug pull or drain pattern

Explain all outputs in plain English

5. Output Specification

Agent must output two forms:

A. Human-readable summary

Example style:

“⚠️ High Risk: This contract contains a backdoor function called withdrawAll() allowing the owner to drain all tokens.”

“✅ Safe: This is a standard Uniswap swap. No malicious behavior detected.”

B. Machine-readable JSON report

Must include:

{
  "contract": "0x...",
  "riskScore": 0-100,
  "riskLevel": "low|medium|high|critical",
  "flags": ["delegatecall", "upgradeable", "ownerPrivileges"],
  "functions": {...},
  "simulation": {...},
  "recommendation": "avoid / safe with caution / safe",
  "signature": "0xXnodeSignature"
}

6. Telegram Mini App UX Flow

Provide screen-by-screen UI description:

Home Screen:
“Paste a Contract Address or TX Hash to analyze”

Analyzing Screen:
“Fetching code… Running static analysis… Simulating behavior…”

Result Screen:

Threat summary

Flags

Recommendation

Button: “View On-Chain Verified Report”

Verified Report View:
Shows transaction hash of the TBA-signed attestation.

History Screen:
Users can see all past analyses.

Include examples of friendly text responses and warnings.

7. On-Chain Interaction Flow

Explain every transaction performed by BaseGuard TBA:

Agent computes risk report (off-chain).

Agent signs structured data with its TBA wallet.

Relayer submits signed attestations to Base.

On-chain record is stored as immutable proof of analysis.

This proves the analysis was produced by a decentralized agent and not tampered with.

8. Smart Contracts Required

(include function names)

A. BaseGuardAgentNFT.sol

mintAgent()

getAgentWallet()

Metadata

B. BaseGuardAttestation.sol

storeReport(agentWallet, hash, riskLevel)

verify(reportHash)

C. TBA Registry / Factory

(standard ERC-6551 pattern)

9. Backend Architecture (Node.js/TS)

List all services:

router-service (Telegram)

bytecode-service (fetch on-chain code)

analysis-service (calls Xnode)

simulation-service

relayer-service

attestation-service

database (Postgres)

cache (Redis)

Include API routes:

/analyze/address

/analyze/tx

/report/store

/report/verify

/history

10. Risk & Safety Requirements

Xnode must sign responses.

All reports require expiry timestamp.

Nonces to prevent replay.

Gas buffer: minimum $2 in agent wallet.

Max 20 analysis reports/day.

Verified contracts stored with SHA-256 hash.

User must explicitly approve any on-chain attestation.

11. “Winning Factor”

Emphasize the most important innovation:

The agent produces verifiable, tamper-proof security reports using its own on-chain identity (ERC-6551).

Proof of authenticity

Impossible for centralized AI to fake

Demonstrates full autonomous AI behavior on Base

12. 5-Min Demo Script

Show exactly how to present:

Paste suspicious contract

AI runs analysis

Shows “⚠️ This contract can drain your wallet”

AI signs report from ERC-6551 wallet

On-chain attestation appears in Base explorer

Show shareable report link

Done — judges immediately understand value

13. Build Plan (2 Week)

Include daily goals:

Week 1

Smart contracts

Telegram UI

Backend skeleton

Xnode integration

Bytecode fetcher

Week 2

Risk engine

Report signer

On-chain attestations

UX polish

Test cases

Final deploy to Base testnet

Include acceptance tests for each milestone.

batman.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. bdba.title: Bdba
bdba.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

bercerk.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS): AI Narrative & Market Manipulation Radar for Crypto Analysts
1. Project Overview

Develop an AI-powered system that identifies early-stage market narratives, detects coordinated manipulation attempts, and predicts narrative-driven price movements. The tool analyzes large-scale unstructured data across social networks, news outlets, Telegram channels, and on-chain behavior to detect coordinated patterns.

2. Core Purpose

Detect emerging trends before they become mainstream.

Identify artificial or coordinated hype campaigns.

Monitor behavior of influential wallets connected to narratives.

Predict potential market moves caused by narrative shifts.

3. Key Features
3.1 Narrative Detection Engine

NLP model trained on crypto-specific terminology

Clustering algorithms to group similar narratives

Trending narrative ranking system

Signal strength scoring (0–100)

3.2 Manipulation Pattern Detection

Unusual coordinated posting activity across X/Twitter, Telegram, TikTok

Bot activity detection (repetitive messages, sudden volume spikes)

AI-based shill detection

On-chain wash trading pattern detection

3.3 On-Chain + Social Linking

Map wallet activity to narrative spikes

Identify wallets consistently active before narrative surges

Show correlation between tweet activity and on-chain volume

3.4 Early Warning Alerts

New narrative detected

Suspicious coordinated activity

Whale wallet activity linked to narrative token

Sudden influx of “copy–paste” social posts

Unusual buying patterns on DEXs

3.5 Narrative Impact Score

For each narrative, system calculates:

Sentiment polarity

Engagement velocity

Wallet activity relevance

Market cap sensitivity

Risk/Manipulation probability

Final score: Bullish / Bearish / Neutral / Manipulated

4. Data Sources
4.1 Social

X/Twitter API

Reddit crypto communities

Telegram public channels

TikTok trending crypto hashtags

4.2 News & Media

RSS feeds of crypto news

Medium/Substack blogs

YouTube description + comments parser

4.3 On-Chain

Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain, Bitcoin

MEME token activity

DEX trade events (Uniswap, Raydium, PancakeSwap)

5. System Architecture
5.1 Data Pipeline

Data ingestion microservices

Message queue (Kafka)

NLP preprocessing (cleaning, tokenization, embedding)

Graph clustering for narrative grouping

5.2 AI Models

LLM-based narrative extraction

Anomaly detection model

Bot detection classifier

Wallet similarity clustering (graph neural networks)

5.3 Backend

Python (FastAPI)

Vector database (Pinecone / Milvus)

PostgreSQL for metadata

Redis for caching

5.4 Frontend

React.js

Real-time narrative stream

Graph visualizations (wallet-to-narrative links)

Sentiment heatmaps

6. Unique Visualizations

Narrative Timeline Graph (rise/fall of hype)

Manipulation Radar Heatmap

Wallet–Narrative Graph Network

Bot Activity Meter

Sentiment Constellation Map

7. Performance Requirements

Handle 5M+ social posts per day

On-chain indexing < 3 seconds delay

Narrative detection latency < 1 minute

Handle 50k concurrent users

8. Security

Sanitization of external data sources

Internal API authentication

Rate limits and DDoS protection

Encrypted user configurations

9. Deliverables

Full AI pipeline

Frontend dashboard

Backend API + docs

Data models + training scripts

Deployment scripts (Docker / Kubernetes)

Testing suite

Developer documentation

10. Competitive Advantage

This tool provides insights unavailable in typical analytics dashboards. It helps crypto analysts:

detect hype before the masses see it

avoid pump-and-dump traps

identify manipulative bot-driven narratives

find tokens early through on-chain/social connections

track wallet groups influencing sentiment

1. Adapt the System for a Mobile Application

You must develop a native or cross-platform mobile application version of the “AI Narrative & Market Manipulation Radar.”
The mobile app must include:

Real-time narrative alerts (push notifications).

Interactive dashboards optimized for mobile screens.

Lightweight data visualizations with high performance.

Secure local storage for user preferences.

Smooth UX, minimal latency, and battery-efficient background processes.

iOS and Android builds.

AI Narrative & Market Manipulation Radar — Mobile App Version

Sentiment scoring

New narrative detection

Limited narratives per day

Real-time alerts

Access to advanced manipulation radar

Whale movement correlations

Priority API speed

Advanced AI predictions

Extra narrative credits

High-frequency alert packages

Advanced on-chain modules

Auto-renewing subscriptions

App Store / Google Play billing

Optional lifetime license

berri.title: Berri
berri.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Personal Journal & Mood Tracker App
1. Project Overview

This app is designed to help users keep a personal digital journal combined with mood tracking. Users can write daily notes, reflect on their experiences, and track their emotional state over time. The app also provides insights, statistics, and optional reminders for journaling.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Journal Entries

Users can create, edit, and delete entries.

Each entry may include:

Date and time

Title

Body text

Optional mood tag (Happy, Sad, Stressed, Calm, etc.)

Optional image or attachment

Tagging system for categorizing entries (e.g., Work, Family, Personal Growth).

2.2 Mood Tracking

Users can log their mood multiple times per day.

Track intensity on a scale (e.g., 1–10).

Optional notes describing reasons for mood.

2.3 Analytics & Visualization

Graphs showing mood trends over days, weeks, or months.

Correlation between mood and journal entries.

Highlight unusual patterns or streaks.

2.4 Reminders & Notifications

Optional reminders to write journal entries or log mood.

Motivational notifications to encourage daily journaling.

2.5 Search & Filtering

Search entries by keyword, tag, or date.

Filter by mood or category.

2.6 User Interface

Clean and minimal UI for writing and reviewing entries.

Calendar view to quickly navigate past entries.

Dashboard showing mood trends and recent entries.

Light/Dark mode options.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile: iOS & Android

Optional web version

3.2 Performance

Creating or editing an entry should take <1 second.

Analytics charts should load instantly (<0.5s for 1000+ entries).

3.3 Data Storage

Local database (SQLite, Realm, Hive) for offline use.

Optional cloud sync for multi-device access.

3.4 Security

Protect user data with encryption.

Optional passcode, fingerprint, or face authentication.

3.5 Usability

Intuitive and simple UI for daily use.

Easy navigation between entries, calendar, and analytics.

4. Technical Stack
Mobile

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local database: SQLite, Realm, or Hive

Notifications: native push/local

Web (Optional)

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

5. Future Enhancements

Mood prediction using AI based on journal text.

Export entries to PDF or text files.

Collaborative journals (optional, share with therapist or friends).

Integration with mindfulness or meditation exercises.

Gamification: streaks for daily journaling.

Technical Specification (TS) – Multi-Translation Bible Application
1. Project Overview

The Multi-Translation Bible Application is a software tool designed to provide users access to various Bible translations, advanced word/phrase search, historical context, and biblical commentary.
The program serves as a study tool for readers who want deeper understanding through parallel translations, explanatory notes, and supplemental historical information.

The application is intended for personal study and educational use.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Bible Translations

The program must include support for multiple Bible translations such as:

King James Version (KJV)

New International Version (NIV)

English Standard Version (ESV)

Original-language texts (Hebrew/Greek) – optional

Any additional translations added by the user or developer

Features:

Switch translations instantly

Display parallel translations side-by-side

Store all translations locally or load via API

2.2 Search System

The search engine must allow:

Searching by word, phrase, or verse reference

Exact match and partial match

Search filters:

by Book (e.g., Genesis, Matthew)

by Testament (OT/NT)

by translation

Highlighting search results in the text

Displaying all verses that match the query

Search performance must be fast and optimized.

2.3 Historical Additions

The program should contain or support adding:

Historical background for each Bible book

Timeline of events

Information about authorship, dates, and cultural context

Maps (optional)

Extra articles (e.g., about ancient Israel, Roman Empire, traditions, etc.)

Historical materials may be shown:

in a separate section

or as pop-up notes linked to verses

2.4 Commentary & Interpretation

The application must include:

Commentary section for each book or verse

Ability to attach multiple commentary sources

Short explanations or theological notes

Cross-references to related passages

Users should be able to:

expand/collapse commentary

switch between commentary authors

2.5 User Interface Requirements

Clean, readable text layout

Chapter and verse navigation panel

Buttons for switching translations

Search bar with filters

Dedicated panels for:

Text

Commentary

Historical notes

Dark/Light mode

Font size adjustment

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

The program may be:

Desktop application (Windows/Linux/Mac)

Web application

Mobile app (optional)

3.2 Performance

Text display should load instantly

Search should return results under 0.5 seconds

Smooth navigation through books and chapters

3.3 Data Handling

All Bible texts stored in structured format (JSON, XML, or database)

Commentary and historical notes stored separately

Support offline use if translations are downloaded locally

3.4 Security

No user-generated content requires monitoring

If cloud sync is used, user notes must be encrypted

3.5 Legal

Only use translations with appropriate copyright or open licenses

Display a disclaimer:
“This application provides biblical texts and commentary for educational and personal study purposes.”

4. Recommended Technical Stack
Option A – Desktop (Python)

Python

PyQt5 / Tkinter

SQLite for storing texts

Requests for optional API access

Option B – Web Application

The Multi-Translation Bible Application is a software tool designed to provide users access to various Bible translations, advanced word/phrase search, historical context, and biblical commentary.

The application is intended for personal study and educational use.

2. Functional Requirements
