King James Version (KJV)

New International Version (NIV)

English Standard Version (ESV)

Original-language texts (Hebrew/Greek) – optional

Any additional translations added by the user or developer

Features:

Switch translations instantly

Display parallel translations side-by-side

Store all translations locally or load via API

2.2 Search System

The search engine must allow:

Searching by word, phrase, or verse reference

Exact match and partial match

Search filters:

by Book (e.g., Genesis, Matthew)

by Testament (OT/NT)

by translation

Highlighting search results in the text

Displaying all verses that match the query

Search performance must be fast and optimized.

2.3 Historical Additions

The program should contain or support adding:

Historical background for each Bible book

Timeline of events

Information about authorship, dates, and cultural context

Maps (optional)

Extra articles (e.g., about ancient Israel, Roman Empire, traditions, etc.)

Historical materials may be shown:

in a separate section

or as pop-up notes linked to verses

2.4 Commentary & Interpretation

The application must include:

Commentary section for each book or verse

Ability to attach multiple commentary sources

Short explanations or theological notes

Cross-references to related passages

Users should be able to:

expand/collapse commentary

switch between commentary authors

2.5 User Interface Requirements

Clean, readable text layout

Chapter and verse navigation panel

Buttons for switching translations

Search bar with filters

Dedicated panels for:

Text

Commentary

Historical notes

Dark/Light mode

Font size adjustment

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

The program may be:

Desktop application (Windows/Linux/Mac)

Web application

Mobile app (optional)

3.2 Performance

Text display should load instantly

Search should return results under 0.5 seconds

Smooth navigation through books and chapters

3.3 Data Handling

All Bible texts stored in structured format (JSON, XML, or database)

Commentary and historical notes stored separately

Support offline use if translations are downloaded locally

3.4 Security

No user-generated content requires monitoring

Only use translations with appropriate copyright or open licenses

Display a disclaimer:
“This application provides biblical texts and commentary for educational and personal study purposes.”

Python

Flutter or React Native

Technical Specification (TS) – Creative Ideas & Inspiration App
1. Project Overview

The Creative Ideas & Inspiration App helps users generate, organize, and develop creative ideas for projects, hobbies, writing, art, or problem-solving. It encourages brainstorming, tracks idea progress, and provides prompts and suggestions to spark creativity.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Idea Capture

Users can quickly create new ideas with:

Title / short description

Detailed description or notes

Category or type (e.g., Writing, Art, Design, DIY, Business)

Tags for organization (e.g., “brainstorm”, “urgent”, “inspirational”)

Optional attachments (images, links, sketches, documents)

2.2 Idea Organization

Organize ideas into projects, folders, or boards.

Assign status: “New”, “In Progress”, “Completed”.

Search and filter ideas by category, tag, or date.

2.3 Creative Prompts

Daily or random creative prompts to inspire new ideas.

Prompts can be generated automatically based on user preferences or categories.

Optional AI-generated suggestions for expanding existing ideas.

2.4 Progress Tracking

Track the development of an idea over time.

Add notes, images, or updates for each idea.

Visual timeline or kanban-style board for project progress.

2.5 Sharing & Collaboration

Share ideas or projects with friends, collaborators, or public community (optional).

Commenting or brainstorming together on shared ideas.

Export ideas or boards to PDF or image.

2.6 User Interface

Dashboard showing new ideas, trending ideas, and recently updated projects.

Quick-add button for capturing inspiration immediately.

Drag-and-drop interface for boards or project organization.

Light/Dark mode and customizable themes.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile (iOS & Android recommended)

Optional web app

3.2 Performance

Quick creation of new idea entries (<1 second).

Smooth navigation between boards, projects, and idea lists.

3.3 Data Storage

Local database (SQLite, Realm, or Hive) for offline access.

Optional cloud sync for multi-device use.

3.4 Security

Protect private ideas with encryption if stored in cloud.

Optional passcode, fingerprint, or face authentication.

3.5 Usability

Intuitive interface optimized for quick idea capture.

Minimal taps to save new ideas or notes.

Easy search and filtering.

4. Technical Stack
Mobile

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local database: SQLite, Realm, or Hive

Notifications: native push/local (for prompts or reminders)

Web (Optional)

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

5. Future Enhancements

AI-powered idea expansion and suggestions.

Mood-based idea prompts (e.g., prompts to spark creativity when stressed).

Gamification: streaks for daily idea creation, achievements for completed projects.

Community sharing and inspiration feed.

Integration with note-taking or drawing apps (e.g., exporting sketches or diagrams).

bouncy-banana.title: Bouncy Banana
bouncy-banana.prompt:
Create a fun, addictive, mobile-friendly Farcaster mini-app game called "Bouncy Banana Barrel".

Game concept (physics-based launcher):
- Player launches a banana projectile from the left side of the screen using touch/swipe: drag finger to set angle and power (like Angry Birds).
- Banana flies with realistic physics: gravity pulls it down, bounces elastically off randomly placed obstacles (floating platforms, walls, bumpers).
- Goal: Land the banana inside a glowing barrel target at the right/bottom of the screen. Perfect center = bonus points!
- If it lands in barrel: WIN with confetti explosion. Miss: retry with "Relaunch".
- Use Matter.js library (via CDN) for pro physics: bouncy collisions, rotation, friction.

Obstacles and levels:
- Level 1: Few simple platforms.
- Auto-progress: After win, add more obstacles (10 levels max, then endless mode).
- Banana peels trail behind for visual fun.

Features:
- Clean, vibrant design: Yellow banana emoji/graphic, wooden barrel, crypto-themed obstacles (e.g., coin bumpers, whale walls). Mobile-first, full-screen canvas.
- Power meter + angle indicator during drag.
- Score: Points = 1000 - (bounces * 100) + (distance bonus). Track high score and streak in localStorage.
- "Next Level" / "Endless Mode" buttons.
- Win screen: Big "SHARE ON FARCASTER" button that auto-generates cast: "🍌 BOUNCED my banana into the barrel in X bounces! Beat my score? Play Bouncy Banana Barrel → [your-miniapp-link] #farcaster #banana #degen"
- Optional wallet connect (Warpcast/WalletConnect): Include @farcaster handle in share.
- Sound effects: Boing on bounce, splash on win (Web Audio API).
- Fast, lightweight, instantly playable in Warpcast.

Generate full standalone HTML + CSS + JS code (include Matter.js CDN), ready to deploy as Base Mini App with farcaster.json verification.

boxer.title: Boxer
boxer.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

APP NAME & TAGLINE 
SpendSense Quiz

“Test your money skills. Learn something new every time

INTRO MESSAGE on a different page

Welcome to SpendSense Quiz!
Test how smart you are with money through fun, quick questions about spending, saving, and budgeting.
Learn easy tips that help you make better daily financial decisions.
Ready to find out your money score? Let’s begin!

SpendSense Quiz Questions
---

1. What’s the first step in tracking your daily expenses?

A. Ignore small purchases
B. Write down everything you spend
C. Only track big expenses
D. Wait until the end of the month
Correct: B
Explanation: You can’t manage what you don’t measure — start by recording everything.


---

2. Which of these is a need?

A. New sneakers
B. Pizza delivery
C. Rent
D. Concert tickets
Correct: C
Explanation: Needs are essentials like food, housing, and transport.


---

3. What’s a good habit for saving money?

A. Spend first, save later
B. Save only when you feel like it
C. Pay yourself first
D. Save only once a year
Correct: C
Explanation: Paying yourself first means saving before spending.


---

4. What is the biggest spending trap?

A. Buying only what you planned
B. Impulse buying
C. Creating a budget
D. Tracking expenses
Correct: B
Explanation: Impulse buying leads to unnecessary spending.


---

5. Which item is usually cheaper?

A. Eating out
B. Cooking at home
C. Ordering snacks daily
D. Buying bottled water every day
Correct: B
Explanation: Cooking at home generally saves more money.


---

6. What’s a safe way to avoid overspending?

A. Take only cash you need
B. Carry all your bank cards
C. Borrow money
D. Shop when hungry
Correct: A
Explanation: Limited cash helps you stay within your budget.


---

7. What does a budget help you do?

A. Spend more
B. Guess your expenses
C. Plan your money
D. Avoid saving
Correct: C
Explanation: Budgets help you plan and manage your money better.


---

8. What should you cut first when money is tight?

A. Rent
B. Transportation
C. Entertainment
D. Groceries
Correct: C
Explanation: Cut non-essentials, not necessities.


---

9. What is impulse buying?

A. Buying after planning
B. Buying with a list
C. Buying without thinking
D. Buying with a budget
Correct: C
Explanation: Impulse buying is unplanned and emotional.


---

10. Which of these is a good money habit?

A. Not checking your account
B. Borrowing frequently
C. Tracking expenses daily
D. Spending without a list
Correct: C
Explanation: Daily tracking helps you stay aware and disciplined.


---

11. What’s the best way to reduce data costs?

A. Stream videos all day
B. Use Wi-Fi when possible
C. Always buy daily plans
D. Ignore data usage
Correct: B
Explanation: Wi-Fi reduces mobile data charges.


---

12. When should you buy something new?

A. When you see a sale
B. When a friend has it
C. When you need it & can afford it
D. When you feel like it
Correct: C
Explanation: Buy only when necessary and within budget.


---

13. What’s a smart shopping strategy?

A. Shopping without a list
B. Buying on impulse
C. Price comparing
D. Shopping when stressed
Correct: C
Explanation: Comparing prices helps you save money.


---

14. What is the purpose of an emergency fund?

A. For vacations
B. For impulse purchases
C. For urgent, unexpected expenses
D. For gifts
Correct: C
Explanation: Emergency funds protect you during surprises.


---

15. Which payment method makes overspending easier?

A. Cash
B. Debit card
C. Credit card
D. Gift card
Correct: C
Explanation: Credit cards make it easy to spend money you don’t have yet.


---

16. What is a good rule before buying something?

A. Buy first, think later
B. Ask if you can borrow it
C. Ask: “Do I really need this?”
D. Copy what others buy
Correct: C
Explanation: Questioning the purchase stops wasteful spending.


---

17. What does “living within your means” mean?

A. Spending more than you earn
B. Spending less than you earn
C. Borrowing constantly
D. Ignoring a budget
Correct: B
Explanation: It means keeping expenses below your income.


---

18. What’s a good way to save while shopping?

A. Use a shopping list
B. Shop when hungry
C. Buy random items
D. Avoid comparing prices
Correct: A
Explanation: Lists help you stay focused and avoid extra spending.


---

19. If your income increases, what should you do first?

A. Increase unnecessary spending
B. Start impulse shopping
C. Increase savings
D. Travel immediately
Correct: C
Explanation: Save more before increasing lifestyle spending.


---

20. What’s the best way to track expenses?

A. Guess at the end of the month
B. Use a notebook or app daily
C. Never track anything
D. Ask people what they think
Correct: B
Explanation: Daily tracking gives clarity and control.

ENDING MESSAGE (After showing score)
Thanks for playing SpendSense Quiz!
Come back anytime to test yourself, learn new money tricks, and build better daily habits.

calculator.title: Calculator
calculator.prompt:
Create a responsive calculator app with two modes — Standard and Scientific — that users can toggle between using a simple switch button.

Requirements:

UI:

Clean, minimal interface similar to Windows Calculator (dark mode).

A toggle or button at the top to switch between “Standard” and “Scientific” modes.

A display area for showing current input and results.

A history panel to show recent calculations.

Standard Mode Features:

Basic arithmetic: addition (+), subtraction (−), multiplication (×), division (÷).

Percentage (%), square (x²), square root (√x), and reciprocal (1/x).

Clear (C), Clear Entry (CE), and backspace options.

Support for keyboard input.

Scientific Mode Features:

Include all Standard mode features.

Add advanced operations: exponent (x^y), factorial (n!), modulus (mod), logarithm (log, ln), π, e, parentheses, and trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan).

Option for degree/radian toggle.

Functionality:

Accurate mathematical parsing and operator precedence.

Smooth transition when toggling between modes (keep current input and result intact).

Store and recall memory values (MC, MR, M+, M−, MS).

Tech Stack Suggestion:

Frontend: React or Vue (or any framework supported by the AI).

Styling: Tailwind CSS or Material UI.

State management: React hooks or Vue composition API.

Bonus:

Optional theme toggle (Light/Dark).

Mobile-responsive layout.

Goal: Build an intuitive, aesthetic calculator app that users can switch between simple and scientific views instantly.

casidog.title: Casidog
casidog.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

cheker.prompt:
Program Description: Risk Assessment Tool for Long/Short Trading

Overview
The Risk Assessment Tool is a lightweight software application designed to help traders evaluate the potential risk before entering long or short positions on cryptocurrency, forex, or stock exchanges. The program analyzes market data, calculates key risk metrics, and provides a clear recommendation based on the user’s risk tolerance and market conditions.

Key Features

Real-time Market Data Input

Accepts price data from an exchange API or manual input.

Displays current trend direction, volatility, and price momentum.

Risk Metrics Calculation

Stop-loss and take-profit ratio estimation

Risk-to-reward ratio

Volatility Index (based on ATR or standard deviation)

Position size calculator based on user-defined risk percentage

Long/Short Risk Evaluation

Identifies the likelihood of trend continuation or reversal

Provides a “risk score” for opening long or short positions

Highlights dangerous market conditions (e.g., low liquidity or high volatility spikes)

User Interface

Simple dashboard showing key metrics and recommendations

Green/Yellow/Red risk indicator for both long and short entries

Optional chart displaying recent price movement

Recommendations Engine

Suggests optimal entry zone, stop-loss level, and potential profit target

Warns the user if the risk-to-reward ratio is unfavorable

Supports different trading strategies (scalping, swing trading, day trading)

Target Users

Beginner traders who need guidance

Intermediate traders wanting quick risk evaluation

Algorithmic traders needing a simple risk module for strategy validation

Platform

Can be implemented as a desktop app (Python), web app (JavaScript), or mobile app.

If you'd like, I can also generate:
✅ project architecture
✅ code template (Python/JS)
✅ UI mockup
✅ full technical specification (ТЗ)

cheko.title: Cheko
cheko.prompt:
Cheko: Sports Equipment Exchange App - Development Plan
1. App Concept and Overview

Name: Cheko
Purpose: A platform for users to exchange, borrow, or lend sports equipment.
Target Audience: Active individuals, sports enthusiasts, gyms, sports clubs, and outdoor activity lovers.

2. Key Features

User Registration & Authentication

Users can register and log in via email or social media accounts (Google, Facebook).

Profile creation with details (name, age, sport interests, location).

Equipment Listings

Users can list their sports equipment for exchange or loan.

Options to add descriptions, pictures, and condition of the equipment.

Categories based on sport (e.g., tennis rackets, bicycles, fishing gear).

Search & Filter

Users can search for specific items by name, sport type, or location.

Filters for item condition, distance, and availability.

In-App Messaging

Chat functionality for users to communicate, negotiate terms, and arrange the exchange.

Notifications for new messages, requests, and offers.

Transaction Management

Users can agree on the terms (exchange/loan).

Option to mark items as exchanged/borrowed once completed.

Rating and review system after transactions for feedback.

Geolocation

Integration of GPS to show nearby users with available equipment.

Map view to see local exchanges and borrow opportunities.

Push Notifications

Alerts for new listings, offers, and messages.

Reminders for pending exchanges or returns.

Admin Panel

Moderation tools to manage users, listings, and reports of inappropriate behavior.

Analytics dashboard to track app usage, popular categories, etc.

3. Technology Stack

Frontend (Mobile App)

React Native: For cross-platform development (iOS & Android).

Expo: For faster development, deployment, and testing.

Redux: For state management.

React Navigation: For seamless navigation between screens.

Backend

Node.js with Express.js: Server-side framework for API development.

MongoDB: NoSQL database to store user data, equipment listings, and transactions.

Firebase: For real-time messaging and notifications.

Authentication

Firebase Authentication: For easy email and social media logins.

JWT (JSON Web Tokens): For secure user sessions.

Geolocation

Google Maps API: To implement location-based search and show nearby users.

Push Notifications

Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM): To send notifications for new listings, messages, etc.

Hosting/Server

Heroku or AWS for backend deployment.

MongoDB Atlas: For cloud-based database hosting.

4. App Development Timeline

Phase 1: Planning & Research (1-2 weeks)

Define user personas and app requirements.

Conduct competitor analysis.

Finalize app features, design, and user journey.

Phase 2: Design & Prototyping (2-3 weeks)

Create wireframes and app mockups (Figma or Adobe XD).

Design user interfaces (UI) and user experience (UX) for all screens.

Review and refine design based on feedback.

Phase 3: Backend Development (3-4 weeks)

Set up server and database structure.

Develop APIs for user management, equipment listing, messaging, etc.

Implement authentication and authorization.

Develop geolocation features.

Phase 4: Frontend Development (3-4 weeks)

Develop the core screens (Home, Profile, Equipment Listings, Messages, etc.).

Implement search and filtering functionalities.

Integrate with backend APIs for data exchange.

Add in-app messaging and notifications.

Phase 5: Testing & Bug Fixing (2 weeks)

Conduct unit tests, integration tests, and user acceptance testing (UAT).

Fix bugs and performance issues.

Test app on various devices (iOS, Android).

Phase 6: Launch & Deployment (1-2 weeks)

Deploy backend to a cloud server (Heroku or AWS).

Submit the app to App Store and Google Play Store.

Set up app store optimization (ASO) for visibility.

Phase 7: Post-Launch & Maintenance (Ongoing)

Monitor app performance and user feedback.

Release updates for bug fixes and new features.

Regularly update the app with new sports categories and equipment types.

5. Monetization Strategy

Freemium Model

Basic features are free (e.g., limited listings per month).

Premium features like unlimited listings, advanced search filters, or enhanced visibility can be part of a paid subscription.

Transaction Fees

A small percentage fee on exchanges or loans made via the platform.

Advertising

In-app ads for sports brands or local events.

6. Marketing & Growth Strategy

Social Media Campaigns

Leverage Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok to target sports enthusiasts.

Collaborate with influencers in the sports and fitness community.

Referral Program

Offer rewards or credits for users who refer friends to join the app.

Partnerships

Partner with gyms, sports clubs, or sporting goods stores to promote the app.

Community Engagement

Create a blog or forum for users to share tips, reviews, and recommendations for sports equipment.

7. Potential Challenges

User Trust & Safety: Ensuring that users trust each other with their equipment.

Solution: Implement a rating and review system, and consider user verification.

Logistics & Insurance: Users may hesitate to exchange expensive equipment.

Solution: Partner with insurance companies to offer optional coverage during exchanges or loans.

8. Future Features & Expansion

Equipment Delivery Integration: Integration with delivery services to allow users to send items safely.

Rentals: Expand to allow rentals in addition to exchanges (e.g., daily/weekly rentals).

Multi-language Support: Expand the app to multiple languages to target international users.

click-the-color.title: Click The Color
click-the-color.prompt:
Game Title/Concept: "Color Rush" – A fast-paced "find and tap the matching colors" game.

Gameplay:
- Create a grid of 7 rows × 5 columns (35 clickable squares in total).
- Each square must be filled with a random solid color.
- Use only a set of 8-10 common, clearly distinguishable colors (e.g., red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, brown, black, white, cyan, lime, etc.). Make sure the colors are very different from each other so they are easy to recognize.

Layout (top to bottom):
1. Top bar containing:
   - A large example color swatch (the target color for the current round).
   - Next to it, clearly display the name of the color (optional but recommended).
   - A countdown timer (format: 10.0 seconds, with one decimal place).

2. Below the top bar: the 7×5 grid of colored squares.

Rules and mechanics:
- At the start of each round, randomly choose one of the colors as the "target color" and show it in the top bar.
- Randomly fill all 35 grid squares with colors (including several squares of the target color). There must always be at least 3–10 squares of the target color.
- The timer starts at 10 seconds for the first round and counts down to 0.
- The player must tap ONLY the squares that exactly match the target color shown at the top.
- Tapping a wrong color does nothing negative (no penalty), but it wastes time.
- As soon as the player has correctly tapped EVERY square that matches the target color, the round is instantly won:
   - The timer immediately freezes/stops at the remaining time.
   - A "Round Complete!" message appears briefly.
   - The next round automatically starts after 1 second.
- For each successfully completed round, the starting time for the next round decreases by 1 second (10 → 9 → 8 → 7 → ... down to a minimum of 2 or 1 second).
- If the timer reaches 0 before the player finishes tapping all correct squares, the game ends and shows the final score (number of rounds completed).

Additional requirements:
- Make the game visually clean, colorful, and mobile-friendly (large tap targets).
- Add a score counter: "Round X" or "Score: X rounds".
- After game over, show the final score and a "Play Again" button.
- Include satisfying sound effects (optional but preferred) for correct taps, round win, and game over.

clock.title: Clock
clock.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

color-rush.title: Color Rush
color-rush.prompt:
Make a color-matching game:

- Grid: 7 rows × 5 columns = 35 squares
- Each square has a random color (use only 8 simple colors: red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, black)

At the top:
- Show one big target color + the timer

Game rules:
- Timer starts at 10 seconds and counts down.
- Player must tap all squares that have exactly the same color as the target.
- When all correct squares are tapped, the round is won and the timer stops immediately.
- Next round starts automatically with 1 second less (10 → 9 → 8 → etc.).
- If timer reaches 0, game over.

Show the round number or score.
When game ends, show final score and "Play Again" button.

Make it clean and easy to tap on phone.

3. Render the matrix using a library like Chart.js or D3.js.
4. Add a time-slider to change the calculation window dynamically.
5. Deploy as a single-page application.

Provide users with a simple offline tool to track evaluation points for new crypto projects and keep everything organized in one place.

crypto-goal-tracker.title: Crypto Goal Tracker
crypto-goal-tracker.prompt:
Crypto Goal Tracker — App Description

Create a simple mini app called “Crypto Goal Tracker”.
The app helps users set and track their personal crypto-related goals.
No internet access or external data is required — all information is entered manually by the user.

Core Features
 1. A text input field for the user to enter a goal name (e.g., “Save 0.5 ETH”, “Buy 10 SOL”).
 2. A numeric input field to set a target amount.
 3. A numeric input field to enter the current progress amount.
 4. A button “Add Goal” that saves the goal to a list.
 5. A visible list displaying all added goals in a clean layout:
 • Goal name
 • Target amount
 • Current progress
 • Progress percentage
 6. A “Update Progress” button for each goal, opening a small dialog where the user can enter a new progress value.
 7. A “Delete” button for each goal to remove it.

How the app should work
 • User enters a goal name, target, and current progress.
 • Presses “Add Goal”, and the goal appears in the list.
 • The app calculates the progress percentage automatically (current ÷ target × 100).
 • User can update progress anytime using the built-in update dialog.
 • User can delete goals from the list.
 • All data lives inside the app session and requires no external API.

UI Requirements
 • Inputs placed at the top in a clean form layout.
 • Goals displayed below in a simple table or cards.
 • Progress percentage should update immediately after any change.
 • Buttons and labels must be clearly marked.

Goal of the App

Provide users with a simple, offline-friendly way to track personal crypto accumulation goals without any external integrations.

crypto-hangman.title: Crypto Hangman
crypto-hangman.prompt:
Build a very simple Hangman mini-game.

Requirements:

1) Use this exact list of 20 words (all lowercase except OPENXAI):
blockchain, bitcoin, ethereum, wallet, gas, mining, staking,
airdrop, liquidity, defi, halving, bullrun, bearish,
smartcontract, token, ledger, governance, hash, satoshi, OPENXAI

2) At the start of the game:
   - Select 1 random word from the list.
   - Display it as underscores (e.g. "_ _ _ _ _").

3) Add alphabet buttons A–Z.
   - If a guessed letter exists in the word → reveal it.
   - If not → increase wrong attempt count.

4) Maximum wrong attempts = 6.
   - If player reaches 6 wrong guesses → show “You Lost” and reveal the word.
   - If player guesses all letters → show “You Won”.

5) Add a “Play Again” button that restarts the game and picks a new random word.

6) Keep UI very simple and compatible with Farcaster mini-apps:
   - Basic text, buttons, and simple layout.
   - No animations or multiple levels yet.

Output:
- Provide complete working code.
- Keep everything minimal and easy to extend later.

cryptogastracker.title: Cryptogastracker
cryptogastracker.prompt:
GasPulse – Crypto Gas Fee Tracker

Description:
GasPulse is a simple, real-time gas tracker that displays current gas fees on Base and Ethereum networks. Users can quickly check the latest gas costs, recommended fee levels (low, average, high), and basic traffic insights.

Core Functions:
 1. Show current gas fees for:
 • Base
 • Ethereum
 2. Display recommended gas levels:
 • Low
 • Average
 • High
 3. Auto-update:
 • Refresh gas data every time the user opens the app
 • Allow manual refresh with a “Refresh Gas Data” button
 4. Simple UI:
 • Gas values shown as numbers
 • Color indicators:
 • Green = low
 • Yellow = average
 • Red = high
 5. Extra utility:
 • “Explain gas fee” button → AI gives a simple explanation of how gas fees work
 • “Estimate transaction cost” → user enters gas units → app calculates estimated cost

User Actions:
 • “Check Gas Now”
 • “Refresh Data”
 • “Estimate Transaction Cost”
 • “What are gas fees?”

Requirements:
 • No external API needed — use built-in AI estimation based on common gas ranges.
 • Keep everything simple and minimalistic.
 • The app should run fully on AI logic and internal calculations.

dca-planner-lite.title: Dca Planner Lite
dca-planner-lite.prompt:
Title: DCA Planner Lite

Description:
Create a simple app that helps users plan their Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) strategy. The app should work entirely offline and must not use the internet or external APIs. All data is manually entered by the user.

Functionality:
 • Display three input fields:
 1. “Token Name”
 2. “Investment Amount per Period”
 3. “Number of Periods”
 • Add a button labeled “Add Plan”. When clicked, the app calculates:
 • Total Investment = Investment Amount × Number of Periods
 • Show the results in a section titled “Your DCA Plans”, where each entry includes:
 • Token Name
 • Investment Amount per Period
 • Number of Periods
 • Total Investment
 • Each plan should have a “Delete” button allowing the user to remove that specific entry.
 • Add a “Clear All” button to remove all DCA plans.
 • If any required field is empty or invalid, show a message:
“Please fill in all fields with valid numbers.”

UI Requirements:
 • Use simple UI: text fields, labels, buttons, and a list.
 • Keep the layout clean and easy to understand.
 • All calculations and updates must happen locally inside the app.

dcasim.title: Dcasim
dcasim.prompt:
Idea: A Dollar Cost Averaging (DCA) simulator and backtester.
User Goal: Validate the strategy of buying small amounts regularly versus trying to time the market.
Core Features (MVP):

* Input: Coin, Investment Amount, Frequency (Daily/Weekly), Start Date.
* Comparison: DCA vs. Lump Sum (buying all at once on day 1).
* Output: Total invested, Current Value, ROI %, Average Entry Price.
* Visual chart of Portfolio Value over time.

Development Plan:

1. Build a robust historical price database (daily close prices).
2. Create the calculation logic: iterate through dates and simulate buys.
3. Develop a clean, "calculator-style" UI.
4. Add a "Share Result" feature (image generation) for social media.
5. Add support for top 50 coins.

demof.title: Demof
demof.prompt:
Demof – Mini App Creation Plan (Ticket Exchange Platform)
1. Project Overview

Demof is a mini application that enables users to exchange, resell, or give away event tickets in a secure and easy way. The platform connects people who can no longer attend an event with those who are looking for tickets.

2. Core Features
2.1 User Accounts

Email / phone / social login

User profile with basic information

Ticket ownership verification (optional)

2.2 Ticket Listings

Create a ticket listing (event name, date, seat, price, QR code upload)

Edit or delete listings

Mark ticket as sold / exchanged

2.3 Ticket Exchange Mechanism

Direct message between users

Button: Request Exchange or Buy Ticket

Automatic confirmation and ticket transfer system (optional MVP: manual confirmation)

2.4 Event Search & Filtering

Search by event name, city, category

Filter by date, price, availability

2.5 Notifications

When a requested ticket becomes available

Messages and exchange confirmations

2.6 Security & Verification

Basic verification of users

Secure payment integration (Stripe/PayPal) – optional for MVP

Fraud protection (warnings, reporting)

3. Technology Stack
Frontend

React / React Native (for mobile mini-app)

TailwindCSS or Material UI

Backend

Node.js + Express

Database: MongoDB / PostgreSQL

Authentication: JWT / OAuth

Third-party Integrations

Payment API: Stripe or PayPal

Cloud storage for tickets: AWS S3 / Firebase Storage

Notifications: Firebase Cloud Messaging

4. Architecture Overview

Client application communicates with REST API backend

Database stores users, tickets, and transactions

Storage service keeps uploaded ticket images

Payment gateway handles financial operations (if included)

5. Development Milestones
Phase 1 — Planning & Design (1–2 weeks)

Define MVP functionality

Create wireframes & UI/UX design

Prepare database schema

Phase 2 — Backend Development (2–4 weeks)

Set up authentication

Implement ticket CRUD operations

Implement messaging (basic)

Add event search & filters

Deploy backend

Phase 3 — Frontend Development (3–6 weeks)

Build UI components

Integrate API endpoints

Add ticket upload & preview

Add messaging UI

Implement notifications

Phase 4 — Testing & QA (1–2 weeks)

Unit and integration tests

Usability testing

Fix bugs and optimize performance

Phase 5 — Launch & Iteration (ongoing)

Publish the app (web or mobile)

Collect user feedback

Add advanced features: secure escrow payments, QR code auto-verification, analytics dashboard

6. Optional Future Features

AI-based fraud detection

Dynamic price suggestions

Event organizer partnerships

Loyalty system or points for exchanges

destroy-machine.title: Destroy Machine
destroy-machine.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

 • Plans displayed below in table or card format with clear labels.
 • Buttons should be easy to identify and intuitive to use.

erenda.title: Erenda
erenda.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

financ.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Personal Finance & Expense Tracker App
1. Project Overview

The Personal Finance & Expense Tracker App helps users track their income, expenses, and savings goals. The app categorizes spending, provides insights, and assists with budgeting to improve financial habits.

Goal: Enable users to manage personal finances efficiently and make informed spending decisions.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Expense & Income Logging

Users can add income and expense entries with:

Amount

Date and time

Category (e.g., Food, Transport, Bills, Entertainment)

Optional notes

Option to attach receipts or photos.

2.2 Budget & Goal Management

Create monthly budgets by category.

Set savings goals with target amounts and deadlines.

Track progress toward goals and budgets.

2.3 Analytics & Visualization

Dashboard with total income, expenses, and balance.

Graphs and charts showing spending by category or time period.

Monthly/weekly summaries.

Highlight overspending or unusual spending patterns.

2.4 Notifications & Reminders

Reminders for bill payments or recurring expenses.

Alerts when spending exceeds budget limits.

2.5 Search & Filtering

Search past transactions by date, amount, category, or note.

Filter by income vs. expenses, category, or time period.

2.6 User Interface

Clean and intuitive UI with dashboard overview.

Easy addition of income/expense with minimal taps.

Light/Dark mode and customizable categories.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile: iOS & Android

Optional web version

3.2 Performance

Logging a transaction should take <1 second.

Dashboard and charts should load instantly (<0.5 seconds for 1000+ entries).

3.3 Data Storage

Local storage for offline access.

Optional cloud sync for multi-device access (encrypted).

3.4 Security

Optional passcode, fingerprint, or face authentication.

Encrypt sensitive data in local and cloud storage.

3.5 Usability

Minimal taps to log expenses (<3 taps).

Intuitive navigation between dashboard, budgets, and transaction history.

4. Technical Stack
Mobile

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local DB: SQLite, Realm, or Hive

Notifications: native push/local

Web (Optional)

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

5. Future Enhancements

AI-powered insights for spending habits.

Automatic categorization of expenses using OCR from receipts.

Multi-currency and exchange rate support.

Gamification: achievements for meeting savings goals.

Integration with bank APIs for automatic transaction import.

fitness.title: Fitness
fitness.prompt:
Fitness & Wellness App “FitGen”**

1. Project Overview

FitGen is a mobile application designed for health-conscious users to track workouts, diet, and wellness habits. The app provides personalized training plans, meal recommendations, progress tracking, and community features.

2. Objectives

Help users create personalized workout plans.

Provide diet recommendations based on fitness goals.

Track wellness metrics like sleep, water intake, and steps.

Engage users through gamification and social challenges.

Integrate with wearable devices (Apple Watch, Fitbit, Garmin).

3. Core Features
3.1 Personal Training Plans

AI-based workout recommendations based on goals, fitness level, and available equipment.

Workouts for strength, cardio, flexibility, and HIIT.

Video tutorials and step-by-step guidance.

Ability to log completed workouts.

3.2 Nutrition & Meal Plans

Personalized diet plans based on calories, macros, and allergies.

Recipe library with step-by-step instructions.

Meal logging and calorie tracking.

Integration with barcode scanner for packaged foods.

3.3 Health & Wellness Tracking

Steps, distance, calories burned (integration with Google Fit / Apple Health).

Water intake tracker.

Sleep tracking and reminders.

Mood and stress level logging.

3.4 Community & Gamification

Challenges and leaderboards.

Groups and friend connections.

Badges and achievements.

Sharing workout progress on social media.

3.5 Analytics & Progress

Weekly/monthly progress reports.

Body metrics tracking (weight, BMI, body fat).

Graphical charts and insights.

Personalized suggestions to improve performance.

4. Platform Requirements

Mobile: iOS 13+, Android 9+

Recommended Tech Stack:

Frontend: Flutter / React Native

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

AI/ML: Python (TensorFlow / PyTorch)

5. UI/UX Requirements

Clean, modern, minimalistic design with bright and motivating colors.

Easy navigation with tabs: Workout, Nutrition, Progress, Community, Profile.

Interactive charts for progress tracking.

Personalized dashboard on app start.

6. Database Architecture (ERD Description)

Main Entities:

Users

Workouts

Exercises

Meal Plans

Recipes

Progress Logs

Challenges

Friends / Community

Example Tables:

Users: id, name, email, password_hash, goals, fitness_level

Workouts: id, user_id, date, exercises, completed_flag

Exercises: id, name, type, duration, video_url

Meal Plans: id, user_id, meals, calories, macros

Recipes: id, name, ingredients, steps, nutrition_info

Progress Logs: id, user_id, weight, body_fat, steps, water_intake, sleep_hours

7. Agile User Stories

As a user, I want to follow a workout plan so I can improve my fitness level.

As a user, I want personalized meal suggestions so I can meet my nutrition goals.

As a user, I want to track my sleep and water intake so I can maintain wellness habits.

As a user, I want to participate in challenges to stay motivated.

8. Security Requirements

Role-based access (User / Admin)

Passwords hashed and stored securely

Encrypted personal and health data

GDPR/CCPA compliance

9. Performance Requirements

App load ≤ 2 seconds

Sync with wearable devices ≤ 5 seconds

Real-time notifications for reminders and challenges

10. Monetization Model

Free tier: basic workouts and meal plans

Premium subscription: personalized AI-based plans, challenges, recipes, analytics

One-time purchases: guided courses or specialized programs

11. KPIs

Daily active users (DAU)

Workouts completed per week

Meal logging consistency

User retention rate

Premium conversion rate

flappy-coin.title: Flappy Coin
flappy-coin.prompt:
ROLE & GOAL
You are an expert web game developer creating a simple, fast-loading browser mini game inspired by Flappy Bird, but with a fun crypto theme. The game will live as a mini app and should be easy to play in under 1 minute per round. Players can optionally win tiny sponsored token rewards based on their score, using a pre-funded prize pool that I manage outside the game.

GAME CONCEPT

Title: “The Flappy Coin”

Core mechanic: Tap / click / spacebar to make a character “flap” and avoid obstacles. If they hit an obstacle or the ground, the run ends.

Theme:

Character: a cute pixel-style crypto coin or rocket (with eyes / personality).

Obstacles: on-chain themed (e.g., “gas clouds,” “rug spikes,” “bear walls,” “regulation pipes”).

Background: simple scrolling sky or blockchain-style grid so it runs smoothly on mobile and desktop.

GAMEPLAY & SCORING

Simple one-button control:

Desktop: spacebar or click.

Mobile: tap anywhere.

Score = number of obstacles successfully passed.

Show:

Live score during the run.

“Game Over” screen with: current score, best score (local), and how much token the player would earn for this run.

Game speed should increase slightly as the score goes up to keep it challenging.

REWARD LOGIC (TINY CRYPTO PRIZES)
I will handle the actual token distribution off-chain or via a backend API. Your job is to:

Implement pure front-end reward logic that calculates a “suggested reward” for a completed run using this model:

Example reward tiers (configurable in one place in the code):

Score 0–9 → $0 in tokens (no reward)

Score 10–24 → $0.01 worth of tokens

Score 25–49 → $0.03 worth of tokens

Score 50+ → $0.10 worth of tokens (max per run)

Output the reward in two ways on Game Over:

In USD equivalent (e.g., “Estimated reward: $0.03 in tokens”).

In token units, using a placeholder token symbol (e.g., $GAME):

Let me easily update: TOKEN_SYMBOL, TOKEN_DECIMALS, and TOKEN_USD_PRICE in a config object.

The front-end must not hold private keys or send transactions by itself. Instead, after the game:

Show a CTA button such as “Claim via Sponsor” that triggers a function call like onClaimReward(score, estimatedReward) that I can later wire up to my backend or wallet flow.

SPONSORED PRIZE POOL CONSTRAINTS
Design with the assumption that:

I maintain a finite sponsored prize pool of tokens.

Rewards are tiny and mostly for fun: micro-amounts like $0.01–$0.10.

You should:

Include a comment in the code where I can plug in a backend API (e.g., GET /rewards/estimate and POST /rewards/claim).

Include a visible disclaimer in small text:

“Rewards are promotional, limited, and not guaranteed. Payouts are subject to sponsor availability and may change or end at any time.”

TECH + IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS

Build as a single-page HTML/CSS/JavaScript app using Canvas or a simple DOM approach. No build tools required.

Requirements:

Runs smoothly in a browser inside an iframe/mini app.

Mobile-first, but also playable on desktop.

Clear code structure: separate game logic, rendering, and reward logic into readable functions.

Provide:

index.html, style.css, and script.js (or clearly separable sections).

Comments explaining where to:

Change artwork / colors / character sprite.

Configure reward tiers and token price.

Plug in a wallet or backend onClaimReward handler.

UI & UX

Start screen:

Game title: The Flappy Coin.

“Tap to Start” + brief instructions: “Tap / press space to flap. Avoid obstacles. Higher score = tiny token rewards.”

Game screen:

Top-left: current score.

Top-right: best score.

Game Over screen:

Score, best score, and estimated reward.

Two buttons: “Play Again” and “Claim via Sponsor”.

Tiny disclaimer text about rewards being promotional and limited.

ABUSE / ANTI-SPAM CONSIDERATIONS (FRONT-END ONLY)

Add basic protections that I can later extend:

Limit displayed reward to a maximum per run and optionally a maximum per session (configurable).

Include a simple session ID or timestamp value that can be sent to my backend when claiming.

Do not implement complex security; just structure the code clearly so I can plug in rate limits or per-wallet caps later.

DELIVERABLE

Generate the complete minimal code for this game:

A working prototype I can drop into a mini-app environment.

Easy to customize: colors, character sprite, token symbol, and reward tiers.

After generating the code, briefly summarize:

How the scoring works.

How the reward calculation works.

Where in the code I should integrate my backend or wallet claim flow.

flip-the-coin.title: Flip The Coin
flip-the-coin.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

futures.title: Futures
futures.prompt:
Futures – Mini App Development Plan
1. Project Overview

Futures is a lightweight web/mobile application that allows users to share, view, and discuss cryptocurrency price forecasts. The goal is to create a simple, fast, and community-driven platform focused on short-term and long-term crypto predictions.

2. Core Features
2.1 User Accounts

Email, Google, or wallet-based login (optional Web3 auth).

Basic profile with username and avatar.

User stats: number of forecasts, accuracy score.

2.2 Forecast Creation

Select a cryptocurrency (BTC, ETH, etc.).

Choose forecast type:

Short-term (24h)

Mid-term (7 days)

Long-term (30+ days)

Enter predicted price and reasoning (optional).

Set visibility: public or private.

2.3 Forecast Feed

List of predictions from users.

Filters: by coin, timeframe, popularity, accuracy.

Voting/likes or reaction system.

2.4 Forecast Validation

Automatic checking of outcomes when time expires.

Accuracy score calculation (e.g., mean percentage error).

Displaying “successful/unsuccessful” badges.

2.5 Commenting & Discussion

Comment threads under each prediction.

Upvote/downvote comments.

2.6 Notifications

Forecast result notifications.

New comments or likes.

Trending forecasts.

2.7 Admin Panel

User moderation.

Forecast moderation.

Basic analytics.

3. Technical Stack
3.1 Frontend

React / Next.js

TailwindCSS or Chakra UI

State management: Redux / Zustand

3.2 Backend

Node.js / Express or NestJS

REST or GraphQL API

Authentication: JWT or Firebase Auth

3.3 Database

MongoDB or PostgreSQL

Redis (optional) for caching trending forecasts

3.4 Crypto Data Provider

CoinGecko API / Binance API for real-time prices

3.5 Hosting

Vercel or Netlify (frontend)

Render, Railway, or AWS (backend)

MongoDB Atlas (database)

4. App Structure
4.1 Screens / Pages

Landing page — app description and login.

Dashboard — personalized forecast feed.

Create Forecast — form for adding predictions.

Forecast Details — comments, likes, stats.

User Profile — forecasts history, accuracy.

Admin Panel — moderation tools.

5. Development Stages
Stage 1 — Planning & Design (1–2 weeks)

Feature set finalization

UX wireframes

UI design in Figma

Stage 2 — Backend Development (2–4 weeks)

API structure

Authentication

Forecast CRUD

Accuracy calculation engine

Integration with crypto price API

Stage 3 — Frontend Development (3–5 weeks)

Building all pages

API integration

Responsive UI

Stage 4 — Testing (1–2 weeks)

Unit & integration tests

Bug fixing

UX refinement

Stage 5 — Deployment (1 week)

Deploy frontend + backend

Domain + SSL setup

Performance optimization

Stage 6 — Launch & Iteration

Beta testing

Collect user feedback

Add extended features (chat, leaderboards, etc.)

6. Possible Future Features

Web3 wallet login (MetaMask, WalletConnect)

NFT badges for accurate predictors

Social trading tools

Real-time chat rooms for each cryptocurrency

AI-generated forecast suggestions

game.title: Game
game.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

Technical Specification (TS) – Casual Puzzle Game App
1. Project Overview

The Casual Puzzle Game app is a mobile game designed for quick and entertaining gameplay. The game focuses on solving puzzles, matching elements, or completing levels with increasing difficulty.
The goal is to provide a fun, addictive experience with smooth controls, progressive challenges, and optional social features.

2.1 Gameplay Mechanics

Players interact with game elements by tapping, swiping, or dragging.

Game modes:

Level-based puzzles: Complete tasks to unlock the next level.

Endless mode: Play as long as possible for a high score.

Scoring system:

Points for completing levels or combos.

Bonuses for speed, accuracy, or streaks.

Level difficulty increases progressively.

2.2 Levels & Challenges

Include at least 50 levels for initial release.

Each level can have:

Time limit or move limit

Obstacles or special tiles

Goals (e.g., clear all tiles, match 3 colors)

Optional: daily or weekly challenge levels.

2.3 Rewards & Progression

Players earn coins, stars, or points for completing levels.

Unlockable items, themes, or power-ups.

Track player progress:

Levels completed

High scores

Achievements

2.4 User Interface

Main menu with options:

Play

Levels selection

Shop / Power-ups

Settings

In-game UI:

Score counter

Timer or moves remaining

Pause button

End-of-level summary screen with score, rewards, and option to replay.

2.5 Social Features (Optional)

Leaderboards to compare scores with friends or global players.

Share achievements on social media.

Invite friends to challenge levels.

2.6 Settings

Music and sound effects on/off.

Notifications on/off.

Language selection.

Optional: difficulty adjustment.

3.1 Platform

Mobile: iOS and Android (cross-platform recommended)

Optional web version

Smooth animations at 60 FPS.

Responsive touch controls.

Levels should load in <1 second.

Save game progress locally (SQLite, Realm, or device storage).

Optional cloud save for cross-device sync.

Protect user progress and in-game purchases.

Optional user authentication for social features.

Intuitive tutorial for first-time players.

Easy-to-read visual elements and feedback for player actions.

Mobile

Framework: Unity (C#) or Godot (GDScript/C#)

Multiplayer mode for head-to-head challenges.

In-game events and rewards.

Idea: A tool to detect Price Gaps (CME gaps or weekend gaps).
User Goal: Trade the "Gap Fill" strategy (price often returns to fill empty trading zones).
Core Features (MVP):

* Detect difference between Friday Close and Sunday Open (CME Futures).
* Detect gaps on lower timeframes during high volatility.
* Chart overlay showing open gaps.
* Alert when price enters a "Gap Zone".

4. Dashboard showing list of active unfilled gaps and their distance from current price.
5. Push notifications when a gap fill starts.

Gas3Guardian AI is a DApp running exclusively on Base network (Coinbase-built Ethereum Layer-2) that helps users save on gas fees by:
1. Predicting Base gas prices for the next 1–10 minutes using a simple machine-learning model (linear regression + lightweight ensemble) hosted on OpenxAI X Studio.
2. Bundling up to 10 user transactions into a single transaction only when predicted gas is low.
3. Strictly enforcing a user-defined maximum budget — no transaction ever costs more than the set limit.

Mandatory technical facts (do not invent anything beyond these):
- Chain: Base mainnet only (not Ethereum mainnet)
- Average Base gas price November 2025: 0.01–0.1 gwei
- AI model deployed via OpenxAI X Studio (can use deepseekr1 template or small custom model)
- Smart contract written in Solidity 0.8.x, fully EVM-compatible
- Revenue model: 1% fee taken only from the gas amount actually saved (not 1% of total transaction value)
- AI model monetized via X Studio subscription NFT or pay-per-call
- Frontend: React + Wagmi/viem, free deployment on Vercel/Netlify
- Total MVP deployment cost on Base mainnet: less than $10

- Accuracy claims above 93%

- Unimplemented integrations (e.g., native Coinbase Smart Wallet, full ERC-4337 AA, etc.)

1. Short version (1 paragraph, ~100 words)
2. Long version (max 350 words) with the subheadings “How It Works” and “Why Base”

generation-snake.title: Generation Snake
generation-snake.prompt:
2048 is a simple yet irresistibly addictive puzzle game played on a clean 4×4 grid. Numbered tiles slide around the board using four arrow buttons positioned just below the grid — arranged just like the arrow keys on a keyboard.

When the game begins, two tiles with a value of either 2 or 4 appear in random spots. After every move, a new tile pops into an empty space — 90% of the time it’s a 2, and 10% of the time it’s a 4, so plan your strategy wisely!

Tiles glide as far as they can in the direction you choose, stopping only when they hit another tile or the edge of the board. When two tiles with the same value collide, they merge into one stronger tile worth their combined total. Keep in mind: a freshly merged tile can’t merge again during the same move.

Special cases add to the challenge:

If three identical tiles line up, only the two farthest along the direction of movement will merge.

If a full row or column contains four tiles of the same value, sliding parallel to that line merges the first two and the last two.

A scoreboard in the upper-right tracks your current score, calculated by adding up the values of all tiles on the board.

Your mission? Create the legendary 2048 tile! Achieve it and you win — but you can keep going to chase even higher numbers. The game ends only when the board has no empty spaces left and no adjacent tiles can merge.

Once the game is over, you’ll be able to share your score with others.

And best of all, the 2048 game will be waiting for players right on the home page.

getr.prompt:
Plan for the "Getr" Discount Coupon Exchange App
1. Project Overview

Name: Getr

Purpose: A mobile app that allows users to exchange, share, and redeem discount coupons from various retailers.

Target Audience: Shoppers, bargain hunters, and users who regularly use coupons for savings.

Platforms: Android, iOS

Main Features:

User registration & profile management

Coupon exchange & sharing

Coupon discovery (Browse coupons by store, category, etc.)

Coupon scanning (QR/barcode)

Push notifications for new coupons and offers

Coupon expiration tracking

Social media integration (for sharing coupons with friends)

2. Core Features

User Registration and Login:

Sign up using email, Google, or social media accounts.

User profile (name, email, coupon history).

Security (password recovery, 2FA, etc.)

Coupon Exchange:

Users can upload their own discount coupons (image or code).

Share coupons with friends via in-app chat, email, or social media.

A marketplace to search and browse available coupons by category, store, or popularity.

Coupon Discovery:

Searchable listings of coupons by retailer, category (fashion, groceries, electronics, etc.), or location.

Filter coupons by expiration date, type (percentage off, free shipping, etc.), or popularity.

QR/Barcode Scanning:

Ability to scan coupons directly from other sources (physical coupons, online images, etc.) and store them in the app.

Expiration Management:

Notifications when a coupon is about to expire.

Option to set reminders or save coupons for later use.

Rating & Reviews:

Users can rate and review the coupons they’ve used.

Feedback on the reliability and ease of use of coupons.

Push Notifications:

Alerts about new coupons, expiring coupons, and special promotions.

3. Technical Specifications

Frontend:

Mobile App (UI/UX): Intuitive and user-friendly design with easy navigation.

Libraries for image uploading and scanning (Camera API, QR Code Scanning).

Set up tech stack and choose development tools.

Develop API for managing coupon uploads, searches, and exchanges.

Build mobile app for both Android and iOS.

Implement UI/UX designs.

Integrate QR code scanner and coupon upload feature.

Add push notification functionality.

Conduct extensive testing (unit, integration, UI/UX testing).

Beta testing with a small group of users.

Launch the app on the App Store and Google Play Store.

Monitor user feedback, fix bugs, and add new features.

Regular updates with new coupon sources and improved UI.

Ad Revenue: Displaying ads in the app (banner, interstitial).

Premium Accounts: Offering a subscription for extra features (e.g., no ads, early access to coupons, exclusive coupons).

Affiliate Links: Earning commissions when users redeem coupons that come from affiliate retailers.

Transaction Fees: Charging a small fee for users who exchange coupons for credits or purchase exclusive offers.

Technical Specification (TS) – Creativity Quest App
1. Project Overview

The Creativity Quest App gamifies creative exercises. Users complete quests in areas like writing, drawing, photography, DIY, or music. The app tracks progress, rewards achievements, and encourages daily creative activity.

Goal: Boost creativity through gamified daily challenges, progress tracking, and social interaction.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Quest Generation

Generate quests in multiple creative categories:

Writing (story prompts, poetry)

Drawing/Sketching

Photography

DIY / Crafts

Music or sound design

Quests can be:

Daily random quests

Category-specific quests

Difficulty-based quests (Easy, Medium, Hard)

2.2 Quest Completion

Users mark quests as:

Completed

Skipped

In progress

Optional: upload notes, images, or audio for proof of completion.

Track streaks of consecutive days with completed quests.

2.3 Rewards & Gamification

Points for completed quests.

Badges for streaks, difficulty levels, or category mastery.

Leaderboard (optional) for comparing points with friends.

Progress bar for each creative category.

2.4 User Interface

Dashboard: shows today’s quests, streaks, and total points.

Quest Feed: scrollable list of available quests.

Quest Detail Page: description, category, difficulty, and completion options.

Profile: achievements, badges, completed quests, points, and stats.

Light/Dark Mode and customizable themes.

2.5 Notifications & Reminders

Daily quest notifications.

Reminders for incomplete quests.

Optional motivational messages.

2.6 Search & Filtering

Search quests by category, difficulty, or keyword.

Filter completed vs. pending quests.

2.7 Social & Sharing (Optional)

Share completed quests or creations with friends or public feed.

Commenting or feedback system for shared content.

Invite friends to participate in challenges.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile: iOS & Android

Optional: web version

3.2 Performance

Quest generation <1 second.

Smooth navigation and responsive UI (<100ms per tap).

3.3 Data Storage

Local database for offline use (SQLite, Realm, Hive).

Optional cloud sync for multi-device access.

3.4 Security

Protect user content and data (encryption if using cloud).

Optional authentication: passcode, fingerprint, or face ID.

3.5 Usability

Minimal taps to start a quest (<3 taps).

Intuitive design for quick daily engagement.

Accessible fonts and color schemes.

4. Technical Stack
Mobile

Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local DB: SQLite, Realm, Hive

Notifications: native push/local

Optional AI integration for personalized quest suggestions

Web (Optional)

Frontend: React or Vue.js

Backend: Node.js or Django

Database: PostgreSQL or MongoDB

5. Future Enhancements

AI-powered personalized quest generator based on past activity.

Collaborative quests with friends.

Seasonal challenges and events.

Integration with note-taking, photo, or drawing apps.

Export completed quests and creations as PDF or media files.

gogo.prompt: Coin Rush 2048 is a simple but addictive puzzle game played on a 4×4 grid. Each turn, a new tile with the value 2 or 4 appears in an empty cell. You can slide all tiles up, down, left, or right using the onscreen arrow buttons. When two tiles with the same number crash into each other, they merge into a single tile whose value is the sum of both tiles. Your goal is to keep combining tiles to create bigger and bigger numbers, eventually reaching the legendary 2048 tile or even higher. Every move must be chosen carefully, because if the grid fills up and no more moves are possible, the game ends. Smart planning, quick thinking, and a bit of luck are needed to survive. Chase a new high score, challenge your friends, and see how long you can keep the board alive in Coin Rush 2048!

hedas.prompt:
Project Plan for Creating the Mini Application “Hedas”
1. Project Overview

Hedas is a mini web-application that enables users to upload, share, and download essays. The platform aims to simplify academic exchange, improve access to study materials, and support collaborative learning.

2. Goals and Objectives

Provide a simple interface for uploading and downloading essays.

Enable user registration and authentication.

Implement search and filtering by subject, author, and keywords.

Allow users to rate or comment on shared essays (optional).

Ensure secure file storage and protection from plagiarism or spam.

3. Core Features
3.1 User Features

User registration and login

Profile page with uploaded essays

Essay upload (PDF, DOCX)

Essay browsing and downloading

Search by title, subject, tags

Optional: comments, ratings, favorites

3.2 Admin Features

Approve or reject uploaded essays

Manage users

Delete inappropriate content

Statistics dashboard (optional)

4. Technical Stack
Frontend

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript

Framework: React or Vue (optional)

Backend

Node.js (Express) or Python (Django/FastAPI)

Database

MongoDB or PostgreSQL

Storage

Local storage or cloud storage (e.g., AWS S3, Firebase Storage)

5. System Architecture

Client (Browser) – UI for interaction

Backend API – processes requests, manages authentication

Database – stores users, essay metadata

File Storage – stores actual essay files

6. Development Stages
Stage 1: Planning & Design

Define feature list

Create wireframes and user flow

Prepare database schema

Stage 2: Backend Development

Set up server and API routes

Implement user authentication

Implement file upload and download endpoints

Create essay metadata storage

Stage 3: Frontend Development

Build UI components (upload form, list of essays, profile page)

Connect frontend to backend

Add search functionality

Stage 4: Testing

Unit tests for backend functions

UI testing for form submissions

File upload/download reliability tests

Stage 5: Deployment

Deploy backend (e.g., Render, Vercel, AWS)

Deploy frontend (e.g., Netlify, Vercel)

Set up SSL and environment variables

7. Security Considerations

JWT authentication

File type validation

Size limits for uploaded files

Database access restrictions

Protection against XSS and SQL injection

8. Future Improvements

AI-based essay similarity checker

Private sharing links

Essay translation tool

User badges and gamification

Remiit is a Web3 Telegram mini-app that lets Nigerians in UK, US, Canada, Germany, etc. send money home instantly at real black-market rates with almost zero fees — receiver gets full Naira in Opay, Palmpay or any bank in under 30 seconds.”

1. You open the mini-app inside Telegram (no download)  
2. Connect your wallet (Trust Wallet, Phantom, etc.)  
3. Type how much dollars/pounds you want to send  
4. The app shows exactly how much Naira your person in Nigeria will receive (today e.g. $500 → ₦960,000 at ₦1,920/$ parallel market rate)  
5. You pay with USDT (gas fee less than 20 kobo)  
6. Your mum/sibling/friend in Nigeria gets the Naira instantly in their normal bank app — they don’t need crypto or wallet.

- Beats Western Union/Wise by ₦100,000–₦300,000 on every $1,000 sent  
- Truly instant (not “2–5 business days”)  
- No ridiculous bank forms or “reason for transfer” stress  
- Shareable receipt so everyone sees how much you saved

4. Support different pool weights (e.g., Balancer 80/20 pools).
5. Mobile-friendly design for quick checks on the go.

inayah.title: Inayah
inayah.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

AI-powered learning companion offering hints, summaries, and gentle explanations.

Progress timeline and milestones that focus on growth, not perfection.

Soft reminders based on user mood and energy levels.

Daily motivations, gratitude prompts, and small challenges.

AI suggestions for improving routines in a gentle, caring way.

Reflection journal for emotional check-ins.

Supportive micro-groups for shared learning goals.

Positivity-based chat spaces (no negativity, no comparison).

Daily “kindness tasks” to encourage helpful interactions.

Anonymous “support messages” you can send or receive on difficult days.

Calming breathing exercises or mini-meditations before studying.

Encouraging affirmations tailored to user progress.

Cross-platform (iOS, Android, Web).

Cloud sync for progress and saved learning paths.

Local encrypted storage for private journal entries.

AI-based personalization engine.

Soft pastel palette or soothing dark mode.

Rounded edges, gentle animations, and a cozy design.

Interface that feels welcoming and calm.

Peer study rooms

Shared habit challenges

AI-coach with a caring personality

In-app mini-courses created collaboratively by users

A single app that teaches you, motivates you, and supports you emotionally — combining learning, habits, and human warmth in one gentle ecosystem.

jedu.prompt:
Jedu — Mini App Development Plan
1. Concept Overview

Jedu is a mini-application that enables users to share, exchange, or donate surplus food items within their local community. The goal is to reduce food waste and promote sustainable consumption.

2. Core Features
2.1 User Registration & Profiles

Email/phone registration or social login

Basic profile: name, location, avatar

User rating and reviews

2.2 Product Listings

Add a food item (title, description, expiration date, photos)

Set availability (pickup location, time)

Categorization: fruits, vegetables, bakery, packaged goods, etc.

2.3 Search & Filters

Search by product name

Filters: category, distance, freshness, availability

Map view for nearby items

2.4 Exchange & Messaging

In-app chat to arrange exchange or pickup

Notifications for messages and updates

“Request item” button

2.5 Community & Safety

Reporting system for inappropriate content

Verified users/tagging

Food safety guidelines

2.6 Additional Features (Optional)

Gamification (points for giving away food)

Wishlist for desired items

Push notifications for nearby new items

3. Technology Stack
3.1 Frontend

React Native or Flutter (for mobile app)

Alternatively: Web app with React or Vue

3.2 Backend

Node.js (Express/NestJS) or Python (Django/FastAPI)

Database: PostgreSQL or MongoDB

Cloud storage for images: AWS S3, Firebase Storage, or Cloudinary

3.3 Infrastructure

Hosting: AWS / Google Cloud / Render

Authentication: Firebase Auth or custom JWT

Map API: Google Maps API or OpenStreetMap

4. UI/UX Design
4.1 Design Principles

Minimalistic and friendly

Focus on photos and quick actions

Emphasis on local community connection

4.2 Screens

Login / Signup

Home (list + map view)

Create Listing

Messaging

User Profile

Item Details

Settings

5. Development Stages
Stage 1: Planning & Prototyping

Research user needs

Create wireframes

Define technical specifications

Stage 2: MVP Development

Implement core features: registration, listing, search, chat

Build a simple backend

Deploy early version for testing

Stage 3: Testing

Functional testing

User experience testing

Fix bugs and optimize performance

Stage 4: Launch

Upload to app stores (if mobile)

Promote within communities

Gather first user feedback

Stage 5: Improvements

Add optional features

Improve UI/UX

Introduce gamification and community features

6. Team Requirements

1–2 Frontend developers

1 Backend developer

1 UI/UX designer

QA tester

Project manager (optional)

7. Timeline Estimate

Planning & Design: 2–3 weeks

MVP Development: 6–8 weeks

Testing & Polishing: 2–3 weeks

Launch: 1 week

Total: ~10–14 weeks

Smooth animations and responsive jump.

Fast-paced but easy to learn.

Retro arcade sound effects.
