kopmaster.title: Kopmaster
kopmaster.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

Krespo Mini-App Development Plan
1. Project Overview

Krespo is a mini-application designed to allow users to exchange, give away, or request accessories and jewelry within a community. The app focuses on sustainability, community interaction, and easy peer-to-peer swapping.

2. Core Objectives

Enable users to list accessories/jewelry for exchange.

Allow users to browse available items.

Provide a secure matching and messaging system.

Promote sustainable fashion via reuse and exchange.

3. Key Features
3.1 User Features

User Registration & Login (email/phone/social login)

Profile Page: avatar, bio, location, preferred styles

Item Listing: upload photos, add description, category, condition, desired swap

Search & Filters: by category, condition, distance, style

Exchange Requests: send/receive swap proposals

Built-in Chat for negotiation and arranging exchange

Favorites: save items to wishlist

Ratings & Reviews after completing a swap

3.2 Admin Features

User management

Content moderation (images, reports)

Analytics dashboard (active users, number of exchanges)

4. Technology Stack
4.1 Frontend

React / React Native / Flutter (mobile app)

Responsive UI optimized for simple navigation

4.2 Backend

Node.js / Express or Python / Django

REST or GraphQL API

Cloud storage for images

4.3 Database

MongoDB or PostgreSQL

User profiles, item listings, messages, reviews

4.4 Additional Services

Cloud hosting (AWS / Firebase / DigitalOcean)

Push notifications (Firebase)

Image moderation (AI or custom review)

5. User Flow

User registers or logs in

Views home feed with new items

Lists an item for exchange

Browses and selects an item they want

Sends an exchange proposal

Users chat to confirm swap

Exchange completed

Users rate each other

6. UI/UX Structure
Main Screens:

Welcome / Login

Home Feed

Item Details

Add Item

Chat

User Profile

Settings

Style: clean, minimalistic, pastel tones reflecting jewelry aesthetics.

Phase 1 — Discovery & Design (1–2 weeks)

Market research

Wireframes & UI mockups

Define MVP scope

Phase 2 — Development (4–6 weeks)

Build frontend and backend

Implement database

Implement messaging system

Item listing + filters

Phase 3 — Testing (1–2 weeks)

Functional testing

Fix bugs

Optimize performance

Phase 4 — Launch

Deployment to hosting

Beta testing

Public release

Collect feedback

Add new features (e.g., swap events, geolocation, premium badges)

Premium profiles

Featured item listings

In-app ads (minimal)

Small fees for verified members

Referral bonuses

laubig.title: Laubig
laubig.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Temporal Historian: Interactive History Explorer
1. Project Overview

Temporal Historian lets users explore history like a living, interactive world. Instead of static dates and events, history “breathes”: battles unfold, inventions appear, and personalities interact. Users can explore timelines, alter minor “what-if” scenarios, and collect historical artifacts.

Purpose: Make history interactive, immersive, and exploratory — blending education, storytelling, and gamification.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Interactive Timelines

Explore history via dynamic timelines by region, civilization, or theme.

Tap on events to see expanded details: descriptions, images, documents, and reconstructed maps.

Zoom in/out to see daily, yearly, or century-level views.

2.2 “What-If” Scenario Simulation

Users can tweak minor historical events and see speculative consequences.

AI generates narrative branches based on user changes (e.g., “If a battle had ended differently…”).

Compare alternative timelines side by side.

2.3 Artifact & Document Collection

Unlock digital artifacts (maps, letters, inventions, portraits) by exploring events.

View artifacts in high resolution; optional AR mode to place objects in the real world.

Save artifacts to personal “historical museum.”

2.4 Search & Exploration

Search by keyword, date, location, or historical figure.

Filter events by theme: Wars, Culture, Science, Politics, Discoveries.

Interactive maps showing events across regions.

2.5 Notifications & Daily Exploration

Daily historical fact or “temporal challenge”: explore a random event or artifact.

Alerts when new “artifact unlocks” or timeline expansions are available.

2.6 User Profiles & Gamification

Track completed explorations, unlocked artifacts, and “historical achievements.”

Leaderboards for exploration streaks or artifact collections (optional social mode).

Badges for mastering civilizations, timelines, or historical themes.

3. Non-Functional Requirements

Platform: iOS & Android; optional web interface.

Performance: Smooth scrolling through timelines; event expansion <1s.

UI: Immersive, visually rich; interactive maps and timeline animations.

let-it-grow.title: Let It Grow
let-it-grow.prompt:
App Concept: Let-it-grow
Name: Let-it-growCore
Purpose: A productivity and well-being app that uses the gamified metaphor of growing a virtual garden to track and motivate users in achieving personal goals, completing tasks, and building positive habits.1. Target AudienceThe app is designed for individuals who:Struggle with procrastination and maintaining consistency in daily habits.Are interested in personal growth, habit tracking, and goal setting.Enjoy gamified experiences and visual feedback on their progress.Need a gentle, positive reminder system to stay on track.2. Key FeaturesA. The Virtual Garden (The Core Metaphor)Plant-Based Progress: Every task or habit the user sets is linked to a virtual plant (e.g., a sapling for a long-term goal, a small flower for a daily habit).Watering/Growth Mechanism: When the user successfully checks off a task or habit for the day, their linked plant receives "water" (progress points) and grows slightly.Failure States: If a user misses a habit or fails to log progress, the linked plant visually wilts, but does not permanently die, encouraging them to return and revive it.Visual Rewards: As the user maintains consistency, their garden expands, new decorative items unlock, and their plants mature from seedlings to full-grown flora.B. Habit TrackerDaily, Weekly, and Monthly Cycles: Users can set habits (e.g., "Read for 30 minutes," "Exercise," "Meditate") and assign them specific frequencies.Streak Tracking: Detailed statistics on current and longest streaks to maintain motivation.Goal Linking: Link multiple related habits to a larger "Goal Plant" to show how small actions contribute to the big picture.C. Goal Setter (The Long-Term Crop)Project-based Goals: For larger, multi-step goals (e.g., "Finish Book Draft," "Learn Spanish Basics"), the goal is represented by a large, slow-growing tree.Milestone Breakdown: Users define milestones, and checking off a milestone provides a significant growth boost to the tree.Time Tracking Integration: Optional integration for logging focused work time (e.g., using a Pomodoro timer) that adds progress to the current active goal.D. Customization & AestheticsSeed Shop: Users earn in-app currency (e.g., "Dewdrops") by completing tasks, which they can use to unlock new types of plants, unique terrains, and decorative items for their garden (fences, fountains, garden gnomes).Environmental Themes: Switch the garden setting (e.g., from a lush forest to a desert oasis) to keep the environment feeling fresh.3. Technology Stack RecommendationGiven the need for real-time visual updates and persistent user data:Frontend (UI/UX): React or Angular (using a single file structure). The visuals would benefit from a canvas-based rendering library (like basic Canvas API or Three.js for a more sophisticated 3D look) for the garden environment.Database: Google Firestore for real-time synchronization of user progress, garden state, and habit data.API: Gemini API could be integrated to provide motivational messages or offer smart, personalized suggestions for new habits based on user patterns (e.g., "You tend to finish your tasks before 10 AM, try adding a morning meditation habit!").

Idea: A tool that estimates potential "Liquidation Heatmaps" based on Open Interest data.
User Goal: Predict where price might bounce due to forced liquidations of over-leveraged traders.

* Visualize "clusters" of potential long/short liquidations.
* Logic based on: Entry Price + Leverage assumptions (e.g., 25x, 50x, 100x).

4. Update in near real-time.
5. Note: Accurate liquidation data is hard to get; this would be an estimator tool.

lokas.title: Lokas
lokas.prompt:
Plan for Creating the Mini-App: Lokas (Auto Parts Exchange)
1. Project Overview

Name of the App: Lokas
Purpose: A platform for users to exchange, buy, or sell auto parts in their local area. The app will focus on connecting people looking for specific car parts and those selling them. Users will be able to browse parts, contact sellers, and arrange transactions directly through the app.

2. Core Features
User Authentication

Sign Up / Login: Secure sign-up and login via email, social media (Facebook, Google), or phone number verification.

Profile Management: Ability for users to manage their profiles, including contact information, car models, and parts they wish to sell or are looking for.

Part Listings

Part Listings (Buy/Sell): Users can list auto parts for sale or search for parts they need.

Part Categories: Clear categories for different types of auto parts (engine, transmission, wheels, body parts, etc.).

Search Filters: Advanced search with filters by part type, car model, location, condition (new or used), price range, etc.

Images & Descriptions: Users should be able to upload photos and detailed descriptions of the parts.

Transaction Management

Contacting Sellers: Built-in messaging system to contact sellers and negotiate prices.

Price Negotiation: A platform for buyers and sellers to discuss prices and finalize deals.

Payment Integration: Optional in-app payment integration (Stripe, PayPal) for secure transactions or in-app chat to arrange offline payments.

Ratings/Reviews: A review and rating system for buyers and sellers based on transaction experiences.

Location-Based Features

Geolocation: Display nearby sellers based on the user's current location.

Map Integration: Show nearby sellers on a map, allowing users to find parts in their area.

Notifications

Alerts: Push notifications for new parts that match the user’s search criteria or when a price changes.

Transaction Updates: Notify users when a buyer or seller has responded to an inquiry or when a deal has been closed.

Admin Panel

User Management: Admins can view and manage users (ban users, handle complaints).

Content Moderation: Ability to review listings for inappropriate content.

Transaction Oversight: Track the success and failure of transactions for insights.

3. User Flow

Welcome Screen: Options to log in or sign up.

Home Page: Browse or search auto parts (using filters).

Product Page: Detailed view of a specific auto part, with an option to contact the seller.

Messaging: A simple interface for messaging between buyers and sellers.

Payment: Payment screen if an in-app transaction system is implemented.

Confirmation: Confirmation screen after a successful purchase or sale.

4. Technology Stack

Frontend:

React Native (for mobile app on iOS and Android).

UI Design: Figma/Adobe XD for wireframes and visual design.

Components: Material-UI or Tailwind CSS for frontend design elements.

Backend:

Node.js with Express for the backend server.

Database: MongoDB (for flexible data storage of user profiles, part listings, etc.).

Authentication: Firebase Authentication or OAuth for user login.

Payment Gateway: Stripe or PayPal integration for secure payments (optional based on user needs).

Geolocation: Google Maps API for location-based features.

Notifications: Firebase Cloud Messaging for push notifications.

5. Development Roadmap
Phase 1: Research and Design

Market Research: Analyze competitors, user needs, and features that will set Lokas apart.

Wireframing: Design the initial wireframes for the app’s layout.

UI/UX Design: Create the final UI designs and user flows.

Phase 2: Development

Backend Setup: Develop the server-side functionality, database schema, and user authentication system.

Frontend Development: Build the mobile app using React Native, integrating UI components.

Geolocation and Map Features: Implement location services and map features to help users find nearby parts.

Phase 3: Testing

Beta Testing: Test the app with a small group of users and gather feedback.

Bug Fixing: Identify and fix bugs or issues from user feedback.

Phase 4: Launch

App Store Deployment: Deploy the app on Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

Marketing: Launch marketing campaigns to promote the app (social media, car enthusiast groups, etc.).

Phase 5: Post-Launch & Updates

User Feedback: Gather user feedback for continuous improvement.

manic.prompt:
1. Project Overview

NailPro is a mobile and web application designed for nail salon management and client engagement. The app provides booking, service selection, staff management, payment, and loyalty features. It has two modes:

Client Mode – to browse services, book appointments, view portfolios, and pay.

Staff/Salon Mode – to manage appointments, track clients, record services, and handle inventory.

2. Objectives

Simplify appointment booking for clients.

Help staff manage schedules efficiently.

Track client preferences and service history.

Streamline payment and loyalty programs.

Provide analytics for salon performance.

3. Core Features
3.1 Client Mode

Service Catalog

List of services (manicure, pedicure, nail art, gel, acrylic, etc.)

Price and duration

Staff availability per service

Booking & Scheduling

Select date, time, and preferred staff

Appointment confirmation via push notification

Calendar sync

Portfolio & Inspiration

Photo gallery of styles

Save favorite designs

Share images on social media

Payments

In-app payments (credit card, digital wallets)

Tips for staff

Receipts and invoices

Loyalty & Promotions

Points system

Discounts and offers

Referral rewards

Reviews & Feedback

Rate staff and services

Leave comments

3.2 Staff / Salon Mode

Appointment Management

Daily/weekly/monthly calendar view

Accept or reject bookings

Reschedule requests

Client Profiles

Service history

Allergies or preferences

Notes and reminders

Inventory Management

Track nail products, polish, tools, gels

Low-stock alerts

Supplier management

Analytics & Reports

Revenue by day/week/month

Most popular services

Staff performance metrics

Staff Communication

Internal chat

Notifications for schedule changes

Task reminders

4. Platform Requirements

Mobile: iOS 13+, Android 9+

Web: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge

Tech Stack:

Frontend: Flutter (mobile), React (web)

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / Firebase

Payment Integration: Stripe / PayPal

5. UI/UX Requirements

Client Mode:

Colorful, stylish, easy-to-navigate

Quick booking buttons

Portfolio gallery with swipe navigation

Staff Mode:

Dashboard with appointments and tasks

Notifications for upcoming appointments

Inventory and client management panels

Dark and light modes for different lighting in salons

Offline mode for booking sync in case of internet interruptions

6. Database Architecture (ERD Description)

Main Entities:

Users (Client / Staff / Admin)

Services

Appointments

Clients

Inventory

Payments

Reviews

Table Examples:

Users: id, name, email, role, password_hash, created_at

Services: id, name, description, duration, price, staff_id

Appointments: id, client_id, staff_id, service_id, date_time, status

Clients: id, name, contact_info, preferences, allergies

Inventory: id, product_name, quantity, threshold_alert, supplier

Payments: id, appointment_id, amount, payment_method, status

Reviews: id, client_id, staff_id, rating, comment, date

7. Agile User Stories
Client Stories

As a client, I want to book an appointment online so that I don’t need to call.

As a client, I want to view a gallery of nail designs so that I can choose a style.

As a client, I want to pay in the app to save time at checkout.

Staff Stories

As a staff member, I want to view my daily appointments so that I can manage my schedule.

As a staff member, I want to track client preferences so that I provide personalized service.

As a staff member, I want to monitor inventory to avoid running out of supplies.

8. Security Requirements

Role-based access (Client / Staff / Admin)

Encrypted data storage (AES-256)

Secure payment gateway integration

GDPR/CCPA compliance for client data

9. Performance Requirements

App load time ≤ 2 seconds

Booking confirmation ≤ 1 second

Payment processing ≤ 2 seconds

Smooth gallery and calendar navigation

10. Monetization Model

Free for clients to browse and book

Salon subscription for advanced features (inventory, analytics, multi-staff support)

Premium add-ons: loyalty program, promotions, marketing notifications

11. KPIs

Number of bookings per day/week/month

Client retention rate

Average appointment value

Staff utilization

Inventory usage efficiency

manual-roi-tracker.title: Manual Roi Tracker
manual-roi-tracker.prompt:
Manual ROI Tracker — готовий опис для Mini App Factory

Title: Manual ROI Tracker

Description:
Create a simple app where users can manually calculate their ROI (Return on Investment). The app should not use the internet or external data sources. All values are entered manually by the user.

Functionality:
 • The app shows two input fields:
 1. “Initial Investment”
 2. “Current Value”
 • When the user enters numbers and clicks a button labeled “Calculate ROI”, the app calculates:
ROI % = ((Current Value – Initial Investment) / Initial Investment) × 100
 • Display the result in a clear text area labeled “Your ROI:”
 • Include basic error handling:
 • If fields are empty or contain invalid input, show a simple message like “Please enter valid numbers.”
 • Add a small reset button labeled “Clear” to reset both inputs and the result.
 • No external libraries, no API, no Web3. The app is fully local.

UI Requirements:
 • Clean layout with straightforward labels.
 • Use simple elements only: text fields, labels, buttons, and a result box.
 • Ensure the calculation works instantly after pressing the button.

market-mood-log.title: Market Mood Log
market-mood-log.prompt:
Market Mood Log — App Description

Create a simple mini app called “Market Mood Log”.
The app allows users to manually record their perception of the market’s mood each day.
No external data, no internet access, and no Web3 integrations are needed.

Core Features
 1. A date picker (or automatic “Today” date if available).
 2. A dropdown menu with mood options, such as:
 • Bullish
 • Neutral
 • Bearish
 3. A text input field for optional notes (e.g., “High volume”, “FOMC week”, “Strong breakout”, etc.).
 4. A button “Add Entry” that saves the mood entry to a visible list.

Log List Features

Each entry in the list should display:
 • Date
 • Selected mood
 • Notes (optional)

Each list item must include:
 • An “Edit Entry” button to update the date, mood, or notes
 • A “Delete” button to remove the entry

How the App Should Work
 • User selects a date, chooses a mood, and optionally types notes.
 • Presses “Add Entry” to log the mood.
 • The entry appears in the list below.
 • User can edit or delete entries anytime.
 • All information is stored inside the app session with no external calls.

UI Requirements
 • Clean, simple layout.
 • Inputs at the top, entries displayed below in table or card format.
 • Buttons must be clearly visible and easy to understand.
 • No external dependencies, APIs, or web3 actions.

Goal of the App

Give users a simple offline tool to track and review how the crypto market felt to them day by day.

max.title: Max
max.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

memes.title: Memes
memes.prompt:
Sure! Here's a plan for creating a meme-sharing mini app called Memes:

1. App Overview

Name: Memes

Purpose: A simple app for users to share, browse, and react to memes in a fun and engaging way.

Platform: iOS/Android (or both)

Target Audience: Young adults, meme enthusiasts, social media users, people who love humor and pop culture.

2. Core Features

Meme Feed:

Description: Display a scrolling feed of popular memes.

Features:

Infinite scroll to load more memes.

Ability to like and comment on memes.

Option to filter memes by categories (e.g., "Funny," "Trending," "Animals," "Relatable," etc.).

Meme Upload:

Description: Allow users to upload their own memes.

Features:

Upload images or GIFs.

Add a caption or text to the meme.

Option to add relevant tags (e.g., "funny," "reaction," "viral").

Option to upload directly from the camera or gallery.

Meme Search:

Description: Enable users to search for memes by keywords or tags.

Features:

Search bar with auto-suggestions based on popular tags or meme names.

Filter search results based on categories.

User Profiles:

Description: Each user can have their own profile to showcase their uploaded memes and reactions.

Features:

Display uploaded memes, liked memes, and comments.

Basic user settings (name, avatar, bio).

Follow/Unfollow other users.

Reactions & Comments:

Description: Allow users to interact with memes through reactions and comments.

Features:

Users can "like" memes or use reaction emojis (laugh, love, surprise, etc.).

Comment section to add thoughts or share opinions on memes.

Meme Sharing:

Description: Allow users to share memes externally to social media or via messaging.

Features:

Share via direct links or social media platforms (Instagram, Twitter, etc.).

Option to download memes for offline sharing.

Push Notifications:

Description: Notify users about new memes, popular uploads, and reactions to their content.

Features:

Notifications for new comments, likes, or follows.

Notifications for trending memes or new memes based on user preferences.

3. User Flow

Sign Up/Login: Users can create an account or log in via social media accounts (Google, Facebook, etc.).

Home Feed: After login, users are taken to the home feed of memes.

Interaction: Users can like, comment, share, or upload their own meme.

Profile: Users can view and edit their profile from the settings section.

Search: Tap on the search bar to find specific memes or browse categories.

Settings: Adjust notifications, account preferences, and other settings.

4. Design & User Interface (UI)

Minimalist & Fun Design: The app should have a playful, visually appealing design. It should be easy to navigate with a focus on images.

Bright colors for buttons.

Clear icons for interaction (like, comment, share, etc.).

Large thumbnails for memes.

Navigation:

Bottom navigation bar with tabs: Home, Upload, Search, Profile, Settings.

Clear CTAs (call-to-action buttons) for uploading memes, liking, and sharing.

5. Technical Requirements

Platform: Flutter/React Native for cross-platform support (iOS and Android).

Backend: Firebase/Node.js with a cloud database (e.g., Firestore or MongoDB) for storing memes, user data, and comments.

Image Hosting: Use cloud services (e.g., AWS S3 or Firebase Storage) to store uploaded meme images.

Push Notifications: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for push notifications.

Authentication: Firebase Authentication or OAuth for user login.

6. Monetization Strategy

Ad Revenue: Display ads within the app, such as banner ads or interstitial ads.

Premium Features:

Ad-free experience: Offer a paid subscription to remove ads.

Exclusive Memes: Create a "premium" section where only paid users can access certain content.

In-App Purchases:

Customization of profiles (premium avatars, memes, etc.).

Special effects for memes or reactions (GIF stickers, filters).

7. Marketing & Growth Strategy

Social Media Integration:

Promote user-generated memes on popular social media platforms (Instagram, Twitter, etc.).

Leverage influencers and meme creators to showcase the app.

Referral Program: Reward users for referring friends to the app (e.g., free premium features for every referral).

Viral Features: Make sure the app is shareable, allowing users to easily spread memes to their networks. Encourage memes that could go viral.

Partnerships: Collaborate with meme pages or influencers for in-app campaigns or special meme events.

8. Testing & Launch Plan

Beta Testing:

Conduct closed beta testing with a small group of users to gather feedback.

Collect data on user engagement, feature usability, and bug reports.

Launch:

Launch the app on both iOS and Android platforms.

Promote on social media and through influencers for initial user acquisition.

Post-Launch:

Monitor performance and user feedback.

Release periodic updates based on user requests and bug fixes.

9. Post-Launch Features (Future Updates)

Meme Editing Tools: Add simple meme creation tools (e.g., add text, filters, stickers, etc.).

Trending Section: Show trending memes based on user interactions.

Meme Challenges: Users can participate in themed meme challenges, with rewards or recognition for the best memes.

mental-healt-app.title: Mental Healt App
mental-healt-app.prompt:
Empathic MindCheck is a mini-app dedicated to mental well-being, designed to offer a safe, welcoming, and non-judgmental space where users can explore their feelings.
Through targeted questions, empathetic language, and intuitive tools, the app helps users better understand their emotional state and develop greater awareness of their psychological balance.

The mini-app guides users through short emotional check-ins that assess mood, stress, anxiety, energy, sleep, and need for support. Each interaction is designed to be gentle, reassuring, and respectful: users are free to respond as they wish or skip questions, always maintaining full control of their data.

After each check-in, the app offers personalized feedback, small self-care suggestions (such as breathing exercises or guided micro-reflections), and the option to record thoughts or emotions in a short integrated journal.

Empathic MindCheck is not intended to replace a mental health professional, but offers a simple and human tool to:

reconnect with your emotions

identify patterns of stress or anxiety

find helpful resources in difficult times

track your well-being over time

metaks.title: Metaks
metaks.prompt:
**Technical Specification (TS)

Gen Z-Oriented Mobile Application: “VibeSync”**

1. Project Overview

VibeSync is a mobile application designed for Generation Z users (ages 12–27).
The app combines short-form content creation, event discovery, micro-communities, and AI-powered personalization.
Primary purpose: help Gen Z connect through shared interests while maintaining privacy, authenticity, and low social pressure.

2. Key Objectives

Provide a safe, inclusive digital space for interest-based communication.

Reduce social pressure compared to traditional social media.

Use AI to personalize content recommendations and simplify content creation.

Enable hybrid online/offline interaction through events and micro-communities.

Support fast, lightweight engagement suitable for short attention spans.

3. Core Features
3.1 User Profiles

Minimalist profiles: nickname, avatar, interest tags.

Optional bio (max 120 characters).

Privacy modes: Public / Friends Only / Anonymous.

3.2 AI-Assisted Micro-Content

Short video clips (≤15 sec).

AI auto-editing: filters, captions, background music.

Mood-based templates (e.g., “happy”, “study”, “gym”, “aesthetic”).

Voice-to-text and auto-subtitles.

3.3 Interest-Based Micro-Communities (“Hubs”)

Users can join hubs: e.g., “Anime”, “Studying”, “Skincare”, “Tech”, “Aesthetic Fashion”.

Inside each hub:

Chat threads

Micro-events

Content feeds

Collaborations

3.4 Event Discovery

Nearby events: study meetups, art events, gaming nights.

Virtual sessions: livestream classes, music rooms, co-study spaces.

Event filtering by interests and distance.

3.5 AI Recommendation Engine

Suggests:

Communities to join

Events to attend

Users with similar interests

Uses:

Interaction history

Content preferences

Mood tags

3.6 Messaging System

1-to-1 messaging with ephemeral mode (optional deletion after 24 hours).

Group chats within hubs.

Reactions, GIFs, stickers.

mind-game.title: Mind Game
mind-game.prompt:
Create a “GemSlide Fusion” Game on the Home Page

Build a puzzle game called GemSlide Fusion, played on a 5×5 grid. Instead of numbers, each tile represents a gem with a color and tier. The player moves tiles using four on-screen arrow buttons (Up, Down, Left, Right), arranged directly below the grid in a typical keyboard arrow-key layout.

Gameplay Mechanics

The game starts with three random gem tiles on the board.
After every move, one new gem spawns in a random empty tile.

Gems have tiers instead of numbers:

Tier 1 (Common)
Tier 2 (Uncommon)
Tier 3 (Rare)
Tier 4 (Epic)
Tier 5 (Legendary)

Spawning Rules

New gems spawn with these probabilities:

Tier 1: 70%
Tier 2: 25%
Tier 3: 5%

Higher tiers can only be formed through merging.

Movement Rules
When an arrow is pressed, all gems slide as far as possible in that direction, stopping only when they:
Hit another gem, or
Reach the edge of the grid
If two gems of the same tier collide, they fuse into a single gem of the next tier.
A fused gem cannot fuse again in the same move, even if another matching gem lands on it.

Special Collision Cases

If three identical gems line up and the player moves toward them:
Only the two gems farthest in the direction of movement will merge.
If all five tiles in a row or column contain the same tier, a parallel move merges:

The first two gems,

And the last two gems
(Resulting in two merged gems plus one leftover in the center.)

Scoring

The score is shown in the upper-right corner.

Score = sum of tier values, where:

Tier 1 = 1 point

Tier 2 = 3 points

Tier 3 = 9 points

Tier 4 = 27 points

Tier 5 = 81 points

Fusing gives bonus points equal to the value of the resulting gem.

Winning Condition

The game is won when a Tier 5 (Legendary Gem) appears anywhere on the board.

Players may continue playing to achieve higher scores.

Game Over Condition

The game ends when:

There are no empty tiles, and

No adjacent tiles have the same tier

When the game ends, the user should be able to share their score.

Placement

Place the GemSlide Fusion game directly on the home page.

mini-app-factory-guide.prompt:
ChatGPT ha detto:

Ecco la versione in inglese, semplice, naturale e tutta filata:

Create a mini app called “Base Mini App Factory Guide”. The app should serve as a simple, beginner-friendly guide that helps users understand how to create their first mini app with the Base Mini App Factory. When the user opens the app, show a short introduction explaining what the Mini App Factory is: a tool that lets anyone build a mini app in minutes by describing it in natural language.

The app should guide the user step by step. First, explain how to describe their app idea clearly. Then explain how to submit the description, how the generation process works, and what happens when the app is ready to be deployed. Each step should be explained in short, direct sentences, as if it were a tutorial for absolute beginners.

Include a section that explains the key concepts: what no-code creation means, how the automatic generation system works, what “deploying on Base” means, and how users can update or improve their app after it has been created.

Add a FAQ page with short answers to common questions such as: “How long does it take?”, “Can I edit my app?”, “What happens during deployment?”, and “Do I need technical experience?”. Keep the tone clear, friendly, and supportive.

The interface should be simple and easy to navigate, with a small menu linking to “Introduction”, “How to Create a Mini App”, “Key Concepts”, and “FAQ”. Use a clean layout and readable colors. The goal is to make the user feel confident, supported, and ready to build their first mini app independently.

miniapp.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. misscrypto.title: Misscrypto
misscrypto.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

motivation.title: Motivation
motivation.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Betting Odds Analyzer
1. Project Overview

The Betting Odds Analyzer is a small application designed to help users evaluate and compare betting odds from different bookmakers. The program calculates implied probability, checks for value bets, and gives a basic assessment of whether a bet might be statistically reasonable.
The tool is intended for informational purposes only and does not provide betting advice.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Odds Input

The program must allow users to:

Enter odds manually (decimal format, e.g., 1.75).

Add multiple outcomes (e.g., Team A win, Team B win, Draw).

Optionally load odds from an external API (if available).

2.2 Core Calculations

The system must calculate:

Implied probability for each outcome.

Formula: 1 / odds

Total market margin (to detect bookmaker overround).

Value bet indicator based on user’s own estimated winning probability.

Expected value (EV) of the bet:

EV = (probability * odds) - 1

2.3 Analysis Output

The tool should display:

Implied probability for each outcome

Overround percentage

Expected value (positive or negative)

Simple labels like:

“Possible value bet”

“Neutral bet”

“Negative EV – avoid”

2.4 UI Requirements

Clear input fields for odds and user probability.

Table showing calculations for each outcome.

Color-coded EV indicator:

Green: positive EV

Yellow: neutral

Red: negative EV

Optional: add chart displaying changes in odds over time.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Desktop app (Python) or web-based version.

3.2 Performance

Calculations must run instantly (under 0.2 seconds).

Interface must remain responsive even with multiple outcomes.

3.3 Reliability

If API fails or data is missing, the program should revert to manual mode.

Should validate inputs and warn the user if values are invalid.

3.4 Legal & Safety

Must show a disclaimer stating:
“This tool is for educational purposes only and does not provide betting advice.”

4. Recommended Tech Stack
Option A – Python Desktop

Python

Tkinter or PyQt

Requests (for API access)

Pandas (for data handling)

Option B – Web App

HTML/CSS/JavaScript

Chart.js for visualizations

Fetch API for loading odds data

5. Possible Future Improvements

Auto-detection of arbitrage opportunities

Multi-bookmaker comparison

Live odds tracking

Alerts for large odds changes

myself.prompt:
1. Project Overview

RevTrader is an automated trading bot designed to open reverse positions (counter to a detected signal) in Long and Short strategies.
The bot is suitable for crypto, forex, or stock markets via APIs of trading platforms/exchanges.
Its goal is to exploit market reversals or hedge positions automatically.

2. Objectives

Automatically detect market conditions and open reverse positions.

Support both Long and Short strategies.

Integrate with popular exchanges via API (Binance, Kraken, Coinbase, etc.).

Allow risk management (stop-loss, take-profit, trailing).

Log trades and provide analytics for strategy performance.

3. Core Features
3.1 Market Data Analysis

Real-time price and volume tracking

Support for multiple timeframes (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h)

Technical indicators: RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, EMA, SMA

Signal detection for trend reversals

3.2 Reverse Position Execution

Open reverse Long if a Short signal is detected

Open reverse Short if a Long signal is detected

Optional partial reversal (split position)

Configurable lot size and leverage

3.3 Risk Management

Stop-loss and take-profit per trade

Trailing stop options

Max open positions per symbol

Max daily loss limit

3.4 Exchange Integration

Connect via REST/WebSocket APIs

Place market and limit orders

Check account balance, margin, and open positions

Multi-exchange support

3.5 Logging & Analytics

Trade logs (timestamp, symbol, side, price, size, PnL)

Performance metrics: win rate, average profit/loss, max drawdown

Export to CSV or JSON

mysticmawarmerah.title: Mysticmawarmerah
mysticmawarmerah.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

name.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Family Tree Builder Application
1. Project Overview

The Family Tree Builder is a software application designed to create, edit, and visualize family trees. The program allows users to store personal information about relatives, track relationships, attach media files, and generate multi-generation diagrams.
The app is intended for genealogy research, family history documentation, and personal use.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Person Profile Management

The program must allow users to:

Add new family members

Edit or delete existing profiles

Enter personal details:

Full name

Date of birth / death

Gender

Photos

Biography or notes

Occupation (optional)

2.2 Relationship Management

The system must support:

Parent → Child links

Sibling relationships

Marriage / partnership links

Divorce / separation

Multiple marriages

Step-family or adopted family connections

2.3 Tree Visualization

The app should generate a visual family tree:

Horizontal or vertical layout

Expand/collapse generation levels

Display key data next to each person

Smooth navigation (scrolling, zooming)

Highlight selected individual and direct relatives

Optional visualization modes:

Pedigree chart

Descendant chart

Full tree chart

2.4 Search and Filtering

The program must support:

Search by name

Search by date of birth or death

Filters:

By generation

By surname

By branch of the family

Quick navigation to a selected person

2.5 Media and Documents

Users should be able to:

Attach photos (PNG/JPG)

Attach documents (PDF/notes)

Link media to specific events (e.g., wedding, birth)

View gallery for each family member

2.6 Event Timeline (Optional)

The system may include a timeline showing:

Birth dates

Marriages

Important historical or personal events

Users can view the timeline per individual or for the entire family.

2.7 Data Backup & Export

The application must support:

Exporting family tree to:

PDF (diagram)

Image (PNG)

GEDCOM (common genealogy format)

Importing data from GEDCOM

Local backup and restore

2.8 User Notes & Tags

Users can:

Add personal notes

Assign tags (e.g., “research needed”, “confirmed”, “maternal line”)

Mark incomplete data

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

The program can be:

Desktop app (Windows/Mac/Linux)

Web application

Mobile app (optional)

3.2 Performance

Trees with up to 1,000 individuals should load within 1 second

Smooth zoom and navigation

Efficient memory usage for large trees

3.3 Data Storage

Local database (SQLite recommended) or local JSON/XML files

Optionally: cloud sync

3.4 Security

Family data must be stored locally unless cloud sync is explicitly enabled

If cloud sync is used → encryption required

3.5 Usability

Intuitive interface

Drag-and-drop features for rearranging tree (optional)

Undo/redo support

4. Technical Stack (Recommended)
Option A – Desktop Application (Python)

Python

PyQt5 or Tkinter

SQLite for database

Graphviz/d3-like library for visualization

Option B – Web Application

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

Visualization: D3.js

Option C – Mobile

Flutter or React Native

5. Future Extensions

DNA test integration (Ancestry/23andMe style)

Collaboration between multiple users

Automatic tree generation from uploaded documents

AI-powered relationship suggestion (optional)

Historical map of family migrations

neko.title: Neko
neko.prompt:
App Development Plan: Neko – Football Artifact Exchange
1. Project Overview

App Name: Neko
Purpose: To allow football fans to exchange football memorabilia (such as jerseys, autographs, tickets, etc.) in a secure and user-friendly environment.
Platform: iOS and Android (via React Native or Flutter)
Target Audience: Football enthusiasts, collectors, and fans aged 16–50.

2. Key Features
2.1 User Authentication & Profiles

Login/Sign-up: Users can sign up with email, Google, or Facebook accounts.

User Profile: Each user will have a profile where they can showcase their artifacts, exchange history, and wishlist.

Verification: Option to verify users to prevent fraud (e.g., identity verification or artifact authenticity).

2.2 Artifact Listings

Create Listings: Users can upload artifacts with photos, descriptions, and conditions (e.g., "New," "Worn," "Signed," etc.).

Artifact Categories: Categories like jerseys, football cards, tickets, autographs, and limited-edition items.

Pricing: Users can either list artifacts for sale, trade, or auction.

Search & Filters: Advanced search with filters for price, category, condition, and location.

2.3 Marketplace & Exchange

Buy/Sell/Trade: Users can buy, sell, or trade artifacts directly with others.

Auction System: Option for users to auction their artifacts.

Offers: Ability to send trade offers to other users, which can include multiple items.

Transaction History: A record of all past transactions and exchanges.

2.4 Social Interaction

Chat & Negotiation: Integrated messaging feature for users to negotiate prices or trade offers.

Ratings & Reviews: After each exchange, users can rate each other and leave reviews to ensure trust and accountability.

2.5 Notifications

Alerts: Push notifications for new listings, trade offers, and messages.

Auction End Notifications: Alerts for users when an auction is about to end.

2.6 Security & Trust

Escrow Service: For trades and sales, hold the funds in escrow until both parties confirm the exchange.

Artifact Authentication: Partnership with expert authenticators to verify the authenticity of high-value items.

User Reporting: Feature for reporting fraudulent or suspicious listings.

3. App Design & UI/UX
3.1 General Design

Minimalist and Clean Design: Focus on an intuitive, easy-to-navigate interface.

Color Palette: Use the team's colors or football-related themes (green, black, white, and gold accents).

Icons: Use football-related icons for buttons (e.g., football for listing, trading icons, etc.).

Responsive: Ensure smooth functionality on both small and large screens.

3.2 Main Screens

Home Screen: Feature popular or trending items, categories, and recommended trades.

Explore Screen: Searchable marketplace where users can browse listings.

Profile Screen: User profile with inventory, wishlist, and transaction history.

Messages Screen: In-app chat system for negotiations.

Settings Screen: Personal settings, app preferences, and security options.

3.3 User Flow

Onboarding Process: A simple walkthrough for new users explaining how to create listings, browse artifacts, and participate in exchanges.

Artifact Listing Process: Easy-to-use interface for uploading and categorizing items.

Transaction Process: Clear steps for buying, selling, or trading items to avoid confusion.

4. Technical Stack
4.1 Front-End Development

React Native or Flutter for cross-platform mobile development.

React Navigation for routing and navigation between screens.

State Management: Redux or Context API for managing app state.

4.2 Back-End Development

Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS): Firebase or AWS Amplify for rapid backend development and authentication.

Database: Firebase Firestore or MongoDB for storing user profiles, artifact listings, and transaction history.

Real-Time Features: Firebase Realtime Database or Socket.IO for chat and notifications.

4.3 API Integration

Payment Gateway: Integration with Stripe, PayPal, or similar for in-app purchases.

Email & SMS Notifications: Integrate with SendGrid or Twilio for email/SMS alerts.

4.4 Security

Authentication: Firebase Authentication for secure login and sign-up.

Encryption: Use SSL/TLS for secure data transmission.

Payment Security: Secure transactions via encrypted payment gateways.

5. Development Timeline
5.1 Phase 1: Planning & Design (1–2 months)

Finalize app requirements and features.

Create wireframes and mockups.

Develop a UI/UX design.

5.2 Phase 2: Development (3–4 months)

Set up the backend infrastructure and database.

Implement core features: user profiles, artifact listings, marketplace, and messaging.

Develop the payment and escrow system.

Integrate authentication and security features.

5.3 Phase 3: Testing & Feedback (1–2 months)

Conduct unit testing and user testing.

Gather feedback from test users and make necessary adjustments.

Test payment integration and chat functionality.

5.4 Phase 4: Launch & Marketing (1 month)

Prepare app store listings (Google Play, Apple App Store).

Launch marketing campaigns (social media, influencers, football-related events).

Monitor app performance and resolve bugs post-launch.

6. Monetization Strategies

Transaction Fees: Charge a small fee on each transaction (buy/sell/trade).

Premium Accounts: Offer subscription plans for additional features like advanced listing options, higher visibility, etc.

In-App Purchases: Users can buy premium listings or boost their artifact's visibility for a fee.

7. Post-Launch Considerations

User Support: Set up an in-app help center and customer service team.

User Feedback Loop: Collect user feedback regularly to improve features.

Continual Updates: Regularly update the app with new features, security patches, and performance enhancements.

A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

nft-marketplace.title: Nft Marketplace
nft-marketplace.prompt:
A decentralized, social-driven NFT-based Marketplace where users can easily create, buy, and trade NFTs with gamified features to encourage engagement. The app will also have a unique feature that integrates gamified staking rewards, where users earn tokens for interacting with NFTs and participating in community activities.

This mini-app will focus on ease of use, a clean and intuitive UI/UX, and a no-code minting platform for NFTs. The app will focus on driving social interaction, offering reward incentives, and zero gas fees for trading, thanks to the BASE chain. Its viral nature will come from sharing, user-generated content, and the use of NFT-based incentives.

Mini-App Features:

User-Friendly NFT Creation (No-Code Minting)

Feature: Easy-to-use interface for creating and minting NFTs without technical expertise.

UI/UX: Simple drag-and-drop interface for images, video, or audio. Users can add metadata, like title, description, and royalties.

Sustainability: Zero fees for minting on BASE, ensuring users can create without barriers.

NFT Marketplace:

Feature: A dynamic marketplace where users can buy, sell, and auction NFTs.

UI/UX: Clean, modern, and responsive design with filters, categories, and sorting options (e.g., price, rarity).

Sustainability: Low gas fees for transaction processing, making buying and selling frictionless and efficient.

Gamified Staking & Rewards:

Feature: Users can stake NFTs or tokens to earn rewards. Staked NFTs provide passive income, unlocking exclusive content or boosting social profile stats.

UI/UX: Easy-to-understand staking dashboard showing how much a user has staked, rewards earned, and real-time progress.

Sustainability: Incentive-driven gameplay mechanics where the rewards (e.g., native tokens) encourage long-term engagement.

Social Sharing & Community Engagement:

Feature: Users can easily share their NFTs on social media platforms. The app will also allow creating NFT galleries where users showcase their owned or created NFTs.

UI/UX: Highly interactive NFT showcase with a "like", "comment", and "share" buttons, creating viral loops of exposure.

Sustainability: Social engagement and community-driven content will drive viral growth.

NFT Rarity and Power-Up System:

Feature: Each NFT has rarity and power-up attributes that influence the staking rewards or unlock exclusive features within the app.

UI/UX: Rarity score and power-up levels are visually represented on each NFT’s profile page with easy-to-understand icons and tooltips.

Sustainability: Encourages the acquisition of rare NFTs and incentivizes continued participation through rewards.

Integrated Wallet with BASE Chain Support:

Feature: In-app wallet that supports BASE chain transactions with no need for third-party wallets.

UI/UX: Easy-to-navigate wallet interface showing balances, transaction history, and NFT holdings.

Sustainability: Integration of BASE chain's low gas fees ensures smooth and seamless transactions.

AI-Driven Personalized NFT Recommendations:

Feature: Personalized suggestions for NFTs based on user preferences, activity, and previous purchases.

UI/UX: AI-based recommendation engine that displays NFTs relevant to the user's tastes, visible directly on the homepage or as a sidebar.

Sustainability: Increases user retention by making the app feel tailored to each individual.

Collaborative NFT Projects:

Feature: Users can collaborate to create and mint NFTs as a group. The app facilitates the pooling of funds, sharing, and creation of NFT collections for group ownership.

UI/UX: Multi-user interface where groups can seamlessly communicate and mint their collaborative NFTs.

Sustainability: Builds a sense of community, where users create and share NFTs together, further encouraging retention and virality.

Cross-Platform Integration (Mobile and Web):

Feature: The app will be accessible on both mobile and web, making it convenient to use anytime, anywhere.

UI/UX: Responsive design to ensure fluid transitions between mobile and desktop. Smooth user flow with consistent design elements.

Sustainability: Cross-platform usage increases app accessibility and broadens the potential user base.

Real-Time Auction and Live Events:

Feature: Real-time NFT auctions and live events for big drops, collaborations, or NFT artist showcases.

UI/UX: Simple auction interface with countdown timers, bid placement buttons, and notifications.

Sustainability: Live events and auctions keep the user base actively engaged and create a sense of urgency around NFT drops.

Key UI/UX Principles:

Minimalist & Intuitive: Clean, simple, and intuitive layout to ensure ease of use, even for users new to blockchain.

Fast Performance: Speed is critical for keeping users engaged, so optimize the app for quick load times and low-latency interactions.

Mobile-First Design: Focus on mobile app design, with responsive design for web, making sure the user experience is seamless across all devices.

Gamification: Reward systems should be prominent and easy to engage with, including progress bars, achievement badges, and notifications that make users feel accomplished.

Virality Elements:

Referral Program: Users get rewards for referring others to the platform. When someone signs up through their link, both users earn exclusive NFTs or tokens.

Viral NFT Challenges: Weekly or monthly NFT creation challenges where users can submit NFTs to win prizes. Challenges encourage virality by encouraging content creation and sharing.

Social Sharing Incentives: Users get rewards for sharing their NFTs on social media platforms, with leaderboard systems showing the most active content creators.

Description:

NFT Mint Reminder helps users keep track of upcoming NFT mint events. The app displays simple countdowns and event details for selected NFT collections in a clean, easy-to-read dashboard.

 • Shows upcoming NFT mint events with collection name and mint date.
 • Countdown timer for each event.

 4. Quickly check the dashboard to see all upcoming mints.

Benefits:
 • Never miss an NFT mint event.
 • Simple visual countdowns make tracking easy.
 • Minimal setup and intuitive design for all users.

nftauction.title: Nftauction
nftauction.prompt:
Description:
NFT Auction Sniper helps users track live NFT auctions and automatically identify optimal bid timing. Stay ahead of competitors, monitor price movements, and snipe the best deals before auctions close.

Key Features:
 • Real-time tracking of ongoing NFT auctions across major marketplaces.
 • Alerts for last-minute auction opportunities.
 • Price history and bid trend analysis.
 • Custom “snipe zones” based on user-defined price limits.
 • Multi-marketplace support (OpenSea, Blur, Magic Eden, etc.).

Target Users:
NFT collectors, flippers, traders, and bargain hunters looking to gain an edge in competitive NFT auctions.

Usage Instructions:

 2. Set your maximum bid and snipe conditions.
 3. Receive alerts when the auction nears closing or hits your target.
 4. Make informed bids with real-time data.

Benefits:
 • Beat competitors with precise timing.
 • Avoid overpaying by setting smart snipe thresholds.
 • Track auctions efficiently across many marketplaces.

nftcollection.title: Nftcollection
nftcollection.prompt:
Description:
NFT Collection Health Score analyzes the overall strength and stability of any NFT collection using key metrics such as liquidity, holder diversity, trading activity, and market trends.

Key Features:
 • Generates a health score based on multiple on-chain and market factors.
 • Tracks unique holders, floor price stability, and liquidity depth.
 • Detects wash trading and suspicious activity.
 • Visual performance charts (volume, sales count, holder trends).
 • Multi-marketplace support (OpenSea, Blur, Magic Eden, etc.).

Target Users:
NFT traders, collectors, analysts, and investors who need a quick and reliable way to evaluate the quality and stability of NFT collections.

Usage Instructions:
 1. Enter the NFT collection address or select from the list.
 2. View the health score and detailed breakdown of metrics.
 3. Monitor changes in holder distribution, liquidity, and trading volume.
 4. Use the score to identify strong or risky collections.

Benefits:
 • Quickly assess the strength and reliability of NFT projects.
 • Detect red flags before buying or minting.
 • Compare multiple collections to find high-potential opportunities.

nftfloorresistanceanalyzer.title: Nftfloorresistanceanalyzer
nftfloorresistanceanalyzer.prompt:
App Name: NFT Floor Resistance Analyzer**

Description:
NFT Floor Resistance Analyzer is a Mini App that analyzes the buy and sell pressure around an NFT collection’s floor price. It identifies how many listings exist at key price levels, detects “walls” of sellers, and highlights zones of strong resistance or support. This helps users evaluate how easily a floor can rise or fall based on current market depth.

Key Features:
 • Real-time analysis of floor price resistance and support levels
 • Detection of large listing clusters (“seller walls”)
 • Monitoring floor depth across multiple marketplaces
 • Historical data showing changes in resistance zones
 • Dashboard to compare resistance profiles of multiple collections

Use Case:
Perfect for NFT traders and collectors who want to understand price structure, anticipate floor breakouts, and identify opportunities based on market depth dynamics.

nfttrade.title: Nfttrade
nfttrade.prompt:
Project Plan: NFTTrade – Mini NFT Exchange App
1. Project Overview

NFTTrade is a lightweight application that allows users to create, list, buy, sell, and exchange NFTs. The app focuses on simplicity, speed, and low transaction fees. It will integrate with a blockchain (e.g., Ethereum, Polygon, or Solana) and support common NFT standards.

2. Core Features
2.1 User Accounts & Wallet Integration

Connect external wallets (MetaMask, Phantom, WalletConnect).

Display user balance, owned NFTs, and transaction history.

Optional guest mode with limited functionality.

2.2 NFT Listing & Browsing

Browse NFTs by categories, price, trending, and newest.

View NFT details: image, description, owner, contract address, and metadata.

Search and filter functionality.

2.3 NFT Minting

Simple form to upload media (image/video).

Add metadata (name, description, attributes).

Mint NFT to selected blockchain.

2.4 Buying & Selling NFTs

List NFTs for sale at a fixed price or via auction.

Initiate secure blockchain transactions.

Automatic update of ownership after purchase.

2.5 Trading / Swapping NFTs

Peer-to-peer NFT swap system between users.

Two-party confirmation mechanism.

Optional additional payment during the swap.

2.6 Activity Feed & Notifications

Track sales, bids, and new listings.

Real-time updates using WebSockets or blockchain event listeners.

3. Technology Stack
Frontend

React / Next.js

TypeScript

Web3.js or Ethers.js

TailwindCSS or Material UI

Backend

Node.js + Express

API for user profiles, metadata storage, and listing management

Optional: serverless functions (AWS Lambda / Vercel)

Blockchain

Ethereum (ERC-721, ERC-1155)

Or: Solana (Metaplex), Polygon, BNB Chain

IPFS for decentralized storage (via Pinata or NFT.Storage)

Database

MongoDB / Firebase / PostgreSQL

Store user profiles, listings, and caching of metadata

4. Architecture Overview

Client communicates with backend API for listing and metadata.

Blockchain interactions happen directly through the user’s wallet.

Metadata stored on IPFS; only references stored in database.

Backend listens to blockchain events to update states (ownership, sales).

5. Development Stages
Stage 1: Planning & Design

Define user flows and core features.

Create UI/UX mockups (Figma).

Choose blockchain and NFT standards.

Stage 2: Environment Setup

Configure frontend and backend structures.

Set up blockchain development environment (Hardhat/Foundry).

Create development smart contracts.

Stage 3: Smart Contract Development

NFT minting contract (ERC-721/ERC-1155).

Marketplace contract (buy/sell functions).

Swap/trade contract (two-party exchange).

Deploy to testnet (Goerli, Mumbai, etc.).

Stage 4: Frontend Integration

Connect wallet integration.

Implement minting, listing, and buying UIs.

Display NFTs using metadata from IPFS.

Stage 5: Backend & Database

User and listing management APIs.

Store metadata references and activity logs.

Implement security (JWT, rate limiting).

Stage 6: Testing & Optimization

Smart contract audits.

UI testing across multiple devices.

Load testing for marketplace operations.

Stage 7: Deployment

Deploy frontend (Vercel/Netlify).

Deploy backend (AWS/DigitalOcean).

Deploy smart contracts to mainnet.

Stage 8: Launch & Maintenance

Add analytics and monitoring.

Regular updates and bug fixes.

Roll out new features: staking, royalties, multi-chain support.

6. Additional Features (Optional)

NFT fractionalization

Social features (likes, comments, follows)

Multi-chain bridge for NFTs

Mobile app version (React Native / Flutter)

niya.title: Niya
niya.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

On-Chain Reputation Score evaluates blockchain addresses based on their transaction history and activity, providing a clear “trustworthiness” metric. Use it to assess counterparties, DeFi participants, NFT traders, and more.

Target Users:
Crypto traders, NFT collectors, DeFi users, and anyone who wants to evaluate on-chain trustworthiness.

Usage Instructions:

 2. View the reputation score, historical trends, and key metrics.
 3. Set alerts for significant changes in reputation.
 4. Make informed decisions when interacting with unknown addresses.

Benefits:
 • Assess counterparty reliability before engaging in transactions.
 • Detect potential scams or risky addresses early.
 • Gain deeper insights into on-chain behavior for smarter decisions.

openxai.prompt:
The app is called "OpenxAI Word Guesser". Every day, a new five-letter word is chosen (make sure to have a list of words for every day for the next 365 days), and players attempt to guess it within six tries. After each guess, the letters are color-coded to indicate their accuracy: green means the letter is correct and in the right position, yellow means it is in the word but in the wrong position, and gray means it is not in the word at all. orderbooklens.title: Orderbooklens
orderbooklens.prompt:
Idea: A visual order book and liquidity heatmap.
User goal: Quickly see where major liquidity clusters and walls are.
Core features (MVP):

* Real-time order book depth (bids/asks).
* Cumulative depth chart (classic depth graph).
* Price levels with highlighted “walls” (large resting orders).
* Configurable depth range (e.g., ±1%, ±3%, ±5% from mid-price).

Development plan:

1. Connect to an exchange’s order book WebSocket API.
2. Aggregate levels and compute cumulative volume.
3. Render:

a depth chart (using a chart library),
a list of top N levels with color intensity by size.


4. Add user controls: pair selection, depth range, minimum wall size.
5. Optimize throttling/batching of updates so the UI stays smooth.

parasiteve.title: Parasiteve
parasiteve.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

portfolio-allocation-planner.title: Portfolio Allocation Planner
portfolio-allocation-planner.prompt:
Portfolio Allocation Planner — App Description

Create a simple mini app called “Portfolio Allocation Planner”.
This app helps users create and manage their ideal crypto portfolio allocations using only manual input.
No internet access, APIs, or Web3 integrations are required.

Core Features
 1. A text input field for entering the token name.
 2. A numeric input field for entering the desired allocation percentage (e.g., 25%).
 3. A button “Add Allocation” that adds the entry to a list.
 4. A visible list or table showing each allocation:
 • Token name
 • Target allocation percentage
 5. Each item in the list should have:
 • A “Edit” button opening a dialog to update the percentage
 • A “Delete” button to remove the token
 6. A summary section at the bottom that displays:
 • Total allocation percentage (sum of all tokens)
 • A warning message if the total exceeds 100%

How the app should work
 • User enters a token name and a target percentage.
 • Presses “Add Allocation” to add the token to the portfolio list.
 • The app recalculates the total percentage after each change.
 • If the total exceeds 100%, show a clear warning message.
 • User can edit or delete any token allocation manually.
 • All data lives inside the app session.

UI Requirements
 • Inputs at the top in a clean form.
 • Allocations listed below in a simple structured layout.
 • Summary total displayed clearly at the bottom.
 • Warning message shown in a simple text label if needed.

Goal of the App

Allow users to plan their ideal crypto portfolio structure by manually defining allocation percentages in a clear and easy-to-use interface.

position-size-helper.title: Position Size Helper
position-size-helper.prompt:
Position Size Helper — App Description

Create a simple mini app called “Position Size Helper”.
The app helps users calculate the position size for trades based on their balance and chosen risk percentage.
All inputs and calculations are done manually; no internet or external data is required.

Core Features
 1. Numeric input field for account balance (total available funds).
 2. Numeric input field for risk percentage (e.g., 2% risk per trade).
 3. Numeric input field for entry price (optional, for reference).
 4. A button “Calculate Position Size” that performs the calculation:
\text{Position Size} = \text{Balance} \times (\text{Risk %} / 100)
 5. A display area showing the calculated position size.
 6. Optional: allow multiple calculations in a list format, storing previous results.

How the App Should Work
 • User enters balance and risk percentage.
 • Presses “Calculate Position Size”, and the app displays the result immediately.
 • Users can perform multiple calculations if needed.
 • Results are stored locally and can be removed manually.
 • All calculations occur locally without internet or Web3 integration.

UI Requirements
 • Simple form layout with input fields at the top.
 • “Calculate Position Size” button clearly visible.
 • Result displayed prominently below inputs.
 • Optional list of previous calculations shown below result.
 • Clean, minimal design with clearly labeled buttons.

Goal of the App

Provide traders with a lightweight, offline-friendly tool to quickly calculate trade position sizes based on their chosen risk.

pro44.title: Pro44
pro44.prompt:
1. Project Overview

The Personal Finance Tracker is a mobile/web application designed to help users monitor their income, expenses, and budgets. The app provides visualizations, financial reports, reminders, and goal tracking to improve money management and financial awareness.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Income & Expense Management

Users can add, edit, and delete financial transactions.

Each transaction includes:

Title/description

Amount

Date

Category (e.g., Food, Transport, Entertainment, Salary)

Payment method (optional: cash, card, bank)

Recurring transactions for subscriptions, bills, and salary.

2.2 Budgeting

Users can create budgets per category.

The app tracks spending against budgets and warns if limits are exceeded.

Monthly, weekly, or custom periods for budgets.

2.3 Reports & Analytics

Graphs showing income vs. expenses over time (bar, line, pie charts).

Category breakdown for expenses.

Summary of total income, total expenses, and net savings.

Optional: forecast future savings based on past spending patterns.

2.4 Reminders & Notifications

Remind users of upcoming bills, due payments, or budget limits.

Optional push notifications or email alerts.

2.5 Search & Filtering

Search transactions by title, category, or date.

Filter by income, expense, or specific categories.

2.6 Data Export & Backup

Export transactions to CSV or PDF.

Backup and restore data locally or via cloud sync.

2.7 User Preferences

Theme: Light / Dark mode.

Default currency selection.

Language selection.

Configure recurring transaction reminders.

3. Non-Functional Requirements
3.1 Platform

Mobile app (iOS/Android recommended)

Web app optional

3.2 Performance

Adding, editing, or searching transactions should be instantaneous (<0.5s).

Analytics charts must render quickly (<1s for 1000+ transactions).

3.3 Security

Store sensitive data securely (encrypted at rest and in transit).

Optional: password or biometric authentication.

3.4 Usability

Intuitive interface for adding transactions quickly.

Simple navigation between dashboards, budgets, and reports.

4. Recommended Technical Stack
Mobile

Flutter or React Native

Local database: SQLite or Realm

Push notifications: native or via Firebase

Web

Frontend: React / Vue.js

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL / MongoDB

5. Future Enhancements

Multi-currency support

Bank account integration for automatic transaction import

AI-powered expense predictions

Financial goal tracking (e.g., saving for a car, vacation)

Shared accounts for families or roommates
