proeckt.title: Proeckt
proeckt.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS): Crypto Analytics Tool
1. Project Overview

Develop a crypto analytics tool designed to support analysts in making data-driven decisions. The tool must collect, process, visualize, and interpret blockchain and market data in real time. It should provide actionable insights on price movements, on-chain activity, market sentiment, liquidity flows, and risk levels.

2. Core Objectives

Provide real-time and historical cryptocurrency market data.

Analyze on-chain metrics for selected blockchains (e.g., Bitcoin, Ethereum).

Offer visualization dashboards for better interpretation of data.

Enable alerts based on user-defined thresholds or AI-driven anomaly detection.

Provide exportable reports (CSV, PDF).

Ensure high performance and minimal latency.

3. Key Features
3.1 Data Collection

Integrate with major market data providers (CoinGecko, Binance API, Coinbase, Kraken).

On-chain data via providers such as Glassnode, CryptoQuant, Alchemy, Infura, Chainbase.

Social sentiment sources (Twitter/X API, Reddit API, LunarCrush).

Data refresh interval: 1s–60s (configurable).

3.2 Analytics Modules
3.2.1 Market Analytics

Price tracking and volatility analysis

Market depth and order book aggregation

Volume and liquidity metrics

Moving averages (SMA, EMA), RSI, MACD

3.2.2 On-Chain Analytics

Active addresses, new addresses

Transaction volume, fees, mempool size

Whale movements tracking

Exchange inflows/outflows

Supply distribution and holder age metrics

3.2.3 Sentiment Analysis

NLP sentiment scoring (positive/neutral/negative)

Fear & Greed index calculations

Social trend detection using keywords and hashtags

3.2.4 Risk & Anomaly Detection

Volatility spikes

On-chain anomalies (unusual inflows/outflows)

Exchange wallet activity alerts

Sudden sentiment changes

4. User Interface Requirements
4.1 Dashboard

Modular, customizable widgets

Real-time charts (candles, depth charts, heat maps)

Alerts panel

Multi-asset comparison view

4.2 Visualizations

Time-series charts

Pie charts, bar graphs

Heatmaps of liquidity or sentiment

On-chain flow diagrams

4.3 User Settings

Custom alert thresholds

Watchlists

API key management

Dark/light mode

5. System Architecture
5.1 Frontend

Technologies: React.js / Vue.js

Real-time data handling: WebSockets

Charting: TradingView Charting Library or D3.js

5.2 Backend

Technologies: Node.js / Python (FastAPI / Django)

Data processing pipeline with caching

Database: PostgreSQL or MongoDB

Redis for real-time caching

Microservices architecture is recommended

5.3 Integrations

External APIs for data ingestion

Optional AI/ML module (Python-based)

Authentication via JWT or OAuth

6. Performance Requirements

Real-time data latency < 1 second

Backend uptime 99.9%

Efficient handling of 100k requests/min

Scalability to support thousands of concurrent users

7. Security Requirements

HTTPS and data encryption

Protection against DDOS

Rate limiting for API endpoints

Secure storage of user API keys (encrypted vault)

8. Deliverables

Complete architecture diagrams

Frontend + Backend source code

Documentation (API docs, installation, architecture)

Unit and integration tests (>80% coverage)

Production-ready deployment scripts (Docker/Kubernetes)

9. Timeline (Example)
Phase	Duration	Deliverables
Research & Planning	1–2 weeks	Requirements, architecture
Backend Development	3–5 weeks	API modules, DB setup
Frontend Development	3–5 weeks	UI, dashboards, charts
AI/ML Features	2–4 weeks	Sentiment & anomaly detection
Testing	2 weeks	QA, bug fixes
Deployment	1 week	Production launch
10. Success Criteria

Stable real-time analytics system

Accurate and verified data

Intuitive UI for crypto analysts

Scalable infrastructure

High user satisfaction

profit-and-loss-snapshot.prompt:
Profit and Loss Snapshot — текст для розгортання

Title: Profit and Loss Snapshot

Description:
Create a simple app where users can quickly view their profit or loss based on manual inputs. The app should work entirely offline, without external data or API calls. All values must be entered manually.

Functionality:
 • Display three input fields:
 1. “Buy Price”
 2. “Current Price”
 3. “Amount Held”
 • When the user clicks a button labeled “Calculate”, compute:
 • Total Cost = Buy Price × Amount Held
 • Current Value = Current Price × Amount Held
 • Profit/Loss = Current Value – Total Cost
 • Profit/Loss % = (Profit/Loss / Total Cost) × 100
 • Show the results in a clean results section with labels:
 • “Total Cost:”
 • “Current Value:”
 • “P/L Amount:”
 • “P/L Percentage:”
 • If any input is missing or invalid, display a message:
“Please enter valid numbers.”
 • Add a small “Reset” button that clears all inputs and the results.

UI Requirements:
 • Use only simple UI elements: text fields, labels, buttons, and a results box.
 • All calculations must run locally inside the app.
 • Keep the layout minimal and easy to understand.

promo.prompt: Create a cheerful and festive mobile app for New Year celebrations where users can create, send, and receive greetings with friends, family, or the community. The app’s unique charm is turning New Year greetings into a magical, interactive, and memorable experience for everyone.

proof-of-vibe.title: Proof Of Vibe
proof-of-vibe.prompt:
Create a groundbreaking AI-powered mini app for Base called “Proof-of-Vibe” – the first on-chain mood & reputation layer.

Core idea:  
Users connect their wallet once and grant the app permission to anonymously read their on-chain history (trades, NFT holds, DeFi positions, social posts on Farcaster, Lens follows, etc.). The AI instantly generates a beautiful, shareable “Vibe Card” – a dynamic NFT that visually represents their unique crypto personality, risk profile, aesthetics, and community alignment in real-time.

Unique features that make it stand out:
1. Daily regenerating Vibe Card (free mint or small fee) with rare traits based on actual behavior (e.g., “Diamond Hands Since 2021”, “Degenerate Gambler”, “Based Art Collector”, “Farcaster Poet”, “Yield Chad”, etc.)
2. Vibe Score (0–1000) that updates live and can be used by other dApps (with user permission) for social matching, exclusive access, airdrops, or dating-style “vibe checks”
3. “Vibe Match” – swipe-like interface to find other users with compatible crypto personalities (e.g., “find me diamond-hand maximalists who love memes and purple NFTs”)
4. Mini-games: predict your own Vibe Score in 7 days for bonus points/tokens, or bet with friends whose vibe will rank higher
5. Monetization: 
   - Premium cosmetic frames & animations (paid in OPENX or ETH)
   - Boosted visibility in the leaderboard
   - Allow projects to sponsor rare traits or temporary “badges” (e.g., “Attended Devcon 2025” verified badge)
6. Fully on-chain provenance: every Vibe Card is an SVG NFT stored on Base, tradeable, and composable with other protocols

Make it fun, slightly sarcastic, visually stunning, and deeply crypto-native. Include memes, references to 2021–2025 cycles, and easter eggs for OGs. The tone should feel like a mix of Dune, Farcaster, and a fortune teller who actually knows your wallet.

Generate:
- Full app name & tagline
- Complete description for the Mini App Factory
- Suggested UI layout (home, card reveal animation, match screen, profile)
- Key prompts for the AI engine
- Monetization settings
- Suggested tokenomics/integration with $OPENX
- Viral sharing hooks for Farcaster/X/Base

qwwery.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Coin Flip Randomizer with Multiple Modes
1. Project Overview

The Coin Flip Randomizer is a simple application designed to simulate coin tosses with different modes and variations. The program provides a clean interface, multiple randomization options, statistics tracking, and customizable coin designs.
The tool is meant for games, decision-making, testing randomness, or entertainment.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Basic Coin Flip

The program must provide:

A standard Heads or Tails random result

Visual animation of a coin flip (optional)

Instant output if animation is disabled

Output format examples:

“Heads” / “Tails”

Icon-based display

Custom text if user enables custom labels

2.2 Multiple Flip Modes

The program must include several flip variations:

Mode 1: Single Flip

One flip per click

Displays result immediately

Mode 2: Multi-Flip

User selects number of flips (e.g., 10, 50, 100, 1000)

Program shows:

count of Heads

count of Tails

percentage distribution

optional chart (bar or pie chart)

Mode 3: Streak Mode

Tracks longest streaks during flips

Shows:

Longest Heads streak

Longest Tails streak

Current streak

Mode 4: Custom Coin

User can rename “Heads” and “Tails” (e.g., “Yes/No”, “Red/Blue”)

Program behaves like a normal flip but with custom labels

Mode 5: Weighted Coin

User can set probability of Heads or Tails (e.g., 60/40, 75/25)

Program must calculate result based on the chosen weight

2.3 Randomness Engine

Must use a high-quality pseudorandom number generator

Should avoid repeating patterns in short sequences

Optional: “True random mode” using online random API (if available)

2.4 Statistics & History

Keep flip history for the current session

Show:

total flips

Heads/Tails ratio

recent results (e.g., last 20 flips)

Optional: export history to a text or CSV file

3. User Interface Requirements

Simple, clean UI

Large button for coin flip

Clear display of results

Mode selector dropdown/menu

Statistics panel for multi-flip mode

Light/Dark mode

Optional:

coin animation

customizable coin color or image

4. Non-Functional Requirements
4.1 Platform

The program can be:

Desktop app (Windows/Linux/Mac)

Web app

Mobile app (optional)

4.2 Performance

Single flip results must be instantaneous

Multi-flip (1000+ flips) must complete under 1 second

UI should remain responsive during calculations

4.3 Data Handling

No personal data required

History stored only in current session (unless user saves)

4.4 Safety

Must show a disclaimer:
“This randomizer is for entertainment and simulation purposes only.”

5. Technical Stack (Recommended)
Option A – Desktop (Python)

Python

Tkinter or PyQt

Random module for RNG

Matplotlib for charts

Option B – Web App

HTML/CSS/JavaScript

Canvas or SVG for coin animation

Chart.js for statistics

LocalStorage for session history

Option C – Mobile

Flutter or React Native

6. Future Expansion

Dice roll modes

Spinner mode (like a wheel)

“Tournament flip” mode

Multiple coins flipped simultaneously

Custom coin images upload

Sound effects

refer.title: Refer
refer.prompt:
Plan for Creating the Mini-App "Refer" – Antiquities Exchange Platform

1. Introduction:
"Refer" will be a mobile and web-based application designed to facilitate the exchange of antiques and collectibles. It will connect individuals, collectors, and dealers who are interested in buying, selling, or trading antiques. The app will feature a user-friendly interface, secure transactions, and community features to support a passionate group of antique enthusiasts.

2. App Concept and Features Overview:
2.1. Core Features:

User Profiles:

Users can create personal or business profiles.

Profile customization with a display of their antique collection, preferences, and trade history.

Marketplace:

Users can list antiques they wish to sell or trade, including high-quality images, detailed descriptions, and price.

Search and filter options to browse items by category, era, location, price, or condition.

Trade/Exchange System:

An option for users to trade items directly, not just buy/sell.

Secure trade negotiation and agreement system (chat feature, item valuation).

Item Valuation and Authentication:

Users can request professional valuations or authentication from verified experts within the app.

Integration with third-party appraisers.

Secure Payments:

In-app payment gateway for transactions.

Escrow system to hold payments until both parties confirm the item is received in the expected condition.

Communication Tools:

Direct messaging for negotiation and discussion.

Group forums for antique enthusiasts to share knowledge, post collections, and organize events.

Authentication of Sellers:

Reputation scoring or reviews for sellers based on previous transactions.

Verification process for sellers to ensure they deal in legitimate antiques.

Location-based Search:

Users can search for nearby antiques or trades, helping users locate local sellers and buyers.

Option to deliver or pick up items locally.

Push Notifications:

Alerts for new items listed, new trades, or updates from followed users.

Educational Resources:

Articles, blogs, and videos about antique preservation, care, and history.

Expert advice for collectors and dealers.

3. Target Audience:

Antique Collectors:

Individuals passionate about collecting antiques who want to expand their collections or trade with others.

Antique Dealers:

Professionals who buy, sell, and trade antiques in the market, looking for a platform to reach more clients.

Casual Sellers:

People who wish to sell personal items, whether inherited or collected over time.

Experts/Appraisers:

Appraisers who provide authentication and valuation services within the app.

4. Technical Specifications:
4.1. Platform:

Mobile app (iOS and Android).

Web app for desktop access.

4.2. Architecture:

Backend:

Cloud-based architecture (AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure).

REST API for communication between app and server.

User management, transaction, and data storage services.

Frontend:

Mobile: React Native for cross-platform development (iOS and Android).

Web: React or Vue.js for interactive UI.

4.3. Database:

SQL (PostgreSQL or MySQL) for storing user data, item listings, transaction records, etc.

NoSQL (MongoDB) for flexible storage of item images and metadata.

4.4. Security:

End-to-end encryption for communication.

Two-factor authentication (2FA) for account security.

Secure payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, or custom integration).

4.5. User Authentication:

OAuth 2.0 for login via social accounts (Facebook, Google).

Email/password sign-up with password recovery options.

5. Development Plan:
5.1. Phase 1: Research & Design (2-3 months)

Conduct market research to understand user needs.

Create wireframes and prototypes for the app’s user interface (UI) and user experience (UX).

Develop an app design that is visually appealing and easy to navigate.

Gather feedback from potential users to refine the app's features.

5.2. Phase 2: Core Features Development (3-4 months)

Develop the basic functionalities: user registration, profile management, marketplace, and messaging system.

Implement secure payment gateway and escrow system.

Integrate item listings with filters and search capabilities.

Develop trade/exchange features and item authentication processes.

5.3. Phase 3: Testing & QA (1-2 months)

Perform user testing to identify any issues in usability, functionality, or performance.

Conduct security testing to ensure data protection.

Beta release with limited users for feedback and bug fixing.

5.4. Phase 4: Launch & Marketing (1 month)

Official release of the app on app stores and web platform.

Implement a marketing campaign targeting antique communities, dealers, and collectors.

Leverage social media, influencer marketing, and partnerships with antique experts or bloggers.

5.5. Phase 5: Post-Launch Support & Iteration (Ongoing)

Address user feedback and continuously improve the app.

Add additional features, such as advanced search filters, personalized recommendations, and a loyalty program for top sellers.

Regular updates with new antiques, educational content, and community events.

6. Marketing Strategy:

Community Engagement:

Create a community of antique enthusiasts through social media platforms, online forums, and partnerships with influencers in the antique market.

Content Marketing:

Publish educational content about antique collecting, history, and care to drive organic traffic to the app.

Paid Campaigns:

Paid advertising through Google, Facebook, Instagram, and influencer collaborations targeting antique lovers.

Referral Program:

Implement a referral program where users can earn benefits (e.g., discounts, premium membership) for bringing in new users.

7. Monetization Strategy:

Transaction Fees:

Charge a small fee on each successful transaction (purchase or trade).

Subscription Models:

Premium accounts for professional dealers and users who want additional features (e.g., advanced analytics, higher visibility).

Advertisement:

Allow non-intrusive ads for antique-related products or services within the app.

Commission on Valuations:

Take a small commission for any valuation or authentication services requested through the platform.

8. Future Features:

Augmented Reality (AR):

AR feature to allow users to visualize antiques in their homes before purchasing.

Global Expansion:

Localized versions of the app for different languages and countries to facilitate international trades.

Auction System:

A feature allowing users to auction rare or valuable items to the highest bidder.

9. Conclusion:

The "Refer" app will revolutionize the way antiques are bought, sold, and exchanged by providing a secure, accessible, and community-oriented platform for collectors and dealers. With a focus on user-friendly design, educational resources, and secure transactions, the app will create an unparalleled experience for antique enthusiasts. The ongoing development, community engagement, and adaptation of new technologies will ensure long-term success and growth.

robo.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. • “Safe to explore”
• “Proceed with caution”
• “Likely rug — avoid”

 • Users can input a token address to instantly scan it.
 • Example: “Scan this contract: 0x123…”

Purpose:
RugChecker helps users avoid scams by providing transparent, quick, and simple smart contract analysis on Base.

Style:
Clear, direct, safety-first.

salar.title: 2048 Mini App
salar.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

seta.title: SETA - T-Shirt Swap
seta.prompt:
Project Plan for the Mini-App “SETA”
1. Concept Overview

SETA is a mini-application that allows users to exchange T-shirts with creative and unique prints. The goal is to build a simple, user-friendly platform where people can upload their items, browse offers, and request swaps.

2. Key Features
2.1 User Accounts

Email or social media login (Google, Facebook).

User profile with:

Username

Avatar

Location (optional)

List of available T-shirts for exchange

Swap history

2.2 T-Shirt Listing System

Upload photos of T-shirts (front, back).

Add details:

Size

Material

Condition

Print description

Tag system (e.g., “vintage”, “anime”, “graphic art”).

2.3 Swapping Mechanism

Browse available T-shirts by:

Size

Category

Style

Location

“Request Swap” feature:

Send a swap offer with one or several T-shirts.

Built-in chat to discuss details.

Users can accept or decline swap offers.

2.4 In-App Chat

Simple messaging system between users.

Image sharing for clarification.

Notifications for messages and swap requests.

2.5 Rating & Verification

After each swap, users can rate each other.

Optional identity verification to improve trust.

2.6 Admin Dashboard (for SETA team)

Manage reported users or listings.

Approve or remove inappropriate content.

View statistics (active users, swaps, listings).

3. Design Requirements

Minimalistic UI with a modern and clean look.

Color palette: soft pastels or earth tones (to reflect creative fashion culture).

Intuitive navigation with large visuals for T-shirts.

Mobile-first design.

4. Technology Stack
Frontend

React / React Native (for mobile)

Tailwind CSS or custom styling

Responsive UI components

Backend

Node.js + Express

RESTful API

Database

MongoDB or PostgreSQL

Other Tools

Firebase (for authentication, storage, and notifications)

Cloudinary (for fast image uploading)

5. Development Stages
Stage 1: Planning

Define core features.

Create wireframes and UI mockups.

Choose platform (web, mobile, or both).

Stage 2: Design

UX/UI design for all screens:

Home feed

Listing page

User profile

Swap request page

Chat

Stage 3: Development

Frontend development of UI components.

Backend development of:

Database structure

API endpoints

Authentication system

Integration of chat and image upload features.

Stage 4: Testing

User testing for UI/UX.

Fixing bugs.

Stress testing for image uploads and chat.

Stage 5: Launch

Release beta version to a small group.

Collect feedback.

Public launch.

6. Marketing Strategy

Social media campaigns (Instagram, TikTok).

Collaboration with local artists to create custom prints.

Referral program (invite friends to earn exclusive designs).

Partnership with eco-friendly fashion brands.

7. Monetization Options

Featured listings (pay to boost visibility).

Small service fee for premium swap features.

Selling limited SETA-branded T-shirts.

Ads (optional, non-intrusive).

shill2earn.title: 2048 Mini App
shill2earn.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

shoose.title: Shoose \u2013 Shoe Exchange App
shoose.prompt:
Project Plan for Mini Application “Shoose”
1. Project Overview

Shoose is a mini mobile application that allows users to exchange shoes with each other. Users can upload shoes they want to trade, browse available shoes from others, and arrange exchanges.

2. Main Goals

Create a simple and user-friendly shoe-exchange platform.

Allow users to upload shoe photos and descriptions.

Enable browsing, searching, and filtering of available shoes.

Provide in-app messaging for users to negotiate exchanges.

Ensure safety and verification of user accounts.

3. Target Audience

Sneaker enthusiasts

People who want to trade instead of buying new items

Eco-friendly and sustainable fashion fans

Students and young adults

4. Core Features
4.1. User Features

User registration/login (email, Google, or social login)

User profile with shoe size, style preferences

Uploading shoes (photos, size, brand, condition, location)

Browsing and filtering (size, style, gender, brand, condition)

Wishlist & bookmarks

In-app chat for negotiating trades

Rating system after completed exchange

4.2. Admin Features

Manage users and listings

Content moderation

Handling reports and disputes

Analytics dashboard

5. Application Flow

User signs up or logs in

Sets shoe details and personal preferences

Uploads shoes available for exchange

Browses other users’ shoes

Initiates a chat to negotiate a trade

Confirms exchange and leaves feedback

6. Technical Stack
Frontend:

React Native or Flutter (cross-platform mobile development)

Backend:

Node.js (Express) or Django

REST API or GraphQL API

Database:

Firebase or MongoDB

Cloud Storage:

Firebase Storage / AWS S3 for photos

Authentication:

Firebase Auth or OAuth2

7. UI/UX Design Plan

Simple, clean interface with minimal steps

Home feed with cards showing available shoes

Photo-first design (like a small marketplace)

Easy upload flow

Dark and light theme options

Week 1–2: Planning & Design

Requirements gathering

Wireframes and UI/UX design

Database schema design

Week 3–4: Frontend & Backend Development

Build authentication

Create shoe upload system

Implement home feed and search

Week 5: Chat & User Profiles

Real-time messaging

Profile pages

Ratings and reviews

Week 6: Testing

Bug fixing

UI polishing

Performance optimization

Week 7–8: Launch

Deployment

App Store / Google Play preparation

User onboarding materials

9. Future Improvements

AI-based size matching

Advanced search and recommendations

Push notifications

Location-based matching

Premium features (boosted listings, highlights)

simple-risk-journal.title: Simple Risk Journal
simple-risk-journal.prompt:
Title: Simple Risk Journal

Description:
Create a simple app that allows users to record and review their daily trading or investment risk notes. The app should work entirely offline, without the internet or external APIs. All entries are added manually by the user.

Functionality:
 • Display an input field labeled “Risk Note” where the user can type a new journal entry.
 • Add a button labeled “Add Entry” that adds the written note to a visible list below.
 • Below the input, show a section titled “Your Risk Journal” displaying all saved notes in order.
 • Each entry should include a small “Delete” button allowing the user to remove that specific note.
 • Add a “Clear All” button that removes every entry from the journal at once.
 • If the user tries to add an empty note, show a message:
“Please enter a note before adding.”

UI Requirements:
 • Use only basic interface elements: text fields, buttons, and a list.
 • Keep the layout clean and easy to understand.
 • All interactions must update instantly and locally within the app.

slipguard.prompt:
Idea: A slippage estimator for both CEX and DEX trades.
User goal: Know how much slippage to expect before executing a large order.
Core features (MVP):

* Input: pair, side (buy/sell), order size.
* Pull current order book (CEX) or quote (DEX aggregator).
* Calculate expected average fill price and slippage vs. mid-price.
* Display slippage in % and absolute value.

Development plan:

1. Integrate one CEX order book API and one DEX aggregator API (e.g., 1inch, 0x).
2. Implement slippage calculation based on depth and order size.
3. Create a simple form-based UI with results panel.
4. Add presets for common order sizes (small/medium/large).
5. Optional: history log so users can compare past estimates vs. real fills.

slots-base.title: Fruit Slot Machine
slots-base.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

smartcontractaudit.prompt:
Description:
Smart Contract Audit Checker helps users quickly assess the security of smart contracts. Detect potential vulnerabilities, review risk metrics, and make informed decisions before interacting with new DeFi projects or tokens.

Key Features:
 • Automatic analysis of smart contract code for common vulnerabilities.
 • Risk scoring and alerts for potentially unsafe contracts.
 • Supports ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155, and other standards.
 • Historical audit summaries for known contracts.
 • Multi-chain support for Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, and others.

Target Users:
Crypto investors, DeFi participants, NFT traders, and developers who want to evaluate contract safety before engagement.

Usage Instructions:
 1. Enter the smart contract address.
 2. View risk assessment and detected vulnerabilities.
 3. Set alerts for updates or changes to the contract.
 4. Use insights to decide whether to interact with the contract.

Benefits:
 • Reduce risk when interacting with new contracts.
 • Quickly identify potentially unsafe or malicious code.
 • Make informed, data-driven decisions in DeFi and NFT ecosystems.

spin-and-win.title: 2048 Mini App
spin-and-win.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

st.title: USDT Trailing Stop (KuCoin Feed)
st.prompt:
App Name: USDT Trailing Stop (KuCoin Feed)

Description:
A trailing stop app for USDT using real-time price data from KuCoin. Users set a starting price and trailing range, and the app automatically adjusts stop levels to protect profits and minimize losses.

Features:

Real-time USDT price feed from KuCoin.

Set starting price and trailing range in USDT.

Automatic stop level adjustment as price moves.

Alerts when stop levels are reached.

Designed for traders to protect profits and limit losses.


How It Works:

1. User enters starting price and trailing range.


2. The app continuously fetches USDT price from KuCoin.


3. If price rises, the stop level moves up according to the trailing range.


4. If price falls to the stop level, the app triggers an alert or execution.

Optional rarity-based filtering.

Basic editor for uploading custom sticker images.

Crop/resize tools.

Moderation queue for approval.

2.6. Social Features

Friend list and search by username or QR code.

Activity feed showing recent trades.

2.7. Mini-App Optimization

Fast loading.

Lightweight data usage.

Adaptive UI for mobile screens.

3. Technical Architecture
3.1. Frontend

Framework: React / Vue / Flutter Web / Mini-App native framework.

UI library: TailwindCSS / Material UI.

Key components:

Sticker Gallery

Trade Panel

Chat/Inbox

Profile Page

Notifications

3.2. Backend

Node.js / Python / Go.

REST API or GraphQL.

Real-time communication: WebSockets or Firebase.

Services:

Authentication Service

Sticker Management Service

Trade Service

Notification Service

3.3. Database

MongoDB or PostgreSQL.

Collections/Tables:

Users

Stickers

Trades

Messages/Notifications

3.4. Storage

Cloud storage for sticker images (AWS S3, Firebase Storage).

4. Design & UX
4.1. Style

Playful, bright colors.

Smooth animations.

Rounded elements.

4.2. Screens

Home screen (Sticker feed)

My Stickers

Friends & Search

Trade menu

Settings / Profile

5. Development Roadmap
Phase 1 – MVP (4–6 weeks)

User authentication

Basic sticker gallery

Sending stickers to friends

Receiving stickers + notifications

Simple UI

Phase 2 – Enhanced Features (6–8 weeks)

Trading system

User search + friend list

More advanced sticker filtering

Backend optimizations

Phase 3 – Advanced (Optional)

Sticker creation tool

Marketplace for rare stickers

Social feed

Analytics dashboard

6. Testing

Unit tests for API and UI components.

Usability testing.

Load testing for real-time features.

7. Deployment

Backend: Deploy on cloud (AWS / Google Cloud / Render).

Frontend: Deploy to hosting or mini-app environment.

CDN for faster sticker loading.

8. Monetization Ideas

Paid premium sticker packs.

Subscription for exclusive collections.

In-app ads (optional).

Creator marketplace fees (optional).

sudoku.title: Sudoku Mini App
sudoku.prompt:
create a sudoku game Sudoku Puzzle Generation Logic

A valid, playable Sudoku puzzle cannot be generated simply by placing random numbers on the board. It requires a two-step process: first, creating a complete, solved board, and second, strategically removing numbers to ensure the remaining puzzle has only one unique solution.

This logic is best implemented using a Backtracking Algorithm.

Phase 1: Generating a Complete, Valid Board

The goal of this phase is to create a 9x9 grid where every row, column, and 3x3 box contains the numbers 1 through 9 exactly once.

Step 1.1: The Backtracking Solver Function

Create a recursive function, often called solve() or fillGrid(), that takes the current board state and the current cell coordinates (row, col) as input.

Base Case: If the entire grid is filled (i.e., you successfully moved past the last cell (8, 8)), the board is complete and valid. Return True.

task-manager-for-traders.prompt:
Task Manager for Traders — App Description

Create a simple mini app called “Task Manager for Traders”.
The app helps crypto traders organize their daily tasks by manually adding, marking, and removing items.
No internet access or external integrations are required.

Core Features
 1. A text input field where the user can type a task (e.g., “Review charts”, “Check portfolio”, “Set alerts”).
 2. A dropdown menu to set a priority level:
 • High
 • Medium
 • Low
 3. A button “Add Task” that saves the task to a visible list.
 4. A task list showing:
 • Task name
 • Priority level
 • Status (Pending / Completed)
 5. Each task should include:
 • A “Mark as Completed” button that changes its status
 • An “Edit Task” button to modify the text or priority
 • A “Delete” button to remove the task

How the App Should Work
 • User enters a task and selects a priority.
 • Presses “Add Task”, and the task appears in the list.
 • User can update the task text or its priority via the edit button.
 • User can mark a task as completed with one click.
 • User can delete tasks at any time.
 • All data is stored locally within the app session.

UI Requirements
 • Inputs at the top for quick task creation.
 • Task list displayed below in a clean table or card layout.
 • Completed tasks should show a simple visual indicator (e.g., “Completed” label).
 • No external data, no API calls, no Web3 interactions.

Goal of the App

Provide traders with a clean, minimal tool to manage their daily activities and stay organized without relying on external data sources.

testermitch.title: 2048 Mini App
testermitch.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

tini.title: TaxMate: Multi\u2011Country Tax Estimator
tini.prompt:
Create an app that does taxes for US, Canada and European countries.
Upload your payslips, forms, receipts or full tax return PDFs — the app reads them, matches fields to your country’s rules, and gives a clear, explainable estimate of tax due or refund, plus a checklist of actions to maximize return.”

Secure user accounts + encrypted storage (optional client-side encryption).

Upload: PDF, images, screenshots, email receipts.

OCR & document classification (paystub, invoice, W-2 / T4, 1099, local equivalents).

Field extraction (income, tax withheld, deductions, dependents).

Country selector + currency detection.

Rule engine: apply country-specific tax tables & basic credits to compute tax owed/refund estimate.

Simple results screen: taxable income, tax owed/refund estimate, assumptions, confidence score.

Exportable summary PDF and CSV.

Automatic document matching to tax forms (e.g., US W-2, Canada T4, UK P60, Australia PAYG).

Multi-year comparisons and carry-forwards.

Integration with email (optional, with user consent) to auto-import receipts (Gmail API / IMAP).

Explainability: LLM-powered plain-English explanations of each line and suggested actions.

Refund tracking (notify if government processes refund).

Auto-fill native tax return for local e-filing (where legal).

Bank integrations to reconcile income.

Country-specific deeper rules (state/provincial taxes, social security, special credits).

Auditable logs and professional-grade export formats.

token-priority-list.title: Token Priority List
token-priority-list.prompt:
Token Priority List — App Description

Create a simple and clean mini app called “Token Priority List”.
This app should help users organize their tokens by assigning a priority level to each of them.

The app does not require internet access or external data.
All information is entered and stored locally inside the app session.

Core Features
 1. A text input field where the user can enter the name of a token.
 2. A dropdown menu with three priority options:
 • High
 • Medium
 • Low
 3. A button “Add Token” that adds the token and its selected priority to a visible list.
 4. A list section that displays all added tokens in a clean table or card layout:
 • Token name
 • Assigned priority
 5. Each item in the list must have a Delete button so users can remove tokens.
 6. No external API requests, no web3 actions, no internet access.

How the app should work
 • The user enters a token name, selects a priority level, and presses “Add Token”.
 • The token appears in the list with its chosen priority.
 • The user can delete any token from the list at any time.
 • The list updates immediately after every action.
 • Everything works offline using only internal app state.

User Interface Requirements
 • Simple, clean layout.
 • Inputs at the top, list below.
 • Clear labels for every field.
 • The app should be lightweight and responsive.

Goal of the app

Provide a minimal, easy-to-use tool where users can manually organize tokens by importance without requiring any external data sources.

Name: Small Token Analyzer
Purpose: Fast analysis of new, small-cap, or lesser-known tokens.
Deployment Description:
This mini app generates a structured token analysis based on publicly available information. The user enters a token name or ticker, and the bot returns a detailed breakdown: utility, tokenomics, unlock schedule, risks, competition, triggers for growth, and a risk warning.
No APIs required — the app acts as an intelligent analytical template.
Core Features:
At least 8 analytical categories: Utility, Tokenomics, Unlocks, Competitors, Risks, Stage, Potential, Risk Score
Checks exchange presence (based on known market data patterns, no API)
Provides a final rating (“high / medium / low risk”)
Supports user questions about the project
Deployment Instructions:
Deploy as an analytical mini-app with the main instruction:
“When the user enters a token or project name, return a structured analysis in the format: Overview → Token Utility → Tokenomics → Unlocks → Roadmap → Risks → Opportunities → Final Score.”

tokenbuybackmonitor.prompt:

tokensniper.title: Mini App Factory App
tokensniper.prompt:
App Name: TokenSniper

Description / Functions (paste this into Mini App Factory):

TokenSniper is a simple and fast mini app that scans newly created tokens on the Base network.
The app helps users discover fresh token launches and evaluate basic risk indicators before interacting with them.

Core Features:
 1. New Token Feed
 • Displays a list of tokens that were recently deployed on Base.
 • Shows deployment time and contract creation details.
 2. Basic Token Info
 • For each token, display:
• Total supply
• Contract creator
• Deployment timestamp
• Basic metadata (if available)
 3. Risk Assessment
 • Provide a simple risk evaluation: Low / Medium / High.
 • Base this assessment on factors like:
• Liquidity presence
• Contract age
• Is ownership renounced
• Any suspicious patterns
 4. User Tips
 • Offer safety advice for new tokens:
• “Always verify liquidity lock.”
• “Check if the contract owner still holds too many tokens.”
• “Avoid tokens with extremely low liquidity.”
 5. Simple Query Mode
 • Users can request more details about any token from the list.
 • Example: “Tell me more about Token #3.”

Purpose:
TokenSniper helps users quickly identify new tokens, understand basic risks, and avoid obvious scams on the Base network.

Style:
Clear, concise, helpful, beginner-friendly.

toyt.title: ToyT
toyt.prompt:
ToyT Mini-App Development Plan

Project Overview:
ToyT is a mobile application that enables users to exchange, sell, or donate children's toys. The platform connects parents, guardians, and caretakers who are looking to give away toys their children no longer use or seek new toys at no or low cost. The app fosters a sustainable approach to toy use while promoting community engagement.

1. Market Research & User Analysis

Target Audience:

Parents and guardians of children (aged 0-10 years)

Community-based organizations or local charities focused on children

Environmental-conscious individuals looking to reuse toys

Competitor Analysis:

Investigate existing platforms for toy sharing (e.g., Facebook Marketplace, local charity swap groups, etc.)

Identify key features, gaps, and areas for improvement

2. Features & Functionalities

Core Features:

User Registration/Login:

Sign-up via email, social media accounts, or phone number.

Basic profile (name, age of child, location).

Toy Listings:

Add Toy: Users can add toys they want to exchange or donate with a photo, description, and condition (new, used, lightly used).

Categories: Toys can be listed by categories such as Age Group, Toy Type (e.g., educational, dolls, outdoor toys), Condition, etc.

Search & Filter: Users can search for toys based on categories, condition, and location.

Toy Exchange Mechanism:

Swap Option: Users can choose to exchange their toy for another toy. The system suggests potential swaps based on similar age group or toy type.

Buy/Donate Option: If users are not interested in swapping, they can donate the toy or sell it directly.

Location-based Matching:

Toy listings and requests are filtered based on user location (zip code, city, etc.) to ensure local exchanges and deliveries.

Rating & Reviews:

Users can rate each other based on the exchange experience to build trust within the community.

Messaging System:

A built-in chat function for users to communicate directly about exchanges, donations, or sales.

Safety Features:

Identity Verification: Ensure that users are real individuals (through social media logins or phone number verification).

Toy Condition Verification: Users can upload a photo/video to prove the condition of the toy before listing.

Additional Features:

Event Listings: Organize community toy exchange events or drives.

Push Notifications: Notify users of new listings, successful exchanges, or updates from potential buyers/sellers.

Wishlist: Users can create a wishlist of toys they are looking for or interested in exchanging.

3. Design & User Interface (UI/UX)

Simple, Intuitive Design:

Focus on clean design with easy-to-navigate pages.

Minimalistic UI to make the process of listing and searching for toys seamless.

Interactive Elements:

Swipeable cards for toy listings.

Easy-to-use filters and search bar at the top of the main page.

Visual Appeal:

Bright, playful colors to appeal to parents and children.

High-quality images of toys to ensure trust in the listings.

4. Technology Stack

Frontend:

React Native (for cross-platform mobile app development)

Expo for rapid development and testing

Backend:

Node.js with Express for API development

MongoDB for storing user data, toy listings, reviews, etc.

Authentication:

Firebase Authentication or OAuth for easy user login and registration.

Geolocation Services:

Google Maps API for location-based toy listings and delivery options.

Push Notifications:

Firebase Cloud Messaging for push notifications to users.

5. Development Phases

Phase 1: Planning & Prototyping (2-3 Weeks)

Define the full scope of features.

Create wireframes and prototypes (using tools like Figma or Adobe XD).

Gather feedback from potential users (focus groups, surveys).

Phase 2: Frontend & Backend Development (4-5 Weeks)

Develop the core functionalities: User sign-up/login, toy listing, search & filter, messaging system.

Set up database and backend for handling user data and toy listings.

Implement the design and ensure user-friendly navigation.

Phase 3: Testing (2 Weeks)

Conduct usability testing on different devices (Android/iOS).

Test app functionalities (registration, toy listings, exchange mechanism).

Collect feedback from testers and refine the app based on input.

Phase 4: Launch & Marketing (1 Week)

Launch the app on Google Play and the Apple App Store.

Create a marketing strategy (social media, local advertising, influencer partnerships).

Offer initial incentives for new users (e.g., free toy listings or premium features).

Phase 5: Post-Launch Support (Ongoing)

Monitor app performance (user engagement, issues, crashes).

Fix bugs and update features based on user feedback.

Consider adding premium features (e.g., highlighted listings, paid advertising).

6. Monetization Strategy

Freemium Model:

Free app download with basic functionality (toy exchange, donation, search).

Premium features like highlighted listings, faster messaging, or unlimited wishlist items for a subscription fee.

Advertisement:

Display ads within the app (non-intrusive).

Sponsored toy listings or promotions for toy brands.

Transaction Fees:

A small fee for transactions involving the sale of toys (e.g., 2-3% per sale).

7. Future Enhancements

Integration with Delivery Services: Partner with local couriers to offer easy delivery of exchanged or sold toys.

Gamification: Implement rewards or badges for users who complete a certain number of successful exchanges or donations.

Social Sharing: Allow users to share listings or exchanges on social media platforms like Facebook or Instagram to increase engagement.

8. Conclusion

The ToyT app has the potential to build a strong community focused on sustainable living by allowing families to share toys, reduce waste, and save money. With thoughtful design, a user-friendly interface, and key features tailored to the needs of parents and guardians, ToyT could become a go-to app for children’s toy exchange.

tradingjournalanalytics.title: Trading Journal & Analytics
tradingjournalanalytics.prompt:
Name: Trading Journal & Analytics
Purpose: A personal trading journal with automatic calculations and performance analytics.
Deployment Description:
This mini app allows traders to quickly log their trades and automatically receive performance statistics. The user enters trade type, pair, position size, entry/exit price, and comments. The bot stores the journal, calculates PnL, win rate, average profit/loss, and generates summaries for any period (daily, weekly, monthly).
No external APIs required — all data is stored locally in the conversation memory.
Core Features:
Add trades to the journal
Automatic PnL calculations
Generate performance stats (win rate, average P/L, drawdown)
Create summary reports by time period
Deployment Instructions:
Deploy as a text-based utility in Mini App Factory with these commands:
/add trade — add a new trade
/stats — show statistics
/reset journal — clear all saved trades

trendy.title: Trendy \u2014 Web3 Mini Social App with TRND Rewards
trendy.prompt:
**Title:** Trendy — Web3 Mini Social App with TRND Rewards

**Description:**
Trendy is a simple Web3-powered social mini app built on Base Network. Users log in with their wallet, create posts, like posts, comment, share content, and earn TRND tokens as rewards. The TRND token has a total supply of 1,000,000,000 (1 billion). The owner holds 300,000,000 TRND, and the remaining 700,000,000 TRND are reserved as user rewards distributed through the Trendy app.

---

## **Core Requirements (Simple Version)**

---

### **1. Wallet Login**

* Enable wallet login for Base & Ethereum networks.
* Users must connect their wallet before posting, liking, commenting, or sharing.

---

### **2. Home Feed (Social Posting)**

Display a scrolling feed of user posts sorted by newest first.
Each post must show:

* wallet address (shortened)
* text (max 200 characters)
* optional image upload
* like count
* comment count
* share count
* timestamp

---

### **3. Create Post**

Form fields:

* text (200 characters max)
* optional image

After submitting:

* Add the post to the feed
* Reward the user **1 TRND** from the reward pool (700M supply)

---

### **4. Like System**

* Users can like any post
* Limit: 1 like per user per post
* When a post receives a like:

  * Post owner receives **0.1 TRND** reward
  * Deduct this from the 700M reward pool

---

### **5. Comment System**

* Users can comment on any post

* Comment fields:

  * wallet address
  * text (max 120 characters)
  * timestamp

* When a post receives a comment:

  * Post owner earns **0.2 TRND** reward
  * Deduct from the 700M reward pool

Comments appear below each post on a modal or expanded view.

---

### **6. Share System**

User can click “Share” on a post.
Sharing creates:

* A re-post that includes:

  * Original post preview
  * “Shared by: [wallet]”
  * New timestamp
* Count share +1

Reward:

* Post owner earns **0.5 TRND** per share
* Deduct from reward pool

---

### **7. Profile Page**

Profile must show:

* connected wallet address
* total posts
* total likes received
* total comments received
* total shares received
* total TRND earned
* "Withdraw TRND" button

---

### **8. Withdraw TRND**

* Implement a withdraw system that sends TRND from the reward supply wallet to the user’s wallet
* Only send what the user has earned
* Ensure withdraw uses Base chain (low gas)

---

### **9. TRND Token Deployment**

Deploy TRND as an ERC-20 token on Base with:

* **Name:** Trendy Token
* **Symbol:** TRND
* **Total Supply:** 1,000,000,000 TRND
* **Owner allocation:** 300,000,000 TRND
* **Reward pool:** 700,000,000 TRND
* Reward pool must be used for:

  * posting rewards
  * likes
  * comments
  * shares

---

### **10. Reward Logic Summary**

Reward distribution from 700M pool:

* **Post:** 1 TRND
* **Like:** 0.1 TRND
* **Comment:** 0.2 TRND
* **Share:** 0.5 TRND

Stop distribution automatically when reward pool runs out.

---

### **11. UI Layout (Simple & Clean)**

Pages:

1. **Home Feed**
2. **Create Post**
3. **Profile**

Every post must include buttons:

* Like
* Comment
* Share

---

### **12. General Notes**

* Keep it lightweight and fast to meet Mini App Factory approval standards.
* No need for complex media features.
* No need for messaging or DMs.
* Focus on:

  * posting
  * liking
  * commenting
  * sharing
  * reward distribution
  * withdraw

tt.title: 2048 Mini App
tt.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

ttrade.title: TTrade - Furniture Exchange App
ttrade.prompt:
TTrade - Furniture Exchange App Plan
1. Concept Overview

TTrade is a mobile app designed to allow users to exchange, sell, or donate old furniture. The platform connects people who want to get rid of their old furniture with others who are looking for affordable, second-hand pieces. It focuses on sustainability, reducing waste, and promoting the reuse of items in local communities.

2. Target Audience

Primary Users: People looking to buy, sell, or donate old furniture.

Secondary Users: Charities, local organizations, and thrift shops that accept furniture donations.

3. Key Features
User Account System

Sign up/Login: Users can sign up via email, phone number, or social media accounts.

Profile Creation: Users can create and manage profiles with personal details, preferences, and location.

Furniture Listings

Create Listing: Users can post furniture items with photos, descriptions, and condition of the item.

Category selection: Sofa, Table, Chairs, etc.

Option to set price (if selling) or mark as free (for donations).

Option to upload multiple photos and provide dimensions or measurements.

Search & Filter

Search: Users can search for specific items based on keywords (e.g., "couch," "wooden table").

Filters: Filters based on category, price, location, condition, and item type (for sale or free).

Location-based Search: Maps integration to find nearby items based on the user’s location.

Communication & Negotiation

Messaging: Direct messaging system between buyers and sellers/donors.

Offers: Option for buyers to make an offer or negotiate price.

Transaction & Exchange

Pickup/Delivery Options: Users can arrange delivery or pickup for exchanged furniture.

Ratings and Reviews: After each transaction, users can rate the quality and condition of the items and the transaction experience.

Donation Feature

Charity Donation: Option for users to donate items to registered charities. This can be facilitated by nonprofit partners.

In-App Notifications

New Listing Alerts: Users receive notifications when new items are listed in their area or category of interest.

Messages & Offers: Notifications when they receive messages or offers related to their posted furniture.

User Authentication & Security

Secure Login: Email and password protection, possibly with two-factor authentication.

Verification: Option for verifying user profiles (especially for sellers), which adds credibility to the listings.

4. Technical Requirements
Platform

Mobile App: Available for iOS and Android devices.

Web Version: Optional website for users who prefer browsing on a desktop.

Technology Stack

Frontend:

React Native or Flutter for cross-platform mobile app development.

React.js for the web version (if applicable).

Backend:

Node.js with Express for server-side logic.

MongoDB or Firebase for real-time database and user data management.

Authentication:

Firebase Authentication or OAuth for secure user sign-in.

Cloud Storage:

Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage for storing images of listed furniture.

Push Notifications:

Firebase Cloud Messaging for sending alerts and updates to users.

5. Design & UI/UX
User Interface Design

Simple & Intuitive: The design should be easy to navigate, with a clean, modern look.

Profile & Listings Screens: Clear and simple design with large images, essential details, and easy-to-read typography.

Search & Filter Features: Prominently placed, with minimalistic icons and quick search results.

Messaging Interface: User-friendly chat with options for quick responses.

User Experience

Fast Load Times: Optimize images and app functionality for minimal wait time.

Ease of Use: The app should be user-friendly for people of all ages, including those who may not be tech-savvy.

6. Monetization Strategy

Freemium Model: Basic usage of the app is free. Premium features (like featured listings or priority visibility) are available for a fee.

Advertising: Display ads from local moving companies or furniture-related services.

Transaction Fee: A small percentage fee could be charged on each transaction (only if the user is selling).

7. Marketing & Launch
Pre-launch Marketing

Social Media Campaign: Create social media accounts and start building an online community.

Website: A landing page with information about the app, how it works, and early sign-up options.

Launch Strategy

App Store Optimization (ASO): Optimize the app description and screenshots on Google Play Store and Apple App Store for visibility.

Partnerships: Collaborate with local moving companies, charities, and influencers to boost app awareness.

8. Development Timeline

Phase 1: Research & Planning (2-4 weeks)

Market research, feature list creation, and initial design mockups.

Phase 2: Design & Prototyping (4-6 weeks)

UI/UX design, wireframing, and prototyping.

Phase 3: Development (8-12 weeks)

Backend and frontend development.

User authentication, database, and messaging system setup.

Phase 4: Testing (3-4 weeks)

Alpha testing, bug fixing, and feedback incorporation.

Phase 5: Launch & Marketing (4 weeks)

Prepare for launch on app stores and social media promotion.

9. Maintenance & Updates

Regular Bug Fixes: Continuous improvement and bug fixing based on user feedback.

Feature Updates: Regular release of new features or improvements based on user requests.

ultra-mini-golf.title: Mini Golf Platformer
ultra-mini-golf.prompt:
Create a complete, ready-to-play 2D mini-golf platformer game for Farcaster (Warpcast frames) using HTML5 + JavaScript (Phaser 3 or PixiJS v7+ is preferred, but pure Canvas is acceptable if it keeps the total size small).

Core requirements:

1. Game type: 2D side view mini-golf (like classic mini-golf but with platformer physics: gravity, bounce, ramps, moving platforms, wind zones, etc.).
2. Multiplayer: 1 human player vs 3 AI-controlled bots (4 players total). Show all 4 balls on screen at the same time with different colors (human = yellow, bot1 = red, bot2 = blue, bot3 = green).
3. Course generation: Every game the entire course (hole) must be 100% procedurally generated and always solvable (the ball must have a physically possible path to the hole with ≤ 20 strokes max). 
   - Screen size: 800 × 600 px (standard Frame size).
   - Start tee on the left side, hole on the right side.
   - Terrain: generate a smooth but wavy ground made of multiple quadratic/cubic Bézier segments or physics polygons.
   - Obstacles (randomly choose 4–7 of the following, never blocking the hole):
     - Static bumps and ramps
     - Moving platforms (horizontal or vertical)
     - Wind zones (left/right arrows that apply constant force)
     - Bounce pads (high restitution)
     - Water hazards (instant respawn at last safe position if touched)
     - Teleporters (pair of portals)
     - Spikes (same as water)
     - Rotating windmills or gates
   - Par is randomly between 3 and 6.
   - The generator must run a quick physics simulation or A* pathfinding check at generation time to guarantee solvability before showing the level to the player.

4. Controls (Farcaster Frame compatible):
   - Tap/click and drag from the ball to set direction and power (classic golf swing meter style: line with arrow + power bar).
   - Release to shoot.
   - One single HTML file + inline JS/CSS (no external assets except Google fonts if needed). Total size < 300 KB so it loads instantly in Frames.

5. Turn order:
   - Players take turns in fixed order (human first, then bot1, bot2, bot3).
   - After all 4 have holed out, show final leaderboard with strokes for this hole and “Next hole” button (new random course).

6. AI bots:
   - Simple but believable: pre-calculate a reasonable path using basic physics prediction (simulate 6–8 bounces ahead) and aim slightly off perfect trajectory (add 2–8% random error) so they sometimes miss but usually score close to par.

7. Visual style:
   - Bright, cartoonish mini-golf aesthetic.
   - Grass texture background, simple shadows under balls.
   - Hole is a classic black cup with flag.
   - Particle effect + sound (use Web Audio beep or short base64 sound) on hole-in.

8. Scoring & UI:
   - Current player highlight.
   - Stroke counter per player.
   - Small leaderboard top-right.
   - “Share on Warpcast” button when the hole ends.

9. Technical constraints for Farcaster Frames:
   - Must work as a single static HTML file hosted on a CDN.
   - Use only inline data URIs for tiny sprites/sounds if needed.
   - Must start instantly when the Frame is opened (no loading screen longer than 1 second).
   - Include the necessary <meta> tags for Frame validation (og:title, og:image preview of a sample hole, fc:frame buttons: “Swing!” and later “Next hole”).

unitown.title: Fruit Slot Machine App
unitown.prompt:
A slot machine with 3 columns and 3 rows, each slot contains one fruit. The fruits should be: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Lemon. Generate an vector style image with white background for each fruit and use it to display that fruit. The fruits should be spawned by the machine at random. The user can press the spin button, which will trigger a spinning animation that moves the columns downward, spawning new fruit at the top repeatedly for 2 seconds. If there are 3 of the same fruit in any row or column at any time while not spinning, display a win message to the user, which they can share on their feed. Check the win condition directly using a conditional render instead of calculating it in a function. The user should always be able to spin again, except while the spinning animation is in progress.

Place the slot machine to the home page.

vas1825.title: 2048 Mini App
vas1825.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

videx.prompt:
Videx – Mini Video-Sharing App Development Plan
1. Project Overview

Videx is a lightweight video-sharing application that allows users to upload, watch, like, and share short videos. The app focuses on simplicity, speed, and a clean user experience.

2. Core Features
MVP (Minimum Viable Product)

User Registration & Login

Email/password or social login (Google/Apple).

Video Upload

Upload short videos (up to 60 seconds).

Basic compression and format validation.

Video Feed

Infinite scroll feed of videos.

Auto-play on scroll.

User Interactions

Like, comment, share.

User Profiles

Profile photo, username, uploaded videos.

Search

Search by username or tags.

Basic Notifications

New likes or comments.

Future Enhancements

Video editing tools (trim, filters, music).

Live streaming.

Private messaging.

AI-generated recommendations.

3. Tech Stack
Frontend

React Native or Flutter for mobile app

UI library: React Native Paper, Tailwind, or Material UI

Backend

Node.js + Express or NestJS

REST API or GraphQL

Database

MongoDB or PostgreSQL

Storage

Cloud storage for videos: AWS S3, Firebase Storage, or Cloudflare R2

Authentication

Firebase Auth or Auth0

Deployment

Backend: AWS / Vercel / Render

Mobile app: Google Play & App Store

4. System Architecture (High-Level)

Mobile App sends requests to the backend API.

Backend API handles:

authentication

video metadata

likes/comments

Cloud Storage stores the video files themselves.

CDN accelerates video delivery.

Database stores user data, video metadata, interactions.

5. Development Phases
Phase 1 – Planning

Define requirements & use cases.

Create wireframes and UI mockups.

Approve architecture.

Phase 2 – Backend Development

Create API structure.

Implement registration/login.

Add video upload endpoint.

Integrate cloud storage.

Phase 3 – Frontend Development

Build navigation.

Create login screen.

Create video upload UI.

Create home feed.

Add profile screens.

Phase 4 – Integration

Connect frontend with backend API.

Test upload, playback, interactions.

Phase 5 – Testing

Unit tests.

Performance tests (especially video streaming).

Bug fixing.

Phase 6 – Launch

Publish on app stores.

Prepare marketing assets.

Monitor app performance.

6. Monetization Options

In-app ads (rewarded or interstitial).

Premium subscription (no ads, extra features).

Paid filters/effects.

Brand partnerships.

7. Success Metrics (KPIs)

Daily/Monthly Active Users.

Number of uploaded videos.

Engagement (likes, comments).

Average watch time.

Retention rate (Day 1 / Day 7 / Day 30).

voice-pinter.title: Pinterest Voice Search
voice-pinter.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS): Voice Search Application for Pinterest
1. Project Overview

You must develop a mobile application that enables users to search Pinterest content using voice commands.
The system must convert spoken input into keywords, send search queries to Pinterest, retrieve results, and display them in a clean, user-friendly interface.

The app must function as a Pinterest voice-powered search engine, supporting visual inspiration discovery through speech.

2. Core Objectives

Enable accurate voice-to-text recognition for search queries.

Convert spoken phrases into Pinterest-compatible search terms.

Retrieve and display Pinterest images, pins, boards, and profiles.

Provide fast, intuitive, and hands-free browsing.

Support multiple languages (initially English, optional language pack support).

3. Key Features (Mandatory)
3.1 Voice Input

The application must:

Use system-level voice recognition (Google Speech API / Apple Speech Framework) or custom ASR.

Start recording with a single tap or voice trigger (e.g., “Search”).

Convert speech to text in real time.

Handle unclear queries through fallback suggestions.

3.2 Pinterest Search Integration

The application must:

Use Pinterest API (official) or web-scraping fallback if required.

Support search categories:

Pins

Boards

Users

Topics / Ideas

Display search results with thumbnails and titles.

Allow users to open and view full pin details.

3.3 Search Optimization

The system must:

Clean and optimize the recognized text.

Suggest relevant keywords.

Handle long or descriptive voice prompts (e.g., “minimalist home office ideas with wood accents”).

3.4 User Interface

The UI must include:

Microphone button (start/stop recording)

Search bar with auto-filled voice text

Results grid styled similar to Pinterest

Pin preview screen

Saved searches section

3.5 History & Saved Searches

The app must:

Store recent voice searches locally

Allow users to re-run previous searches

Provide optional cloud sync (if registered account)

3.6 Additional Features

Dark/Light mode

Share pin externally

Smooth animations and image lazy-loading

Multi-language ASR support (optional)

4. System Architecture
4.1 Frontend

Framework: Flutter / React Native

Voice capture UI

Real-time transcription display

Grid layout for Pinterest results

4.2 Backend

(If Pinterest API requires server-side handling)

Backend must include:

Node.js or Python server

API wrapper for Pinterest search

Rate limiting and authentication

Caching layer for repeated queries

Logging for error tracking

If API access is direct from the app, backend can be minimal or optional.

4.3 Voice Processing

Google STT / Apple STT / Whisper API

Text cleaning algorithms

Keyword extractor (TF-IDF or simple NLP)

5. Performance Requirements

Voice-to-text latency: < 1 second

Search result load time: < 2 seconds

Smooth scrolling at 60 FPS

Handle at least 1000 searches/hour without crashes

6. Security Requirements

Secure connection using HTTPS

Token-based authentication with Pinterest

No permanent storage of raw audio

Comply with Pinterest API usage policies

7. Deliverables

Fully functioning mobile app (Android + iOS)

Source code with documentation

Backend service (if applicable)

UI/UX mockups

Test builds + QA reports

Deployment instructions for App Store & Google Play

8. Optional Monetization (If Needed)

Ads (Google AdMob)

Premium version with:

Unlimited search history

Faster API response

Voice triggers (hands-free mode)

Offline saved pins

voice123.title: Phantom Lens: Surreal Photo Explorer
voice123.prompt:
Technical Specification (TS) – Phantom Lens: Surreal Photo Explorer
1. Project Overview

Phantom Lens is a photo app where every snapshot is a portal to another dimension. Users capture, morph, and explore images that react to emotions, time, and randomness. Ordinary photography becomes surreal storytelling.

Purpose: Turn everyday photos into living, interactive art pieces that evolve unpredictably.

2. Functional Requirements
2.1 Capturing the Unseen

Take photos using the device camera.

Optional “mystery lens” mode: colors, shadows, and distortions change randomly.

Metadata includes emotion tag (happy, sad, eerie), timestamp, and “aura intensity” (AI-estimated mood).

2.2 Photo Morphing & Filters

Filters evolve dynamically based on:

Time of day

Weather

Nearby sounds or movement

Morphing options: liquid distortions, glitch echoes, dreamlike overlays.

AI-assisted surreal transformations: convert normal photo into something uncanny or abstract.

2.3 Photo Journals & Portals

Users create albums called “Portals”.

Photos in a portal react to each other: linking color schemes, moods, or themes.

Swipe through portals; photos animate slightly as if alive.

2.4 Search & Exploration

Search photos by:

Emotion aura

Dominant color

Filter type

Explore “random portals” created by other users (optional social feed).

2.5 Notifications & Surprises

“Photo whispers”: notifications when an old photo morphs overnight.

Daily prompts to capture an image matching a surreal theme.

2.6 Security & Privacy

Local storage for private portals.

Optional cloud sync with end-to-end encryption.

Permission management for camera, microphone, and location (for dynamic filters).

3. Non-Functional Requirements

Platform: Mobile iOS & Android

Performance: Morphing and filter previews render <1s for 1080p photos.

UI: Surreal, interactive interface with animated transitions.

Storage: Efficient caching for morphing data; offline use.

4. Technical Stack

Mobile Framework: Flutter or React Native

Local DB: SQLite, Realm, or Hive for portal metadata

AI & Effects: TensorFlow Lite / Core ML for emotion and surreal transformations

Optional Cloud: Firebase or AWS for multi-device sync

5. Future Enhancements

AI-generated “dream worlds” from photo combinations.

Interactive AR mode: portals extend into 3D space.

NFT integration: mint surreal images as unique digital assets.

Social exploration: discover and remix other users’ portals.

Gamification: achievements for rare photo morphs, streaks, or moods captured.
