walletscan.title: BaseWalletScan
walletscan.prompt:
# **📌 Prompt: Build “BaseWalletScan” Mini App (Web + Frame)**

Create a Farcaster Mini App + Web App called **BaseWalletScan**.
The app should auto-detect whether the user is inside Farcaster (Frame) or a regular browser.

### **🔐 1. Wallet Connection**

* Browser: support WalletConnect + Privy + injected wallets (MetaMask, Coinbase Wallet).
* Frame: use OnchainKit (BasePay) for signatures + wallet linking.
* Once connected, grab the user’s address and run a full analysis on **Base chain**.

---

# **📊 2. Wallet Activity Scanner (Base Chain Only)**

Pull and analyze data using:

* BaseScan API
* OnchainKit providers
* Optional: Flipside or Covalent if needed

Scan the last **10,000 blocks or last 12 months**, whichever is more complete.

Provide:

### **A. Activity Metrics**

* Total transactions
* Active days
* Inflows / Outflows
* Swap count
* Number of contracts interacted
* Gas used
* Failed transactions
* Total minting events
* Airdrops claimed
* Bridge activity (Base ⇆ L1/L2)

---

# **📈 3. Performance Metrics**

Compute:

* Total Volume (USD + ETH)
* Swap P&L (requires price-fetch at tx timestamps)
* Net deposits vs withdrawals
* Token performance over time
* Monthly heatmap: Volume + Transactions
* Wallet age
* Largest wins / losses
* Profitability score

---

# **🛡 4. Sybil Risk Analysis**

Analyze signals:

* Rapid repetitive small-value transfers
* Very short interaction windows with many contracts
* Highly repetitive swap patterns
* High faucet usage
* Multiple wallets interacting with the same contracts in sync
* Transaction intervals entropy score
* Bot-likelihood score
* Bridging patterns
  Output:
  **Sybil Score: 0–100** (0 = clean, 100 = extremely likely bot)

---

# **⭐ 5. Wallet Score (0–100)**

Based on:

* Activity
* Volume
* Risk
* Diversity of protocols
* Minting vs dumping
* Long-term holding
* NFT and token interactions
* Profitability

Provide:

* Overall score
* Sub-scores: Activity / Diversity / Risk / Profitability / Authenticity

---

# **📦 6. Feature Modules**

Include these modules:

### **🪪 Identity Module**

* ENS/name lookup
* Farcaster handle if linked
* Social graph connections (if available)

### **💰 Token Breakdown**

* Portfolio allocation
* Token age
* Unrealized P&L
* Rug risk alert
* Stale tokens (no transfers for 45+ days)
* Smart money token overlap

### **🔍 Contract Interaction Insights**

* Top protocols used
* New contract interactions
* Recurring smart contracts
* High-risk contract warnings

### **🎯 User Labels**

Automatically detect and display labels like:

* Farmer
* NFT Trader
* DeFi Trader
* Airdrop Hunter
* Whale
* Newbie
* Dormant
* Smart Money-lite
* Burner Account
* Bridge Hopper

---

# **📑 7. Final Output / Dashboard**

The result page should show:

### **Summary Card**

* Address (short format)
* Wallet Score
* Sybil Score
* Total Volume
* Profit/Loss
* Monthly chart
* Activity streak

### **Detail Sections**

* Transaction Analytics
* Swap History
* Token Breakdown
* Contract Interactions
* Risk Analysis
* Identity & Labels

### **Export Options**

* PDF report
* Share result as a Farcaster cast card
* JSON export
* Screenshot of scorecard

---

# **🎨 8. UI / UX Requirements**

* Built in Tailwind
* Frame UI should be compact (step-by-step)
* Web UI should be full dashboard
* Color theme: **Base × Farcaster (soft blue, white, minimal)**
* Mobile optimized
* Add skeleton loading states

---

# **🧠 9. Additional Features (Optional)**

* “Compare two wallets” mode
* Daily score tracker
* “Clean your wallet” suggestions
* Airdrop likelihood prediction
* Badge system for achievements
* AI-generated wallet description (like “You are a DeFi power-user with low risk, high diversity”)

---

If you want, I can now generate:

✅ full HTML/CSS/JS code
✅ full Frame + API endpoints
✅ ready-to-deploy Vercel template
✅ the signature Frame card
✅ the score-engine backend
✅ the final UI design preview

watchlist-priority-sorter.title: Watchlist Priority Sorter
watchlist-priority-sorter.prompt:
Title: Watchlist Priority Sorter

Description:
Create a simple app where users can add tokens to a watchlist and assign each token a priority level. The app should work fully offline and must not use the internet or external APIs. All data is entered manually by the user.

Functionality:
 • Display two input fields:
 1. “Token Name”
 2. “Priority Level” (example: High, Medium, Low, or a number like 1–5)
 • Add a button labeled “Add to Watchlist” that adds the token and its assigned priority to a visible list.
 • The list should automatically sort items by priority (highest priority first).
 • If priorities are text-based (High/Medium/Low), sort them in this order.
 • If numeric, sort in ascending order (1 = highest priority).
 • Show the sorted list in a section titled “Your Sorted Watchlist”.
 • Each entry should have a “Delete” button to remove that token individually.
 • Add a “Clear All” button that removes the entire watchlist.
 • If either field is empty, show an error message:
“Please enter both the token name and priority.”

UI Requirements:
 • Use only simple interface elements: text fields, buttons, labels, and a sortable list.
 • Keep the layout clean and easy to use.
 • All interactions must happen locally and update instantly.

website.title: 2048 Mini App
website.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

wlguide.title: Mini App Factory App
wlguide.prompt:
2048 is played on a plain 4×4 grid, with square numbered tiles that can be moved using the four onscreen arrow buttons. The arrow buttons are placed bellow the grid in the formation they usually appear on on a keyboard. The game begins with two tiles already in the grid, having a value of either 2 or 4, and another such tile appears in a random empty space after each turn. Tiles with a value of 2 appear 90% of the time, and tiles with a value of 4 appear 10% of the time. Tiles slide as far as possible in the pressed arrow's direction until they are stopped by either another tile or the edge of the grid. If two tiles of the same number collide while moving, they will merge into a tile with the total value of the two tiles that collided. The resulting tile cannot merge with another tile again in the same move.

If a move causes three consecutive tiles of the same value to slide together, only the two tiles farthest along the direction of motion will combine. If all four spaces in a row or column are filled with tiles of the same value, a move parallel to that row/column will combine the first two and last two. A scoreboard on the upper-right keeps track of the user's score. The user's score is equal to the sum of all tiles currently on the board.

The game is won when a tile with a value of 2048 appears on the board. Players can continue beyond that to reach higher scores. When the player has no legal moves (there are no empty spaces and no adjacent tiles with the same value), the game ends.

The user should be able to share their score once the game is over.

Place the 2048 game on the home page.

zoo.title: ZooMate \u2013 Zoo Management & Visitor App
zoo.prompt:
Zoo Management & Visitor App “ZooMate”**

1. Project Overview

ZooMate is a mobile and web application designed for zoos to improve visitor experience, animal care management, and staff coordination. The app has two main modes:

Visitor Mode – helps visitors navigate the zoo, explore animals, events, and buy tickets.

Staff Mode – helps zookeepers, veterinarians, and management with animal care, feeding schedules, health monitoring, and task tracking.

2. Objectives

Enhance visitor experience with interactive zoo maps, animal info, and event notifications.

Digitize staff workflows for animal care, maintenance, and reporting.

Provide real-time animal health monitoring and task management.

Integrate ticketing, payments, and visitor analytics.

Support staff communication and visitor feedback.

3. Core Features
3.1 Visitor Mode

Zoo Map & Navigation

Interactive map of zoo zones

Highlight exhibits, restaurants, bathrooms, gift shops

AR animal guides (optional)

Animal Encyclopedia

Photos, species info, diet, conservation status

Audio guides

Event Calendar & Notifications

Feeding shows

Keeper talks

Special events

Tickets & Booking

Online ticket purchase

QR code for entrance

Membership & season pass management

Visitor Feedback & Rating

Rate exhibits

Submit suggestions

3.2 Staff Mode

Animal Management

Animal profiles: species, age, health history, feeding schedule

Health monitoring (weight, vitals, medications)

AI alerts for abnormal behavior or health risks

Feeding & Task Scheduler

Feeding times per animal

Cleaning and maintenance tasks

Task assignment to staff members

Notifications and reminders

Medical Records

Vet reports

Vaccinations

Treatments and medications

History logs

Inventory & Supplies

Food stock tracking

Cleaning supplies

Alerts when inventory is low

Staff Communication

Group and private chat

Task discussion

Emergency alerts

3.3 Shared Features (Visitor + Staff)

News & Updates feed

Emergency notifications

Multi-language support

Push notifications

4. Platform Requirements

Mobile: iOS 13+, Android 9+

Web: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari

Recommended Tech Stack:

Frontend: Flutter (mobile), React (web)

Backend: Node.js / Django

Database: PostgreSQL

Cloud Hosting: AWS / Google Cloud

Optional AI: Health anomaly detection

5. UI/UX Requirements

Visitor Mode:

Colorful, fun, and easy-to-use interface

Map with touch navigation

Quick-access buttons: Map, Animals, Events, Tickets

Staff Mode:

Dashboard with tasks and alerts

Animal cards with vital stats

Notifications for scheduled tasks

Offline mode for staff in areas with poor signal

6. Database Architecture (ERD Description)

Main Entities:

Users (Visitor / Staff)

Animals

Exhibits

Events

Tickets / Bookings

Tasks & Schedules

Inventory / Supplies

Health Records

Feedback

Table Examples:

Users: id, name, email, role (visitor/staff), password_hash, created_at

Animals: id, species, name, age, exhibit_id, health_status, feeding_schedule, medical_history

Exhibits: id, name, zone, description

Events: id, title, description, date_time, location

Tickets: id, visitor_id, type, qr_code, date_of_visit

Tasks: id, staff_id, description, assigned_animal_id, due_date, status

Inventory: id, item_name, quantity, animal_id (optional), threshold_alert

Health Records: id, animal_id, vet_report, treatment, medications, date

7. Agile User Stories
Visitor Stories

As a visitor, I want to view the zoo map so that I can find animal exhibits easily.

As a visitor, I want to see animal info with photos and descriptions so that I can learn about the animals.

As a visitor, I want to buy tickets in the app to skip the line.

As a visitor, I want to get notifications for feeding shows or events.

Staff Stories

As a zookeeper, I want to see daily feeding schedules so that I can feed animals on time.

As a vet, I want to log medical treatments so that the animal’s health record is up-to-date.

As a staff member, I want to receive alerts for low inventory of food or supplies.

As a staff member, I want to assign cleaning tasks and track completion.

8. Security Requirements

Role-based access control (Visitor / Staff / Admin)

Encrypted data storage (AES-256)

HTTPS for all communication

GDPR/CCPA compliance for visitor data

9. Performance Requirements

App load ≤ 2 seconds

QR ticket scanning ≤ 500 ms

Staff notifications ≤ 1 second

Map navigation smooth, even offline

10. Monetization Model

Free for visitors

Paid premium features:

Memberships

AR guides

Exclusive events

Staff module included with zoo subscription

11. KPIs

Daily active visitors using app

Ticket sales via app

Task completion rate for staff

Animal health alerts resolved

Visitor satisfaction ratings

Database: PostgreSQL

Cloud Hosting: AWS / Google Cloud

Optional AI: Health anomaly detection

5. UI/UX Requirements

Visitor Mode:

Colorful, fun, and easy-to-use interface

Map with touch navigation

Quick-access buttons: Map, Animals, Events, Tickets

Staff Mode:

Dashboard with tasks and alerts

Animal cards with vital stats

Notifications for scheduled tasks

Offline mode for staff in areas with poor signal

6. Database Architecture (ERD Description)

Main Entities:

Users (Visitor / Staff)

Animals

Exhibits

Events

Tickets / Bookings

Tasks & Schedules

Inventory / Supplies

Health Records

Feedback

Table Examples:

Users: id, name, email, role (visitor/staff), password_hash, created_at

Animals: id, species, name, age, exhibit_id, health_status, feeding_schedule, medical_history

Exhibits: id, name, zone, description

Events: id, title, description, date_time, location

Tickets: id, visitor_id, type, qr_code, date_of_visit

Tasks: id, staff_id, description, assigned_animal_id, due_date, status

Inventory: id, item_name, quantity, animal_id (optional), threshold_alert

Health Records: id, animal_id, vet_report, treatment, medications, date

7. Agile User Stories
Visitor Stories

As a visitor, I want to view the zoo map so that I can find animal exhibits easily.

As a visitor, I want to see animal info with photos and descriptions so that I can learn about the animals.

As a visitor, I want to buy tickets in the app to skip the line.

As a visitor, I want to get notifications for feeding shows or events.

Staff Stories

As a zookeeper, I want to see daily feeding schedules so that I can feed animals on time.

As a vet, I want to log medical treatments so that the animal’s health record is up-to-date.

As a staff member, I want to receive alerts for low inventory of food or supplies.

As a staff member, I want to assign cleaning tasks and track completion.

8. Security Requirements

Role-based access control (Visitor / Staff / Admin)

Encrypted data storage (AES-256)

HTTPS for all communication

GDPR/CCPA compliance for visitor data

9. Performance Requirements

App load ≤ 2 seconds

QR ticket scanning ≤ 500 ms

Staff notifications ≤ 1 second

Map navigation smooth, even offline

10. Monetization Model

Free for visitors

Paid premium features:

Memberships

AR guides

Exclusive events

Staff module included with zoo subscription

11. KPIs

Daily active visitors using app

Ticket sales via app

Task completion rate for staff

Animal health alerts resolved

Visitor satisfaction ratings
